SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10784788/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-04713-1

sl-test-v2-ff95e5ee6716.label: Use count model with depth offset
sl-test-v2-ff95e5ee6716.text: PITFALL: Using log-normalized expression (log1p CP10K) or ignoring library size gives a quantity that is not a log rate ratio and is biased for low counts; if total_umi differs by genotype or donor, unadjusted counts confound depth with genotype. CHECK: compare total_umi distributions by g and donor; check overdispersion (variance vs mean of pseudobulk or cell counts, Pearson chi2/df of a Poisson fit). IF FOUND: model raw counts with a log link and offset(log total_umi) (summed per donor for pseudobulk); use negative binomial if chi2/df >> 1; the g coefficient is then the per-allele log rate ratio. SOURCE: https://github.com/mancusolab/jaxQTL ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10172138/

sl-test-v2-315a5b393c61.label: resolution / anchor offset
sl-test-v2-315a5b393c61.text: PITFALL: Loop signal depends on resolution (fold-change compression). A loop anchor split across 20 kb bins or offset by one bin shifts the measured enrichment. CHECK: look at the 3x3 neighbourhood around (8,17) at 20 kb to see whether the peak is centred there. Cross-check against the corresponding 40 kb pixel (bins 4 and 8 in bins_40kb.tsv.gz; verify the coordinates match), checking that the case-control direction agrees. IF FOUND: still report the 20 kb (8,17) pixel as asked, but note a peak offset or resolution disagreement in the QC. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10645293/

sl-test-v2-8c4f649394df.label: Cell QC: HBB, depth, doublets
sl-test-v2-8c4f649394df.text: PITFALL: Low-quality barcodes, RBC-contaminated droplets (high HBB) and doublets/ambient-like barcodes in cells.csv distort per-cell CXCL10 and the activation gating. CHECK: plot the distribution of total_umi and the HBB fraction per cell; flag cells whose total_umi is close to the empty-drop range (empty drops have total_umi ~100-200), cells with unusually high total_umi (doublets), and cells with a high HBB fraction or a low LST1 (monocyte marker) fraction. IF FOUND: remove or flag those cells using pre-specified MAD-based thresholds, applied blind to genotype, and report how many cells per donor were removed and whether beta changes. SOURCE: https://www.10xgenomics.com/analysis-guides/common-considerations-for-quality-control-filters-for-single-cell-rna-seq-data ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11374959/

sl-test-v2-f21d5973cc40.label: bad bins and short diagonals
sl-test-v2-f21d5973cc40.text: PITFALL: Low-quality bins (low mappability, outlying coverage) and short-range diagonals (dist 0-1, which carry self-ligation and undigested artefacts) distort balancing and expected. CHECK: flag bins with low mappability or log-coverage more than ~5 MAD below the median. Note that the data have no main diagonal (dist_bin starts at 1). IF FOUND: mask bad bins (set them to NaN) and drop them from the expected averages. Ignore diagonals 0-1 (cooltools default ignore_diags=2) when balancing. Check whether bin 8 or 17 is itself flagged. SOURCE: https://cooltools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/cli.html ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GPTomics/bioSkills/main/hi-c-analysis/matrix-operations/SKILL.md

sl-test-v2-dfffd3a4f957.label: Donor covariates and min cells
sl-test-v2-dfffd3a4f957.text: PITFALL: Donor covariates (sex, age, bmi in donors.csv) may correlate with genotype in a small sample (24 donors) and confound beta; with so few donors, adding many covariates or using donors with very few activated cells also makes estimates unstable. CHECK: cross-tabulate g against sex and age/bmi; count activated cells per donor (one reference workflow drops donors with <5 cells). IF FOUND: adjust for the imbalanced covariates (sex, age) in the donor-level model and report beta with and without them; drop or down-weight donors with very few activated cells and say that you did; check g is coded as an additive 0/1/2 allele count. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8223300/

sl-test-v2-fc52c614c844.label: gb03 data layout
sl-test-v2-fc52c614c844.text: DATA FACT: contacts_20kb.tsv.gz has columns rep, condition, bin_i, bin_j, dist_bin, count. It holds 4 replicates (ctrl_r1, ctrl_r2 = control; case_r1, case_r2 = case) with 276 pixels each: the upper triangle of 24 bins (chr8 from 400 kb), dist_bin 1-23, no main diagonal. Bin annotations include gc_content, mappability and re_sites.

sl-test-v2-f8594abd7fa1.label: IPW for source-population OR
sl-test-v2-f8594abd7fa1.text: PITFALL: The cohort is an outcome- and stratum-dependent sample (sampling_design.tsv gives sample_fraction per clinic_stratum x recruitment_stream x ancestry_group x age_band x case), so an unweighted logistic regression estimates a sample-conditional OR, not the requested source-population OR; because fractions differ by stratum and the stratum variables may correlate with SV dosage (ancestry), the bias does not just fall into the intercept. CHECK: merge sample_fraction onto every cohort row by all five keys (age_band, not continuous age), confirm every row matches exactly one fraction, and compare weighted vs unweighted log OR. IF FOUND: fit an inverse-probability-weighted (weight = 1/sample_fraction) logistic model with design-based sandwich SEs (e.g. survey::svyglm with strata), and report the weighted estimate. SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/survey/html/svyglm.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2822363/

sl-test-v2-00fe5b555179.label: Design strata are not covariates
sl-test-v2-00fe5b555179.text: PITFALL: recruitment_stream and age_band are sampling-design strata, not baseline clinical covariates; putting recruitment_stream (or the design cells) into the outcome model as covariates instead of using them for weights changes the estimand and can over-adjust, and using age_band instead of continuous age for adjustment loses information (file_notes says use continuous age for clinical adjustment). CHECK: read file_notes.tsv and list which variables are weighting strata vs covariates before modelling. IF FOUND: use clinic_stratum/recruitment_stream/ancestry_group/age_band/case only to build weights; adjust the outcome model for age (continuous), sex, pc1-pc3 (and possibly ancestry_group as a confounder of SV frequency), not recruitment_stream. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5783376/

sl-test-v2-2c811c890a03.label: Calibration panel to full cohort
sl-test-v2-2c811c890a03.text: PITFALL: breakpoint_panel.tsv is a long-read calibration subset, not an association cohort; running the clinical association only on panel samples (small, non-random) or treating panel calls as available for everyone gives a biased and imprecise OR. Full-cohort SV dosage must come from a calibration model mapping tag_markers to the long-read segment-B copy index, trained on reliable panel samples and applied to all cohort samples (regression calibration: use E[X|markers], not hard-thresholded calls). CHECK: count overlap of panel sample_ids with cohort/tag_markers; cross-validate the marker->copy prediction (R^2 / concordance) within the panel. IF FOUND: build the predictor with cross-validation in the reliable panel, use predicted dosage (expected copies) for all cohort samples, and if the predicted dosage is shrunk or scaled vs truth, rescale so the OR is per true calibrated copy. SOURCE: http://hdl.handle.net/1773/22645 ; https://github.com/SauersML/ferromic/tree/main/imputation

sl-test-v2-a9fad88f7147.label: Long-read breakpoint QC
sl-test-v2-a9fad88f7147.text: PITFALL: Long-read breakpoint calls in repeat-rich SV regions are unreliable for some samples (low molecule_count, low mean_mapq, high alignment_entropy, unbalanced pair_balance, high local_complexity), and copy_index_segment_B is a continuous index, not an integer; training the calibration or counting carriers on unfiltered or unrounded values inflates noise and miscounts n_calibrated_carriers. CHECK: plot distributions of each QC field and of copy_index_segment_B (look for clusters near 0/1/2 and off-cluster outliers); look at whether outliers concentrate in high local_complexity or low mapq samples. IF FOUND: define a pre-stated reliability filter from QC fields (thresholds justified by the distributions), round/cluster copy index to integer copies among reliable samples only, and count carriers (>=1 copy) only among reliable samples. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9163579/ ; https://doi.org/10.1101/2020.11.01.363887

sl-test-v2-34833f3c215c.label: Separate nested B from outer inversion
sl-test-v2-34833f3c215c.text: PITFALL: The nested segment-B dosage lies inside a broader outer-orientation polymorphism (bp_alt_fraction measures outer orientation), so B and outer dosage are in LD; a marginal regression on B (or tagging B with markers that actually tag the outer inversion) attributes the outer effect to B. CHECK: in reliable panel samples, cross-tabulate integer B copies vs outer-orientation dosage (from bp_alt_fraction ~0/0.5/1) and find which marker blocks predict B separately from outer; check correlation of predicted B and predicted outer dosage in the cohort. IF FOUND: calibrate both B and outer dosage, and fit the clinical model with both terms so the B coefficient is separated from the outer effect; avoid putting expression or other descendants of B into the model, since the target is a total effect. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6608898/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5131787/

sl-test-v2-ad42a002f644.label: Recurrence and ancestry in SV tagging
sl-test-v2-ad42a002f644.text: PITFALL: Inversions and copy-number SVs mediated by repeats are often recurrent or sit on several haplotype backgrounds, so SNP tagging is weaker than for SNPs and can differ by ancestry; a tag model trained mostly on one ancestry can mis-impute others and confound the OR with ancestry. CHECK: report calibration accuracy by ancestry_group within the reliable panel and check whether B frequency differs by ancestry/PCs. IF FOUND: include ancestry (pcs and/or ancestry_group) in the calibration model or fit ancestry-aware predictors, and adjust the clinical model for PCs; flag ancestry groups with poor tagging. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2690135/ ; https://www.cell.com/cell/fulltext/S0092-8674(22)00464-0

sl-test-v2-79d208810213.label: Expression mapping artifacts in duplicated genes
sl-test-v2-79d208810213.text: PITFALL: Genes inside duplicated/copy-variable segments have multimapping reads, so short-read expression can track copy number through mapping artifacts rather than biology, and a gene can appear expression-supported only because of mismapping. CHECK: for each gene, regress log_expr on calibrated B dosage with and without multimapper_fraction/unique_fraction, tissue_source, expr_batch, assay_depth_millions, gc_metric; see whether the B effect is stable and whether multimapper_fraction itself rises with B copy. IF FOUND: pick the supported gene as the one whose B effect survives adjustment for technical covariates (batch, tissue, depth, GC, uniqueness) and also adjusts for the outer dosage; report the log fold-change per B copy from that adjusted model. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6305209/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7330433/

sl-test-v2-48774fb79881.label: Secondary-trait bias for expression
sl-test-v2-48774fb79881.text: PITFALL: The expression panel is a subset of a case-enriched sample; if case status affects expression, an unweighted expression~dosage regression in a case-control sample is a biased secondary-trait analysis. CHECK: test whether log_expr differs by case and whether case proportion in the expression panel differs from the source population. IF FOUND: include case status as a covariate or weight expression samples by inverse sampling fraction, and report how much the estimate changes. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4006579/

sl-test-v2-1caa25b22e75.label: Units and scale for reported effects
sl-test-v2-1caa25b22e75.text: PITFALL: Expression uses log_expr, which is already natural-log; per-copy fold-change must come from the regression slope on the calibrated copy dosage (natural log units), not log2 values or slopes on hard 0/1 carrier status. Likewise subhap_log_or must be per additional copy (additive dosage) on the natural-log scale. CHECK: confirm the dosage scale (0,1,2 copies) and log base before reporting. IF FOUND: rescale slopes to per-copy, natural-log units. SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/survey/html/svyglm.html

sl-test-v2-09c39583b071.label: SNP vs founder haplotype model
sl-test-v2-09c39583b071.text: PITFALL: Single-SNP association with biallelic markers cannot name a founder, because each SNP only splits the 8 founders into two groups and several founders share each allele, so a high SNP allele points to a set of founders, not one. CHECK: For the peak SNP, count how many founders in founders.tsv carry each allele; if more than one founder carries the high allele, the SNP result alone does not identify high_founder. IF FOUND: Rebuild founder haplotype probabilities with a multipoint HMM (R/qtl2 calc_genoprob, cross type riself8, or an equivalent HMM over ordered markers), run an 8-founder additive scan (7 df), and take high_founder from the founder coefficients at the peak, not from one SNP. SOURCE: https://pages.stat.wisc.edu/~yandell/doc/2019/genetics.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13364981/

sl-test-v2-cbd4bcfbc6fa.label: Marker order and ID alignment
sl-test-v2-cbd4bcfbc6fa.text: PITFALL: In the gb10 data the rows of markers.tsv and founders.tsv and the columns of ril_genotypes.npz are not in map order and mix chr 1 and chr 2 (they start m2_065, m2_103, m2_107, m1_054...). A HMM or interval scan run in file order will produce nonsense genotype probabilities and a wrong peak. CHECK: Sort markers by chr and then pos_cM; check that the npz marker_id order matches markers.tsv and founders.tsv by ID, not by row index, and that sample_id order in the npz matches phenotypes.tsv. IF FOUND: Join everything by marker_id and sample_id, and order markers by pos_cM within each chromosome before computing genotype probabilities or LOD curves. SOURCE: https://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/developer_guide.html

sl-test-v2-1ea5ff5731ce.label: Residual risk Bayes formula, ancestry-specific DR
sl-test-v2-1ea5ff5731ce.text: PITFALL: Residual carrier risk after a negative screen is often computed as CF*(1-DR) (or CF - detected-carrier frequency), which ignores the Bayesian denominator; it also often reuses one pooled or EUR detection rate for every ancestry. CHECK: Compute DR separately for AFR, as the fraction of AFR carriers whose variants the screen would detect, using ancestry-specific class frequencies and assay sensitivity; then compute RR = CF*(1-DR)/(1-CF*DR). IF FOUND: Use the full Bayes formula with ancestry-specific CF and DR, and report on the probability scale. SOURCE: https://www.goldenhelix.com/blog/how-reproductive-risk-and-residual-risk-are-cc-calculated-for-couple-carrier-screening-workflows/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8453722/

sl-test-v2-84532024507b.label: Genotype coding consistency
sl-test-v2-84532024507b.text: PITFALL: The genotype codings differ between files and can easily be misread: RIL genotypes in ril_genotypes.npz are int8 values {1,0,-1} while founder genotypes are 0/1. If -1 means missing but is treated as an allele, or if the allele coding is flipped relative to the founders, the founder assignment comes out wrong (for example, the lowest founder gets reported as the highest). CHECK: Tabulate the values in G; check that RIL allele calls match founder alleles (each RIL should match some founder at nearly every marker over long runs); count missing values per marker and per RIL. IF FOUND: Recode -1 as missing (or as a het if the documentation says so; qtl2 treats hets in RILs as missing), make sure the RIL and founder codes refer to the same allele, and drop markers that are monomorphic across founders. SOURCE: https://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/developer_guide.html ; https://groups.google.com/g/rqtl2-disc/c/Ue1aSqcrYV4

sl-test-v2-b4ac27c8cf00.label: Unstable founder coefficients
sl-test-v2-b4ac27c8cf00.text: PITFALL: Founder effect estimates at the QTL can be unstable or extreme when a founder haplotype is rare at that locus (with only 120 RILs, each founder is expected in about 15 lines and could be far fewer), so a sparsely represented founder can come out with the largest fixed-effect coefficient purely through noise. CHECK: At the peak, sum the founder haplotype probabilities across RILs (the expected count per founder) and look at the standard errors of the scan1coef estimates; compare the fixed-effect coefficients with BLUPs (scan1blup). IF FOUND: Report high_founder only if it stays the top founder under the BLUP/shrunken estimates and its effect is clearly separated from the runner-up; note any tie or founders sharing the same SNP haplotype in the region in the reasoning. SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/qtl2/html/scan1blup.html ; https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/qtl2/refman/qtl2.html

sl-test-v2-8291587c150e.label: Couple risk = RR x partner mixture x 1/4
sl-test-v2-8291587c150e.text: PITFALL: Couple reproductive risk is often computed as RR_index*CF_partner*1/4 with an aggregate partner CF, or by plugging in an averaged risk where a mixture is needed. CHECK: Compute P(partner carrier) as the average over every partner_roster row (each row equally weighted), with the carrier probability set by that partner's stratum (ancestry, family_history_tier, testing status/result). IF FOUND: Couple risk = RR_index(AFR, negative) * mean_over_partner_rows(P(carrier)) * 1/4. Because the index and partner are independent, the mixture is linear, but compute partner strata explicitly rather than reusing the screening-roster CF. SOURCE: https://www.goldenhelix.com/blog/how-reproductive-risk-and-residual-risk-are-cc-calculated-for-couple-carrier-screening-workflows/

sl-test-v2-3085c71dd03a.label: Batch covariate
sl-test-v2-3085c71dd03a.text: PITFALL: The phenotype file has a batch column. If batch is left out, batch differences add residual noise or, if batch is unbalanced across founder haplotypes, can shift the founder effects and the peak. CHECK: Compare y means and variances by batch, and cross-tabulate batch against founder dosage at the peak. IF FOUND: Include batch as an additive covariate in both the null and the QTL models (addcovar in scan1, scan1coef and the permutations), and consider an interactive covariate if effects differ by batch. Also check y for outliers or skew; use a rank-based inverse normal transform if needed, and check that the peak does not move. SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/qtl/html/scanone.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4866519/

sl-test-v2-88dd84cb2f2e.label: Significance and interval for position
sl-test-v2-88dd84cb2f2e.text: PITFALL: Reporting only the argmax position without assessing significance or precision; with 120 RILs and a 7-df founder model the LOD peak may be broad or there may be multiple peaks, and a marker-only scan restricts the position to marker locations. CHECK: Run a permutation test (shuffle phenotypes with batch kept attached, about 1000 permutations, genome-wide max LOD) to get the threshold; compute a 1.5-LOD support interval or 95% Bayes credible interval on chr 1; scan a pseudomarker grid (e.g. 1 cM) between markers. IF FOUND: If chr 1 has two separated peaks, fit a two-QTL model or a conditional scan (with the top QTL as a covariate) before picking a position; give the position as the peak of the full-founder (or LMM) LOD and quote the interval in the reasoning. SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/qtl2/html/lod_int.html ; https://kbroman.org/teaching_misc/SISG/2003/intro_ho.pdf

sl-test-v2-ab08fe6c458a.label: Paralog mismapping false SNV carriers
sl-test-v2-ab08fe6c458a.text: PITFALL: Paralog/pseudogene or segmental-duplication reads mismap onto the gene and create false heterozygous SNV calls; MAPQ alone can mislead because a variant can make paralog reads look unique. CHECK: In assay_observations, compare the distributions of paralog_kmer_fraction, segmental_dup_score and mapq_median between alt-supporting calls and reference calls, per target and per batch; look for clusters of low-VAF (about 0.1-0.3) calls with high paralog fraction or low MAPQ. IF FOUND: Treat those calls as artifacts/no-calls rather than carriers (use thresholds validated on calibration_controls), and lower the assay's effective sensitivity/specificity for that target accordingly. SOURCE: https://www.gimjournal.org/article/S1098-3600(21)01425-8/fulltext

sl-test-v2-5abb0e9d7251.label: Genotyping errors and HMM error_prob
sl-test-v2-5abb0e9d7251.text: PITFALL: Genotyping errors (and any residual heterozygosity) in RILs or founders create false double recombinants, which distort haplotype probabilities and can pull the founder assignment and peak position; a founder genotype error is particularly damaging because every RIL is decoded against it. CHECK: Run the HMM with a nonzero error_prob (e.g. 0.002 to 0.01), count crossovers per RIL (look for outlier RILs with very many), look for markers whose calls conflict with flanking markers, and check per-marker missing rates and that markers are polymorphic among founders. IF FOUND: Drop or mask bad markers and samples, keep a nonzero error_prob, and confirm the peak and the top founder are robust to error_prob between 0.001 and 0.01. SOURCE: https://kbroman.org/pdfs/broman2019_g3.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8527519/

sl-test-v2-762ac0d61e97.label: CNV calling needs batch-matched normalization
sl-test-v2-762ac0d61e97.text: PITFALL: Exon-deletion (copy_number target, log2_ratio) calls made with one global threshold across batches/lots misclassify carriers, because depth ratios shift by batch and need a matched reference. CHECK: Plot log2_ratio for DRX1_T02 by batch; a heterozygous deletion should sit near log2(1/2) = -1 relative to a batch-matched normal median. Use calibration_controls (known class_02 vs normal per source_batch) to see where the clusters fall for each lot. IF FOUND: Re-centre log2 ratios per batch against batch-matched normal controls, and call deletions with batch-specific cut-offs or a mixture model; estimate deletion-call sensitivity per batch from controls. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4839673/ ; https://www.fertstert.org/article/S0015-0282(17)31323-7/fulltext

sl-test-v2-217fe5a48bd4.label: Kinship / LOCO and second QTL
sl-test-v2-217fe5a48bd4.text: PITFALL: Relatedness and population structure among MAGIC RILs (from the funnel crossing design and uneven founder contributions) can inflate LOD and create ghost peaks; a polygenic background on other chromosomes inflates residual variance. CHECK: Compare the chr 1 LOD curve and peak from Haley-Knott regression with an LMM using a LOCO kinship matrix (kinship from chr 2 only when scanning chr 1); also check whether the chr 2 signal matters. IF FOUND: If the peak or the top founder shifts, report the LOCO-LMM result; if chr 2 has a strong QTL, include it as a covariate when scanning chr 1. SOURCE: https://kbroman.org/Teaching_UWStatGen2022/qtl_in_mpp.pdf ; https://academic.oup.com/genetics/article/217/3/iyaa041/6067404

sl-test-v2-0fb38f94160e.label: Sign and contrast of founder effects
sl-test-v2-0fb38f94160e.text: PITFALL: Taking the founder with the most extreme coefficient regardless of sign, or reading coefficients under the wrong contrast (scan1coef with zerosum=TRUE gives effects that sum to zero plus an intercept; zerosum=FALSE gives effects relative to a reference founder), can make the analyst report the wrong founder as high-effect. CHECK: At the peak, compute the mean phenotype of RILs whose most likely haplotype (maxmarg, probability >0.5) is each founder, and check that the founder with the highest mean matches the founder with the largest positive coefficient. IF FOUND: Report the founder with the highest positive effect on y, confirmed by both the coefficients and the raw group means. SOURCE: https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2/blob/main/NEWS.md ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8527519/

sl-test-v2-3fcb2bb9c359.label: Correct carrier frequency for assay Se/Sp from controls
sl-test-v2-3fcb2bb9c359.text: PITFALL: Observed screen-positive rates are taken as true carrier frequencies without correcting for imperfect analytical sensitivity/specificity, and sensitivity is assumed equal across variant classes, batches and ancestries. CHECK: Use calibration_controls (ancestry x reference_category x source_batch) to estimate per-class, per-batch sensitivity and false-positive rate under the final calling rules. IF FOUND: Correct prevalence with a Rogan-Gladen-type or Bayesian adjustment (true = (obs + Sp - 1)/(Se + Sp - 1)) and feed the class/batch-specific sensitivity into the detection rate. Propagate uncertainty, which matters most when the class is rare. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10016948/

sl-test-v2-b908afb79c6f.label: Cis/trans phasing and per-person counting
sl-test-v2-b908afb79c6f.text: PITFALL: Two variants in the same person (for example the two class_03 sites T03/T04, or an SNV plus the exon deletion) get double-counted as two carriers, or are wrongly called affected or carrier without checking phase. In cis they form one carrier allele (a complex allele); in trans the person is compound heterozygous/affected and not a carrier. CHECK: Count persons, not variant rows. For each sample with more than one positive target, inspect phase_set (the same PS means the same haplotype block); check how often T03 and T04 co-occur, which would suggest a single complex allele in LD. IF FOUND: Collapse cis co-occurring variants into a single carrier allele; treat confirmed trans pairs as non-carriers for carrier-frequency purposes (or flag them); leave unphased pairs as ambiguous and handle that explicitly. SOURCE: https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/news/2023-03-variant-co-occurrence-counts-by-gene-in-gnomad/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10872287/

sl-test-v2-136c9768c396.label: VAF allele-balance QC and no-call handling
sl-test-v2-136c9768c396.text: PITFALL: Allele-fraction QC is ignored: real germline hets sit near VAF 0.5. Very low VAF suggests artifact, paralog or contamination; VAF near 1 at a het site can mean an SNV in trans with a deletion (apparent homozygosity), not a homozygous carrier. Missing values (blank vaf/log2_ratio) get treated as negative. CHECK: Histogram VAF and alt_reads/depth per target and batch; cross-tabulate high-VAF SNV calls against T02 log2_ratio; count blank/no-call rows per sample and target. IF FOUND: Require allele balance roughly 0.3-0.7 plus minimum depth for het calls; reinterpret SNV+deletion cases; treat no-calls as missing (exclude, impute or reduce DR), never as negative. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12239336/ ; https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(24)00250-2/fulltext

sl-test-v2-3687cef8c2b2.label: Ascertainment: screening-only CF, stratified partner mixture
sl-test-v2-3687cef8c2b2.text: PITFALL: Carrier frequencies are estimated on a sample that mixes ascertainment routes (cohort_roster collection other than 'screening', or family_history_tier above 0), which inflates CF. Likewise the partner roster's family-history and testing-status mix differs from the screening cohort. CHECK: Tabulate cohort_roster by collection x ancestry x family_history_tier and partner_roster by partner_ancestry x family_history_tier x testing_status; confirm that the task estimands ask for 'screening-roster adults' and 'uniformly sampled partner rows'. IF FOUND: Restrict the CF estimate to collection=='screening' (by ancestry). For the partner, compute stratum-specific carrier probabilities (ancestry x family-history tier, using known results where testing is completed and priors or residual risk otherwise) and average over all partner rows uniformly; do not drop non-completed rows. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10391692/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2714692/

sl-test-v2-8a01bfd5575e.label: Ancestry-specific variant spectrum
sl-test-v2-8a01bfd5575e.text: PITFALL: Self-reported or roster ancestry labels are applied as if exact, and a pooled CF/DR is used when variant classes differ sharply by ancestry; the detection rate can differ a lot between AFR and EUR. CHECK: Compare the frequency of each reported_group class (class_01 SNV, class_02 deletion, class_03 sites) by ancestry, in both screening samples and controls. IF FOUND: Compute CF and DR within ancestry; never transfer the EUR DR to AFR. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7521993/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8453722/

sl-test-v2-a0b6b40f7421.label: Allele harmonisation across phases
sl-test-v2-a0b6b40f7421.text: PITFALL: Effect alleles differ between files (e.g. in gb09 the phase2 protein files code rs200000 with effect allele C while phase1, disease and variant_metadata use A), so combining betas without harmonisation flips signs and can reverse or cancel the causal estimate. CHECK: For every SNP compare effect_allele/other_allele across all protein phase files, disease_association, variant_metadata and the LD reference's allele coding; count mismatches. IF FOUND: Multiply beta by -1 (and use 1-EAF) wherever alleles are swapped relative to one reference coding before any meta-analysis, selection or MR; drop SNPs with alleles that cannot be matched. SOURCE: https://mrcieu.github.io/TwoSampleMR/articles/harmonise.html

sl-test-v2-0dc0a1e09f19.label: Signed LD matrix alignment
sl-test-v2-0dc0a1e09f19.text: PITFALL: The signed LD matrix R must match both the SNP order and the effect-allele coding of the summary statistics; using unsigned r^2, the wrong order, or an allele-flipped SNP gives wrong GLS/IVW estimates. CHECK: Confirm locus_correlation_EUR.npz 'snp' order equals the order used for betas, that R is symmetric with unit diagonal and positive semi-definite, and test consistency of z-scores with R (e.g. a SNP's z predicted from neighbours via R: large outliers suggest allele flips). IF FOUND: Reorder R to the analysis order; for a flipped SNP j multiply row and column j of R by -1 (rho*flip%o%flip); drop SNPs with irreconcilable z-vs-LD inconsistencies. SOURCE: https://mendelianrandomization.com/mendelian-randomization-with-highly-correlated-genetic-variants-cis-mr/ ; https://stephenslab.github.io/susieR/articles/rss_mismatch.html

sl-test-v2-5673d69e3e23.label: Ill-conditioned LD in cis-MVMR
sl-test-v2-5673d69e3e23.text: PITFALL: In cis-MVMR with many correlated SNPs, using all variants in GLS/IVW requires inverting an ill-conditioned LD matrix, giving numerically unstable, over-precise estimates; conversely treating correlated SNPs as independent (plain IVW without R) double-counts information and gives wrong SEs and biased weights. CHECK: Compute the condition number/eigenvalues of R restricted to the chosen instruments; re-run the estimate at pruning thresholds r^2<0.1, 0.2, 0.3 (and with PCA of the weighted LD matrix keeping ~99% variance) and see whether the point estimate moves or the SE drops sharply (e.g. by >3x). IF FOUND: Use correlated-instrument GLS, theta=(Bx' S^-1 Bx)^-1 Bx' S^-1 by with S = diag(se_y) R diag(se_y), on an aggressively pruned set (r^2<~0.1-0.3) or PCA components; report the more conservative estimate if SE collapses; do not use plain independent-SNP IVW. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7614127/ ; https://mendelianrandomization.com/mendelian-randomization-with-highly-correlated-genetic-variants-cis-mr/

sl-test-v2-703b3011fce6.label: Winner's curse: screening vs holdout
sl-test-v2-703b3011fce6.text: PITFALL: Winner's curse: selecting instruments by p-value in a protein GWAS and then using the same sample's betas inflates SNP-exposure effects, biasing the causal estimate (usually towards zero for theta since bx is inflated in the denominator) and differently for each protein. CHECK: The data provide a 'screening' phase1 (n=12000) and 'holdout' phase2 (n=8000) protein GWAS; compare phase1 vs phase2 betas (after allele harmonisation) for the selected SNPs: systematic shrinkage in phase2 indicates winner's curse. IF FOUND: Select instruments in phase1 (screening) and estimate SNP-protein effects from phase2 (holdout) only - a three-sample design; do not meta-analyse phase1 into the betas used for estimation for the selected SNPs (or apply a formal winner's-curse correction). SOURCE: https://academic.oup.com/ije/article/48/5/1478/5531250 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2302.10470v1

sl-test-v2-bc8329b5261f.label: Conditional instrument strength in MVMR
sl-test-v2-bc8329b5261f.text: PITFALL: Univariable MR for each of two nearby proteins sharing cis-pQTLs gives total (confounded-by-the-neighbour) effects, not the direct effect conditional on the other protein; and MVMR needs SNPs whose effects on PROTA and PROTB are not collinear, otherwise weak-instrument bias and huge variance arise. CHECK: Fit MVMR (both proteins jointly, by ~ Bx_A*thA + Bx_B*thB with LD-aware GLS); compute Sanderson-Windmeijer/Sanderson-Spiller conditional F-statistics for each protein (MVMR::strength_mvmr, accounting for covariance between the two protein GWAS if overlapping) and the correlation of Bx_A and Bx_B across instruments. IF FOUND: If conditional F < ~10 for either protein, add instruments that separate the proteins (select by association with either protein, union of signals), use weak-instrument-robust inference (Q-minimisation/LIML-type, Andrews robust confidence sets), and report the conditional F alongside estimates. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9479726/ ; https://arxiv.org/html/2408.09868

sl-test-v2-a266822f8c84.label: Per-SD scaling of protein estimates
sl-test-v2-a266822f8c84.text: PITFALL: The target is log-odds per +1 SD of log10 concentration, but protein GWAS betas are per log10(ng/mL) unit (dataset_metadata unit=log10_ng_per_mL), so the raw MR estimate is per log10 unit; reporting it without rescaling, or rescaling with the wrong SD, gives the wrong number. CHECK: Estimate the SD of log10_concentration for each protein from protein_measurements.tsv (3000 rows with protein_id, batch, control_cv); confirm the GWAS unit. IF FOUND: theta_perSD = theta_perlog10unit * SD_log10 (equivalently divide bx by SD before MR); apply the same convention to both proteins and report the SD used. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5985452/

sl-test-v2-ec1168b60823.label: Batch effects in protein measurement SD
sl-test-v2-ec1168b60823.text: PITFALL: protein_measurements has a batch column; batch shifts in mean (or scale) inflate the pooled SD of log10 concentration, and a raw pooled SD would mis-scale the per-SD estimate. CHECK: Compare per-batch mean and SD of log10_concentration for each protein (and per-batch control_cv); test for batch differences (ANOVA) and outliers/out-of-range or duplicated values. IF FOUND: Compute SD after removing batch effects (within-batch centring or pooled within-batch SD), after excluding QC failures/outliers; state the choice and show sensitivity of theta to pooled vs within-batch SD. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8447595/

sl-test-v2-5c63da735049.label: Technical CV and per-SD definition
sl-test-v2-5c63da735049.text: PITFALL: The observed SD of log10 concentration includes technical assay noise (control_cv column gives the assay coefficient of variation), so the observed SD overstates the biological SD; whether 'per SD' should use observed or noise-corrected SD changes the scale. CHECK: Convert control_cv to a log10-scale technical SD (approx CV/ln(10) for small CV) and compare its variance to the observed variance of log10_concentration within each batch; check if CV differs by batch. IF FOUND: Note that pQTL betas are unaffected by classical measurement error in the protein, but consider SD_bio = sqrt(SD_obs^2 - SD_tech^2) for per-SD scaling if the task intends the true concentration; report both and justify the choice. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7694803/

sl-test-v2-923702a7d4c6.label: CRISPRi locus spreads to neighbor gene
sl-test-v2-923702a7d4c6.text: PITFALL: At a lncRNA locus, dCas9-KRAB CRISPRi silences chromatin over a window that routinely spreads to a neighboring/bidirectional-promoter coding gene, so a pooled-screen growth effect assigned to LINC473 may actually be driven by concomitant KIN1 repression (DNA-locus effect), not the LINC473 transcript. CHECK: In local_expression.tsv, for LINC473-targeting guides inspect expr_rel_KIN1 alongside expr_rel_LINC473; quantify how much KIN1 drops when LINC473 is knocked down, and use guide_map dist_neighbor_tss_bp to see which guides sit near the KIN1 TSS. IF FOUND: Do not read the raw CRISPRi LFC as lncrna-specific; use the transcript-directed CasRx data for lncrna_specific_lfc and estimate neighbor_mediated_lfc by modeling the locus effect conditional on KIN1 repression. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5388423/

sl-test-v2-451d4ae88f54.label: Log-odds scale and heterogeneity
sl-test-v2-451d4ae88f54.text: PITFALL: The disease GWAS is case-control (15000 cases/35000 controls) so betas are log-odds; mixing in OR-scale numbers, or treating it as linear/liability scale, gives the wrong scale; also a single external LD reference may not match the GWAS samples, making GLS over-precise. CHECK: Confirm disease beta ~ log(OR) (beta/se consistent with pval; values symmetric around 0); check residual heterogeneity Cochran Q of the MVMR GLS fit against its chi-square df. IF FOUND: Keep estimates on log-odds scale (do not exponentiate); if Q is large, use multiplicative random-effects SEs and investigate outlying SNPs (pleiotropy or LD mismatch) rather than trusting fixed-effect precision. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7384151/ ; https://stephenslab.github.io/susieR/articles/susierss_diagnostic.html

sl-test-v2-73e0a58c0738.label: Collinear co-repression of two genes
sl-test-v2-73e0a58c0738.text: PITFALL: Across guides, local knockdown of LINC473 and of KIN1 are correlated (shared promoter/chromatin), so a single-variable regression of growth on one gene's knockdown absorbs the other gene's effect and mis-splits the phenotype. CHECK: Compute the correlation between expr_rel_LINC473 and expr_rel_KIN1 across guides and the VIF of a joint model growth ~ (1-expr_rel_LINC473) + (1-expr_rel_KIN1). IF FOUND: Fit a single multiple regression including both repression terms to get partial (direct) effects, rather than two separate regressions; report lncRNA effect as the LINC473 coefficient and neighbor effect as the KIN1 coefficient. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3303138/

sl-test-v2-84270a201c2a.label: Attenuation bias extrapolating to 100% KD
sl-test-v2-84270a201c2a.text: PITFALL: The quantities requested are effects at 100% knockdown, but the data only contain partial knockdowns measured with noise; regressing growth on a noisy measured knockdown attenuates the slope (regression dilution), biasing the extrapolated full-knockdown effect toward zero. CHECK: Look at the spread of knockdown_efficiency (CasRx) and expr_rel values; note they are single noisy measurements per guide. IF FOUND: Extrapolate to the full-repression intercept using a dose-response/errors-in-variables (e.g. Deming/total-least-squares) fit rather than naive OLS, so the 100%-knockdown estimate is not under-estimated in magnitude. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regression_dilution

sl-test-v2-cc6b54b71490.label: CasRx collateral and isoform coverage
sl-test-v2-cc6b54b71490.text: PITFALL: CasRx (Cas13d) can show collateral RNA degradation and variable isoform coverage; a guide that only partially overlaps the dominant LINC473 isoform or that triggers collateral activity gives a misleading transcript-specific growth effect. CHECK: In casrx_followup.tsv use major_isoform_overlap and knockdown_efficiency per guide; flag low-overlap or low-efficiency guides and check for anomalously strong growth_lfc at low knockdown. IF FOUND: Weight/filter CasRx guides by isoform overlap and model growth_lfc against knockdown_efficiency, extrapolating to efficiency=1 to define lncrna_specific_lfc. SOURCE: http://sanjanalab.org/reprints/Hart_NBT_2025.pdf

sl-test-v2-34f6bb7de932.label: Off-target guides drive false signal
sl-test-v2-34f6bb7de932.text: PITFALL: In CRISPRi/Cas9 non-coding screens the dominant growth signal often comes from low-specificity or high-GC guides causing off-target fitness effects, not from the intended target. CHECK: In guide_map use guide_gc_frac and look for individual guides whose crispri LFC is an outlier relative to others of the same nominal_target; cross-check against knockdown (local_expression). IF FOUND: Remove or down-weight outlier/high-GC guides before averaging, and require concordance between guide knockdown level and phenotype. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1101/520569

sl-test-v2-e4374c4f690c.label: Knockdown depends on TSS distance
sl-test-v2-e4374c4f690c.text: PITFALL: CRISPRi knockdown strength depends strongly on guide distance from the TSS (max activity ~ -50 to +300 bp); guides far from the LINC473 TSS give weak knockdown and guides near the KIN1 TSS give strong neighbor repression, so treating all guides as equal-effect perturbations is wrong. CHECK: In guide_map relate dist_lnc_tss_bp and dist_neighbor_tss_bp to the measured expr_rel_LINC473 / expr_rel_KIN1. IF FOUND: Model phenotype as a function of measured per-guide knockdown (not guide identity), letting weak-knockdown guides inform the slope rather than diluting a per-guide average. SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25307932/

sl-test-v2-d755d153b2a9.label: Count normalization and low-count QC
sl-test-v2-d755d153b2a9.text: PITFALL: Pooled-screen LFCs are invalid if counts are not properly normalized and low-count guides not filtered; raw day10/day0 ratios are distorted by library-size differences and noisy low-count guides. CHECK: In crispri_counts.tsv check per-replicate total counts, drop guides with very low day0 counts (<~30), confirm 3-replicate concordance, and median-normalize before computing log2(day10/day0). IF FOUND: Apply median/size-factor normalization and matched-control centering, and average replicates, before any effect estimate. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4290824/

sl-test-v2-6e32fb3f5ea1.label: Reference-gene stability for knockdown
sl-test-v2-6e32fb3f5ea1.text: PITFALL: Local expression is reported relative to reference genes (RPLP0, HPRT1); if a reference is itself perturbed by the locus knockdown or by growth selection, all expr_rel ratios are biased. CHECK: In local_expression.tsv verify expr_rel_RPLP0 and expr_rel_HPRT1 stay near 1 across guides (not systematically shifted); compare the two references for agreement. IF FOUND: Use the stable reference(s) only, or geometric-mean normalize across stable references, before deriving LINC473/KIN1 knockdown fractions. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12666847/

sl-test-v2-95e61d97dcd6.reason: Decides the model structure and the uncertainty; a cell-level fit would weight donors by cell number and can shift the point estimate as well as understate the SE.
sl-test-v2-95e61d97dcd6.text: Unit of analysis is the donor, not the cell. Genotype varies only between donors (the library reports about 24 donors; confirm the donor and cell counts yourself), so cells from one donor are pseudoreplicates: a cell-level GLM that treats cells as independent gives badly overconfident standard errors and lets donors with many cells dominate the estimate. Check: count cells per donor and per genotype group inside the activated subset, and compare a naive cell-level fit with a donor-level fit. Recommended estimator: sum CXCL10 counts and total_umi per donor within the activated subset and fit a Poisson or negative-binomial GLM, count ~ g + covariates + offset(log summed total_umi); or fit a cell-level NB mixed model with a donor random intercept. Report the g coefficient on the natural-log scale per allele, with g coded 0/1/2.

sl-test-v2-460e026dc94c.reason: Using the wrong scale or omitting the depth offset gives a number that is not the quantity the task asks for.
sl-test-v2-460e026dc94c.text: The target is a log RATE ratio, so model raw CXCL10 counts with a log link and an offset of log(total_umi) (summed per donor if pseudobulking). Do not regress log-normalised expression (for example log1p of counts per 10k): that slope is not a log rate ratio and is biased when counts are low. Check: compare total_umi distributions by genotype and by donor (if depth differs by genotype, unadjusted counts confound depth with genotype), and check overdispersion (variance against mean, Pearson chi-square/df of a Poisson fit). If chi-square/df is well above 1, use negative binomial rather than Poisson.

sl-test-v2-602f5b59859e.reason: The task's answer depends entirely on which cells count as activated; a gate that touches CXCL10 biases beta by construction.
sl-test-v2-602f5b59859e.text: Do not define the activated subpopulation using CXCL10 itself. Gating or clustering on the outcome gene (or thresholding it) conditions on the outcome, truncates its distribution and biases the genotype effect, usually toward zero but not predictably. Define activation from other interferon-stimulated markers only (the library names IFI6 and ISG15 as available, normalised by total_umi), using a mixture model or a rule fixed in advance and blind to genotype. Then show how the estimate moves across reasonable gates or cutoffs; soft (probabilistic) assignment weights are an alternative to a hard cutoff.

sl-test-v2-e1390f6b1278.reason: A pooled or leaky-gate estimate answers a different question from the one asked and can differ substantially if genotype shifts the activated fraction.
sl-test-v2-e1390f6b1278.text: Separate the within-state effect from a composition effect. Genotype may change the FRACTION of monocytes that are activated as well as CXCL10 per activated cell. An estimate from all monocytes pooled, or from a mis-gated subset, mixes the two, and the task asks for the effect within the activated state. Check: tabulate the activated fraction per donor against g; fit the model in the activated stratum, and also a genotype-by-state interaction model (count ~ g*state + offset, donor random effect). Report beta from the activated stratum (equivalently the g main effect plus the g:state term for activated cells), not the pooled monocyte effect, and describe any composition effect separately.

sl-test-v2-1337d9357d24.reason: Ambient CXCL10 biases the rate ratio directly and also contaminates the ISG markers used for gating; the empty-drop file is easy to overlook.
sl-test-v2-1337d9357d24.text: Check for ambient (cell-free) RNA contamination. Ambient RNA adds counts of highly expressed induced genes (CXCL10, ISG15, IFI6) to every droplet; this inflates expression in low-expressing cells and attenuates genotype log rate ratios toward zero, or creates spurious effects if ambient load differs between samples. The library reports that the data include an empty-droplet file (empty_drops.csv.gz) with counts for low-total_umi barcodes and no donor column, so the ambient profile can only be estimated pooled. Check: compute each gene's ambient fraction (gene/total_umi in empty drops) and compare with cell-level fractions; estimate a contamination fraction rho from a gene that monocytes should not express (for example HBB), SoupX-style: rho is roughly (HBB/total in cells) / (HBB/total in empty drops). Estimate rho after removing RBC-contaminated or low-quality barcodes, since those would inflate it. If contamination is material, subtract the expected ambient counts per cell (rho * total_umi * ambient fraction) before aggregating, or put the ambient expectation in the model, and report beta with and without the correction.

sl-test-v2-e42dcc12ed8f.reason: Contaminated or non-monocyte barcodes enter both the gate and the pseudobulk sums; removal must be genotype-blind and its effect on beta reported.
sl-test-v2-e42dcc12ed8f.text: Do cell-level QC before gating and aggregation. Low-quality barcodes, RBC-contaminated droplets and doublets distort per-cell CXCL10 and the activation gate. Check: look at the distributions of total_umi and of HBB fraction per cell; flag cells with total_umi near the empty-droplet range (the library reports empty drops at roughly 100-200 UMI), cells with unusually high total_umi (possible doublets), and cells with a high HBB fraction or a low fraction of the monocyte marker LST1. Use thresholds fixed in advance (for example MAD-based) and applied blind to genotype. Report how many cells were removed per donor and whether beta changes with and without the filter.

sl-test-v2-9c213f6ab299.reason: With so few donors, a single imbalanced covariate or a few near-empty donors can move the estimate; the adjustment choice needs to be explicit and tested.
sl-test-v2-9c213f6ab299.text: Check donor-level confounding and thin donors. The library reports that donors.csv carries sex, age and bmi. With only about two dozen donors these can be imbalanced across genotype by chance and confound beta, while adding many covariates makes the fit unstable. Check: cross-tabulate g against sex, age and bmi; confirm g is coded as an additive 0/1/2 allele count; count activated cells per donor. Adjust for covariates that are actually imbalanced and report beta with and without them. Donors with very few activated cells give noisy rates: drop or down-weight them under a rule stated in advance (one reference workflow drops donors with fewer than 5 cells), say that you did, and show the sensitivity.

sl-test-v2-fbc0b4b11659.reason: The choice of expected defines the reported quantity; a global or mis-matched expected turns log2(O/E) into a measure of distance decay rather than loop enrichment.
sl-test-v2-fbc0b4b11659.text: The expected value in observed/expected must be distance-matched. Confirm from the data that the pixel (bin 8, bin 17) at 20 kb sits on the diagonal dist_bin = 9, and that the dist_bin column equals bin_j - bin_i. The expected for that pixel is then computed from pixels on that same diagonal only, within the same replicate, after the same normalization as the observed value (the cooltools expected_cis convention). Do not use a whole-matrix mean, pool several diagonals into one average, or borrow an expected from another replicate or another resolution.

sl-test-v2-383ef2cff858.reason: The order of operations (log then average, per replicate) changes the numbers, and the task defines the quantities as means of per-replicate log2(O/E); depth or P(s) differences between conditions would otherwise leak into delta.
sl-test-v2-383ef2cff858.text: Compute everything per replicate first, then average. The four replicates (two control, two case) can differ in sequencing depth and in the shape of the distance-decay curve P(s), so comparing raw counts or pooled matrices confounds depth or P(s) differences with loop differences. Check total counts and log-log P(s) slopes for each replicate. Compute the expected within each replicate (O/E then normalizes itself for depth), take log2(O/E) per replicate, and take the arithmetic mean of the two log2 values per condition; delta is the case mean minus the control mean. The mean of log2(O/E) is not the same as log2 of the mean O/E or log2 of O/E on summed replicates, so do not sum replicates first. Look at the target pixel's count in every replicate and at zeros on its diagonal: a zero gives -inf, so use a pseudocount only if a zero actually occurs, and state it. Report the spread between replicates within each condition; a joint normalization across replicates (multiHiCcompare-style loess) can serve as a sensitivity check.

sl-test-v2-f590c5763406.reason: Whether the reported loop strength is computed on raw or bias-corrected counts can change all three numbers; the bin covariates are supplied in the data and should not be ignored without a check.
sl-test-v2-f590c5763406.text: Raw Hi-C counts carry per-bin visibility biases. The 20 kb bin annotation file gives gc_content, mappability and re_sites (restriction-site density) for each bin, so O/E computed on raw counts may reflect bias at the two anchor bins rather than looping. Per replicate, correlate bin coverage (row sums) with gc_content, mappability and re_sites, and compare the row sums of bins 8 and 17 with the other bins. If bias is present, correct for it before computing O/E: either balance each replicate's matrix (ICE/Sinkhorn, cis-only, excluding the shortest 1-2 diagonals) or fit an explicit Poisson/negative-binomial model with log(gc), log(mappability) and log(re_sites) as covariates. Compute observed and expected on the same corrected scale, and report both the raw and the corrected values.

sl-test-v2-b79621c5639d.reason: Bad bins left in the matrix shift the balancing weights and the diagonal-9 expected, and a flagged anchor bin would change how far the result can be trusted.
sl-test-v2-b79621c5639d.text: Low-quality bins and short-range diagonals distort both balancing and the expected. Flag bins with low mappability or with log-coverage far below the median (about 5 MAD or more), mask them (set to NaN) and leave them out of the per-diagonal expected averages. Check specifically whether bin 8 or bin 17 is itself flagged. The shortest diagonals (distance 0-1 bins) carry self-ligation and undigested-fragment artefacts and should be ignored when balancing (the cooltools default is ignore_diags=2); note that the contact table has no main diagonal (dist_bin starts at 1), so adapt the balancing accordingly.

sl-test-v2-8f1ebe581615.reason: With about 15 pixels per diagonal, the choice between plain mean, median, target-excluded mean and smoothed expected can visibly move the answer, so the choice must be deliberate and its sensitivity reported.
sl-test-v2-8f1ebe581615.text: The 20 kb matrix has only 24 bins, so the diagonal at distance 9 has only about 15 pixels (fewer after masking). The expected there is noisy, is pulled up by the target pixel itself if that pixel is enriched, and can be skewed by other loops, domain structure, edge bins or bad bins. Count the valid pixels on diagonal 9 in each replicate and compare the diagonal mean with the median, with and without the (8,17) pixel; also compare with a smoothed P(s) (log-log regression or loess across diagonals; cooltools smooths P(s) by default). These are still distance-matched expecteds, so they do not conflict with the rule against pooling diagonals into a single mean. Choose and justify one definition of the expected as primary before comparing conditions, state which one was used, and report how much the three quantities move under the alternatives.

sl-test-v2-c4e55de53806.reason: A missed polarisation flips the sign of s at that locus and can change which locus is reported as the more strongly selected one, so it affects both answer fields.
sl-test-v2-c4e55de53806.text: Polarise before fitting: the read counts are for the ALT allele, but s is defined for the DERIVED allele. The library reports that the variant information file (variant_info.tsv) carries an outgroup_allele per locus; the derived allele is the one that does NOT match the outgroup. For each locus, compare outgroup_allele with ref and alt. If the outgroup allele equals alt, then alt is ancestral, so model derived frequency = 1 - alt frequency for that locus before fitting. Compare the two loci on derived-allele s only: a locus whose alt allele falls in frequency can be the one under strong positive selection on the derived allele. Outgroup polarisation by parsimony can itself be wrong, so state it as an assumption in the reasoning.

sl-test-v2-c2bfda7c28ee.reason: It determines how the reported numbers should be interpreted and guards against describing a domain-wide change as a loop change.
sl-test-v2-c2bfda7c28ee.text: A diagonal (global) expected marks every pixel inside a contact domain as enriched, so a high O/E is not by itself evidence of a focal loop. Loop callers (HiCCUPS, cooltools dots) compare the pixel with a local background instead. As QC, compute the enrichment of the (8,17) pixel against a donut neighbourhood (for example a ring of pixels 1-3 bins away, excluding the peak's own row and column) and compare it with the diagonal-expected O/E in each replicate. If the two diverge, keep the diagonal-expected O/E as the primary result, because the task asks for observed/expected, and report the local enrichment as QC. State whether any case-control difference looks like a focal loop change or a broad domain-level change.

sl-test-v2-f2cb241b6898.reason: The choice between the logit slope and exp(slope)-1, or the use of a diploid formula, changes the reported number directly.
sl-test-v2-f2cb241b6898.text: Use the haploid selection model, not a diploid one. For a haploid locus with relative fitness 1+s, p' = p(1+s)/(1+sp), so logit(p_t) = logit(p_0) + t*ln(1+s) exactly. The slope of logit frequency against generation is therefore ln(1+s), not s; the two differ noticeably once s is above about 0.1. Either fit the haploid recursion directly with s as the parameter, or convert a logit slope with s = exp(slope) - 1. Do not use diploid additive or dominance formulas. State in the reasoning which convention the reported s follows.

sl-test-v2-327219bf8ca5.reason: The task supplies 40 kb data that is otherwise unused; it is the available independent check on the 20 kb estimate, and an off-centre peak would change how the result is qualified.
sl-test-v2-327219bf8ca5.text: Measured loop signal depends on resolution, and a loop anchor that is split across two 20 kb bins or sits one bin off shifts the enrichment at the named pixel. Inspect the 3x3 neighbourhood around (8,17) at 20 kb in each replicate to see whether the peak is centred on that pixel. Cross-check with the 40 kb data: find the 40 kb pixel that contains the two 20 kb bins by matching genomic coordinates in the two bin annotation files (the library suggests 40 kb bins 4 and 8, but this is unverified, so confirm by coordinates rather than by index arithmetic), and check that the case-control direction agrees. Expect a smaller fold change at 40 kb. Still report the 20 kb (8,17) pixel as the task asks; record any peak offset or disagreement between resolutions in the QC.

sl-test-v2-6a0ec66ed23e.reason: Fitting on the wrong time column rescales s by a constant factor and would go unnoticed without an explicit check.
sl-test-v2-6a0ec66ed23e.text: Use generation, not calendar year, as the time axis. The library reports that the time series has both a 'generation' column and a 'sample_year' column. s is per generation, so fitting against years (or mixing the two) rescales s by the generations-per-year factor. Confirm that generation increases steadily, see how it relates to sample_year, and check that the Ne schedule is in generation coordinates. Use sample_year only for QC, for example to spot duplicate or out-of-order samples.

sl-test-v2-e6b278e5e032.reason: Whether and how error is handled changes the fitted slope, especially for points near 0 or 1, and the task statement explicitly calls out the ~1% error and the seq_error column.
sl-test-v2-e6b278e5e032.text: Put sequencing error inside the likelihood. Under symmetric error e the observed frequency is p_obs = p(1-e) + (1-p)e, which reads too high near 0 and too low near 1. This flattens the logit trajectory and biases s toward 0, mostly where the allele is rare or near fixation. Look for samples where alt_reads/total_reads is within a few multiples of the error rate (about 0.01) of 0 or 1. Model alt_reads ~ Binomial(total_reads, p(1-e) + (1-p)e) using each row's seq_error value; because that column is already the average of the two directional miscall rates, the symmetric form is the appropriate one. Do not put raw frequencies or 0/1 values into a logit, and do not simply subtract the error and clip.

sl-test-v2-0f27d1e71f11.reason: The estimator and its weighting determine both the point estimate and whether an uncertainty statement is available; the task is graded on analytical reasoning as well as the number.
sl-test-v2-0f27d1e71f11.text: Do not estimate s by ordinary least squares on logit(raw frequency). OLS ignores binomial read-sampling noise (variance about p(1-p)/depth), is unstable or infinite at frequencies of 0 or 1, and weights samples equally even when total_reads differs between them. Inspect total_reads per sample and whether any frequency is at or near 0 or 1. Fit by maximum likelihood with a read-level binomial (plus error) observation model, or at the very least use weighted least squares with weights depth*p(1-p). Report a confidence interval from profile likelihood or bootstrap, not only a point estimate.

sl-test-v2-869ba2174324.reason: Whether drift is modelled, and with which N per interval, changes the s estimate, its uncertainty, and the comparison between loci.
sl-test-v2-869ba2174324.text: Account for the Ne schedule. The library reports that a piecewise Ne schedule by generation is provided (Ne_schedule.tsv with gen_start, gen_end, N), which means drift variance differs between intervals, for example during a bottleneck. Ignoring it treats drift-driven jumps in low-N intervals as selection signal and can confuse drift with selection when comparing the two loci. Read the schedule, see which sampling intervals fall in low-N periods, and see whether large frequency jumps line up with them. Use a model that separates drift and sampling noise from selection under time-varying N: a Wright-Fisher HMM, a Beta-with-spikes model, or a Gaussian/Kalman approximation with drift variance p(1-p)/N per generation in each interval. Compare the result with the deterministic (no-drift) fit as a sensitivity check.

sl-test-v2-7e5d81d32f3a.reason: The selected_locus field depends on a like-for-like comparison of both loci; an informal choice can pick the wrong locus and then report the wrong s.
sl-test-v2-7e5d81d32f3a.text: Do not choose the 'more strongly selected' locus by eye or by the larger raw frequency change. Drift in a small-Ne population, low read depth, or allele polarisation can make the weaker locus look stronger. Estimate derived-allele s at BOTH loci with the same model and give a confidence interval for each. Check whether the intervals overlap and whether each locus differs from neutrality (likelihood-ratio test against s=0, with drift under the Ne schedule accounted for). Base the locus choice on these derived-allele estimates and report both in the reasoning.

sl-test-v2-537ec4e1200e.reason: If the trajectory is not log-linear over the whole series, the interval used to define s changes the reported value, and the team needs to test this rather than assume it.
sl-test-v2-537ec4e1200e.text: Check that a single constant s describes the series. Selection may change over time (for example with environment or at an Ne epoch boundary), or the allele may plateau or fix; a single-s fit then averages across regimes or is dominated by saturated points that carry little information. For each locus, plot error-corrected logit(derived frequency) against generation and look for curvature, breakpoints (especially at Ne schedule boundaries) and samples stuck near 0 or 1. Compare a constant-s model with a piecewise-s model by likelihood ratio or AIC. Report the constant-s estimate only if it fits adequately; otherwise say so and justify which interval defines s. Points near fixation should carry little weight, which a correct binomial-plus-error likelihood does automatically.

sl-test-v2-1c9257fd709f.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-1c9257fd709f.text: PLAN: Estimate per-allele (g=0/1/2) natural-log rate ratio of CXCL10 in activated monocytes. Method: cell QC (MAD thresholds on log total_umi, HBB fraction, LST1 fraction, fixed before looking at genotype); gate activation using (IFI6+ISG15)/total_umi via 2-component Gaussian mixture on log scale (no CXCL10); estimate ambient rho from HBB in clean cells vs empty drops and subtract ambient CXCL10; pseudobulk per donor in activated stratum, NB/Poisson GLM count ~ g + offset(log sum total_umi), donors with <5 activated cells dropped. Checks: cells per donor/genotype, covariate balance sex/age/bmi, overdispersion, depth by genotype, composition (activated fraction vs g), g*state interaction, gate sensitivity, with/without ambient correction and QC. Would change method if LST1-low cells are actually activated monocytes (not contaminants), if overdispersion high (NB), or if covariates imbalanced.

sl-test-v2-5d5b8fe5010b.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-5d5b8fe5010b.text: PLAN: Estimate per-allele (g=0/1/2) log rate ratio of CXCL10 in activated monocytes (ISG-high: IFI6/ISG15 high, LST1 low). Method: cluster cells into activated vs resting by ISG/LST1 markers; estimate per-cell ambient contamination from HBB using empty-drop ambient profile; subtract ambient CXCL10 expectation (or model it as offset); aggregate per donor (pseudobulk) and fit NB/quasi-Poisson GLM of donor CXCL10 counts on g with log(total_umi) offset, adjusting sex/age/bmi as sensitivity. Donor is the unit (24 donors), not cells. Checks: duplicates, cluster separation, HBB as ambient marker, raw vs corrected beta, cell-level GLMM vs pseudobulk, covariate adjustment. Change method if ambient correction moves beta substantively or clusters not separable.

sl-test-v2-d69f8f3b7638.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-d69f8f3b7638.text: PLAN: Estimate per-replicate log2(O/E) at 20kb pixel (8,17), dist 9, then average per condition (2 ctrl, 2 case), delta=case-control. Primary: per-replicate ICE balancing (cis, ignore dist 1, mask low-mappability bins 10,11 and low-coverage bins >5 MAD), expected = mean of balanced valid pixels on diagonal 9 in same replicate. Checks: depth and P(s) slopes per rep, coverage vs gc/mappability/re_sites, bins 8/17 coverage, zeros, diagonal-9 mean vs median vs leave-out vs smoothed P(s), raw O/E, 3x3 neighbourhood, donut local enrichment, 40kb pixel (4,8) confirmed by coordinates. Change method if balancing fails to converge or the results swing sign under alternatives.

sl-test-v2-2c693357b0ab.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-2c693357b0ab.text: PLAN: Estimate log2(O/E) at 20kb pixel (8,17), dist 9 bins, per replicate, averaged within condition, delta=case-control. Method: per replicate, filter low-mappability bins (10,11 have mappability 0.42/0.46), ICE-balance the 20kb matrix (no diagonal present), expected = mean balanced count per diagonal over valid pixels, O/E at (8,17), log2, average reps. Use 20kb file only (40kb is the wrong resolution for this pixel). Checks: depth differences between reps, GC/mappability bias of counts, replicate concordance, sensitivity raw vs balanced, excluding target pixel from expected, GC regression. Change method if balancing fails to converge or if raw vs balanced differ greatly due to bias.

sl-test-v2-e99f963b69ea.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-e99f963b69ea.text: WARNING SIGN: LST1 fraction is bimodal and nearly perfectly anti-aligned with the ISG state: 318 of 352 ISG-high cells have LST1/total<0.02 vs 3 of 236 ISG-low cells. MEANS: low LST1 marks activated monocytes here, not non-monocyte contaminants; a 'low LST1' QC filter would delete the activated stratum. ACTION: dropped the LST1-based QC filter; QC uses total_umi and HBB only.

sl-test-v2-f887c54a2b4f.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-f887c54a2b4f.text: PLAN: Estimate haploid selection coefficient s of the derived allele at the more strongly selected locus. Derived allele polarized by outgroup (outgroup=T=alt, so derived=ref C; derived freq = 1-alt). Method: Wright-Fisher HMM (discretized frequency grid, piecewise Ne schedule, haploid selection p'=p(1+s)/(1+ps)) with binomial read emission incorporating asymmetric miscall (C->T damage e1, T->C e2=0.01, mean=seq_error), max likelihood over s and initial freq; compare loci by LRT vs s=0. Checks: polarization, zero-depth sample, error model symmetric vs asymmetric feasibility, sensitivity to e2, Ne. Change method if asymmetric error model fits poorly or results unstable.

sl-test-v2-66ee44626c15.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-66ee44626c15.text: WARNING SIGN: Activated (ISG-high, LST1-low) fraction rises strongly with genotype: 0.28 (g0), 0.55 (g1), 0.84 (g2); bimodal ISG/LST1 score cleanly separates 335 activated vs 253 resting cells. MEANS: Pooling all cells would confound composition with per-allele expression effect. ACTION: Restrict to activated cluster and estimate within it.

sl-test-v2-a618cf0a175a.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-a618cf0a175a.text: WARNING SIGN: HBB fraction (ambient marker, 7.0% of empty-drop UMI; CXCL10 is 4.9% of ambient) is ~0.022 in donors D09,D11,D13,D15,D17-D24 vs ~0.007 elsewhere, so ambient contamination is confounded with genotype (g2 all high). MEANS: raw CXCL10 counts are inflated by ambient RNA more in g2 donors, biasing beta upward. ACTION: estimate per-cell contamination from HBB vs empty-drop profile and remove expected ambient CXCL10 (offset/subtraction model).

sl-test-v2-758884956c69.reason: The task asks for a source-population OR; ignoring the outcome-dependent sampling design would change the estimand and the reported subhap_log_or.
sl-test-v2-758884956c69.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the files: the cohort is not a random sample of the source population. sampling_design.tsv reportedly gives a sample_fraction for each cell of clinic_stratum x recruitment_stream x ancestry_group x age_band x case, so sampling depends on both outcome and stratum. An unweighted logistic regression then estimates a sample-conditional odds ratio, not the source-population odds ratio the task asks for; because the fractions differ by stratum and the stratum variables (e.g. ancestry) may correlate with structural-variant dosage, the bias is not confined to the intercept. Check: merge sample_fraction onto every cohort row by all five keys (using age_band, not continuous age), confirm every row matches exactly one fraction, and compare the weighted and unweighted log OR. If confirmed: fit an inverse-probability-weighted logistic model (weight = 1/sample_fraction) with design-based (sandwich/survey) standard errors, and report the weighted estimate as subhap_log_or.

sl-test-v2-8be896ff1290.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-8be896ff1290.text: WARNING SIGN: seq_error column is 0.16 for every sample, far above the stated ~1% instrument error, and locus A gen6 alt fraction 36/40=0.90 exceeds 1-0.16=0.84, impossible under a symmetric 16% error model. MEANS: error is asymmetric (ancient DNA, sample_year negative: C->T deamination inflates T=alt reads); with T->C ~0.01, C->T ~0.31. ACTION: use asymmetric emission model P(T read)=pT(1-e2)+(1-pT)e1, e2=0.01, e1=2*0.16-0.01; sensitivity tested.

sl-test-v2-eac317962fe2.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-eac317962fe2.text: WARNING SIGN: outgroup allele equals alt (T) at both loci, so alt is ancestral. MEANS: derived allele is ref C; selection must be measured on 1-alt frequency (alt fraction falls over time). ACTION: polarize to derived=C.

sl-test-v2-1ef719a4bfbe.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-1ef719a4bfbe.text: WARNING SIGN: generation 36 has total_reads=0 at both loci. MEANS: no information, must not be treated as frequency 0. ACTION: skip emission at that time point (drift still propagated).

sl-test-v2-7202d18ae22b.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-7202d18ae22b.text: PLAN: Estimate haploid derived-allele s (p'=p(1+s)/(1+sp)) at both loci A and B. Polarise via outgroup (outgroup=T=alt at both loci, so derived=ref C, derived freq=1-alt). Method: haploid Wright-Fisher HMM on a discretised frequency grid with drift per generation using the piecewise Ne schedule (generation axis, not sample_year), binomial read emission with error inside the likelihood; drop the zero-read sample. Profile-likelihood 95% CI and LRT vs s=0 per locus; compare to deterministic fit; check constant vs piecewise s (AIC). Error model: seq_error column is 0.16 but task says instrument error ~1%; since ref=C/alt=T and samples are ancient (years -4500..-2500), test asymmetric model with T->C=0.01 and C->T=2*0.16-0.01=0.31 (aDNA deamination) vs symmetric 0.16 vs symmetric 0.01, choose by fit/consistency. Would change method if the error models give inconsistent locus choice or the data are impossible under a model.

sl-test-v2-e6649cdf2e7d.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-e6649cdf2e7d.text: WARNING SIGN: seq_error column is 0.16 for every sample at both loci, versus the task's ~1% instrument error; ref=C, alt=T and sample_year spans -4500 to -2500 (ancient DNA). Under symmetric e=0.16 the observed alt freq cannot exceed 0.84, but locus A gen 6 has 36/40=0.90. MEANS: the excess error is likely directional C->T deamination damage, so a symmetric error model is wrong; with avg 0.16 and T->C=0.01, C->T~0.31. ACTION: use asymmetric emission alt_obs = q(1-0.01) + (1-q)*0.31 as primary model, symmetric variants as sensitivity.

sl-test-v2-b876bd135f0e.reason: Which variables go into weights versus the covariate set directly changes the fitted odds ratio and whether it is the requested total effect.
sl-test-v2-b876bd135f0e.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against file_notes.tsv: recruitment_stream and age_band are sampling-design strata, not baseline clinical covariates. Putting recruitment_stream (or the design cells) into the outcome model as covariates, instead of using them to build weights, changes the estimand and can over-adjust; adjusting for age_band instead of continuous age loses information (file_notes reportedly says to use continuous age for clinical adjustment). Check: read file_notes.tsv and list, before modelling, which variables are weighting strata and which are covariates. If confirmed: use clinic_stratum, recruitment_stream, ancestry_group, age_band and case only to build the sampling weights; adjust the outcome model for continuous age, sex and pc1-pc3 (ancestry_group may also be considered as a confounder of SV frequency), and not for recruitment_stream.

sl-test-v2-69d9b2c089b4.reason: The task demands a full-cohort estimate per calibrated copy; how dosage is obtained for non-panel samples determines both bias and scale of subhap_log_or and expression_log_fc.
sl-test-v2-69d9b2c089b4.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the files: breakpoint_panel.tsv is a long-read calibration subset, not an association cohort. Running the clinical association only on panel samples (small and non-random), or treating panel calls as if they existed for everyone, gives a biased and imprecise OR. Full-cohort segment-B dosage has to come from a calibration model that maps the tag markers to the long-read segment-B copy index, trained on reliable panel samples and applied to every cohort sample (regression calibration: use the expected copies given markers, not hard-thresholded calls). Check: count the overlap of panel sample_ids with the cohort and tag-marker files, and cross-validate the marker-to-copy prediction (R^2 / concordance) within the panel. If the predicted dosage is shrunk or rescaled relative to the true copy number, rescale so that the OR is per true calibrated copy.

sl-test-v2-7bf4c6688ef3.reason: n_calibrated_carriers is defined on reliable panel samples, and the calibration training set depends on the same filter; an unfiltered or unrounded panel changes the count and the calibration.
sl-test-v2-7bf4c6688ef3.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the files: long-read breakpoint calls in this repeat-rich region are unreliable for some panel samples (signs: low molecule_count, low mean_mapq, high alignment_entropy, unbalanced pair_balance, high local_complexity), and copy_index_segment_B is a continuous index, not an integer. Training the calibration, or counting carriers, on unfiltered or unrounded values adds noise and miscounts n_calibrated_carriers. Check: look at the distribution of each QC field and of copy_index_segment_B (clusters near 0/1/2 and off-cluster outliers), and whether outliers concentrate in high-complexity or low-MAPQ samples. If confirmed: define a reliability filter from the QC fields with thresholds stated in advance and justified by the distributions, assign integer copies (round/cluster) among reliable samples only, and count carriers (>= 1 copy) only among reliable samples.

sl-test-v2-4333a6c2263a.reason: The task explicitly requires separating nested segment-B dosage from outer-orientation dosage while reporting a total effect; getting either wrong changes the sign or size of subhap_log_or.
sl-test-v2-4333a6c2263a.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the files: the nested segment-B dosage sits inside a broader outer-orientation polymorphism (bp_alt_fraction reportedly measures outer orientation), so the two dosages are correlated. A marginal regression on B, or a B predictor built from markers that actually tag the outer orientation, attributes the outer effect to B. Check: in reliable panel samples, cross-tabulate integer B copies against outer-orientation dosage (bp_alt_fraction near 0/0.5/1), find which marker blocks predict B separately from outer, and check the correlation of predicted B and predicted outer dosage in the cohort. If confirmed: calibrate both B and outer dosage and fit the clinical model with both terms so the B coefficient is separated from the outer effect. Because the target is a total effect of B, do not put expression or other downstream consequences of B into the clinical model.

sl-test-v2-d1ee4598acc1.reason: Ancestry-dependent tagging would bias the calibrated dosage differentially and confound the clinical association; this determines whether the calibration and outcome models need ancestry terms.
sl-test-v2-d1ee4598acc1.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the files: repeat-mediated inversions and copy-number variants are often recurrent or sit on several haplotype backgrounds, so marker tagging is weaker than for SNPs and can differ by ancestry. A tag model trained mostly on one ancestry can mis-predict the others and confound the OR with ancestry. Check: report calibration accuracy by ancestry_group within the reliable panel, and check whether segment-B frequency differs by ancestry group or PCs. If confirmed: include ancestry (PCs and/or ancestry_group) in the calibration model or fit ancestry-aware predictors, adjust the clinical model for PCs, and flag any ancestry group with poor tagging.

sl-test-v2-82aa2621626a.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-82aa2621626a.text: WARNING SIGN: generation 36 has total_reads=0 at both loci. MEANS: no information at that time point. ACTION: drop it from emissions (HMM still propagates drift through it).

sl-test-v2-b146a1db8b01.reason: Choice of the expression-supported gene and its per-copy fold-change depends on whether mapping and technical artefacts are ruled out; this drives expression_log_fc and target_support_code.
sl-test-v2-b146a1db8b01.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the files: genes inside duplicated or copy-variable segments have multimapping reads, so short-read expression can track copy number through mapping artefacts rather than biology, and a gene can look expression-supported only because of mismapping.
