Check: for each candidate gene, regress log_expr on calibrated B dosage with and without the technical fields (multimapper_fraction / unique_fraction, tissue_source, expr_batch, assay_depth_millions, gc_metric); see whether the B effect is stable and whether multimapper_fraction itself rises with B copy. If confirmed: identify the supported gene as the one whose B effect survives adjustment for technical covariates (batch, tissue, depth, GC, uniqueness) and for the outer-orientation dosage, and take expression_log_fc from that adjusted model.

sl-test-v2-284fba89a7a9.reason: The expression panel inherits the outcome-dependent sampling; without handling it, expression_log_fc may not reflect the source population.
sl-test-v2-284fba89a7a9.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the files: the expression panel is a subset of a case-enriched sample. If case status is related to expression, an unweighted expression-on-dosage regression in such a sample is a biased secondary-trait analysis. Check: test whether log_expr differs by case status and whether the case proportion in the expression panel differs from the source population. If confirmed: include case status as a covariate or weight expression samples by the inverse sampling fraction, and report how much the per-copy estimate changes between the approaches.

sl-test-v2-d4d101b1ec42.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-d4d101b1ec42.text: WARNING SIGN: Ambient contamination differs by donor and is confounded with genotype: median per-cell HBB fraction is ~0.007 in all 8 g=0 donors but ~0.016-0.025 in all g=2 donors and 4 of 8 g=1 donors (empty-drop HBB fraction 0.070, so rho ~0.1 vs ~0.3). Empty drops have CXCL10 fraction 0.049, about 3x the cell average 0.017. MEANS: ambient CXCL10 makes up a large, genotype-correlated share of cell counts and also inflates ISG markers used for gating; a pooled single rho or no correction would bias beta. ACTION: estimate rho per donor from HBB, subtract donor-specific ambient expectation from CXCL10, IFI6 and ISG15 before gating and aggregation, and report beta with and without correction.

sl-test-v2-3ab7d22fe60d.reason: A wrong log base or a carrier-versus-copy coding would give numerically wrong expression_log_fc and subhap_log_or even with a correct model.
sl-test-v2-3ab7d22fe60d.text: Library guidance (gb05), to be verified against the file notes: log_expr is reportedly already on the natural-log scale. The per-copy fold-change must be the regression slope of log_expr on the calibrated copy dosage in natural-log units, not a log2 value and not a slope on hard 0/1 carrier status. Likewise subhap_log_or must be per additional copy (additive dosage) on the natural-log scale. Check: confirm the dosage scale (0, 1, 2 copies) and the log base before reporting, and rescale slopes to per-copy natural-log units if needed.

sl-test-v2-66412a7baea3.reason: A data-specific trap that silently invalidates the haplotype reconstruction and the reported position if the team assumes the files are already ordered and aligned.
sl-test-v2-66412a7baea3.text: The library reports that the gb10 input files are not in genetic-map order: the rows of markers.tsv and founders.tsv and the marker columns of ril_genotypes.npz are shuffled and mix chromosome 1 and chromosome 2 markers (the reported first IDs are m2_065, m2_103, m2_107, m1_054). Any HMM or interval scan run in file order gives meaningless haplotype probabilities and a wrong peak. Confirm this in the data, then join every table by marker_id and by sample_id (never by row index), check that the sample_id order in the npz agrees with phenotypes.tsv, and sort markers by chromosome and then pos_cM before computing genotype probabilities or LOD curves.

sl-test-v2-a57beefdab54.reason: A coding mistake would directly corrupt the high_founder answer; the team needs to know the two files use different value sets and that the meaning of -1 has to be checked.
sl-test-v2-a57beefdab54.text: The library reports that the genotype codings differ between gb10 files: RIL genotypes in ril_genotypes.npz are int8 values in {1, 0, -1}, while founder genotypes in founders.tsv are 0/1. The meaning of -1 is not established (it could be missing, or a heterozygous call), so do not assume it. Tabulate the values, count -1 per marker and per RIL, and verify that the RIL and founder codes refer to the same allele (each RIL should match some founder at nearly every marker over long runs). Treat -1 as missing unless the data documentation says otherwise (heterozygous calls in inbred lines are normally treated as missing too), never as a third allele, and drop markers that are monomorphic across the 8 founders. A flipped or misread coding can reverse the founder assignment, so that the lowest founder is reported as the highest.

sl-test-v2-32766f507189.reason: It determines the core method: a SNP-by-SNP scan, the obvious first approach, cannot answer the founder half of the question.
sl-test-v2-32766f507189.text: A single-marker association on the biallelic SNPs cannot identify which founder carries the high allele: each SNP only splits the 8 founders into two groups, and several founders usually share each allele. At any peak SNP, count how many founders carry each allele in founders.tsv; if more than one carries the high allele, the SNP result alone does not name a founder. The appropriate method is to reconstruct 8-founder haplotype probabilities with a multipoint HMM over the ordered markers (R/qtl2 calc_genoprob with an 8-way selfed RIL cross type such as riself8, or an equivalent hand-written HMM), run an 8-founder additive scan (7 degrees of freedom) on those probabilities, and read high_founder from the founder coefficients at the peak.

sl-test-v2-29402f7aa267.reason: It sets an HMM parameter and a QC and sensitivity step that affect both reported quantities; a zero-error HMM is fragile to a handful of bad calls.
sl-test-v2-29402f7aa267.text: Genotyping errors or residual heterozygosity in RILs or founders create false double recombinants that distort the haplotype probabilities and can move both the peak position and the founder assignment. An error in a founder genotype is the most damaging kind, because every RIL is decoded against the founders. Run the HMM with a nonzero genotyping-error probability (about 0.002 to 0.01), count inferred crossovers per RIL and look for outlier lines with very many, look for markers whose calls conflict with their flanking markers, and check per-marker missing rates. Drop or mask bad markers and samples, and confirm that the peak and the top founder are stable when the error probability is varied between 0.001 and 0.01.

sl-test-v2-8f3de7ffb05f.reason: A covariate and phenotype-QC decision that can change the LOD curve, the peak location and the founder ranking.
sl-test-v2-8f3de7ffb05f.text: The library reports that the gb10 phenotype file has a batch column. Leaving batch out adds residual noise and, if batch is unbalanced across founder haplotypes, can shift the founder effects and the peak. Compare phenotype means and variances by batch and cross-tabulate batch against founder haplotype at the peak. If batch matters, include it as an additive covariate in the null model, the QTL scan, the founder-effect estimation and the permutations alike, and consider a batch-by-QTL interaction if effects differ by batch. Also check the phenotype for outliers or skew; if present, repeat the scan on a rank-based inverse normal transform and check that the peak does not move.

sl-test-v2-82e21847c702.reason: It tells the team that chromosome 2 is not just a distraction (it supplies the kinship and possibly a background covariate) and adds a robustness comparison that could change the chromosome 1 result.
sl-test-v2-82e21847c702.text: Relatedness and population structure among multi-parent RILs (from the crossing design and uneven founder contributions) can inflate LOD scores and create ghost peaks, and genetic effects on other chromosomes inflate residual variance. Compare the chromosome 1 LOD curve and peak from plain Haley-Knott regression with a linear mixed model that uses a leave-one-chromosome-out kinship matrix (for a chromosome 1 scan, kinship computed from chromosome 2 only). Also scan chromosome 2: if it carries a strong QTL, include it as a covariate when scanning chromosome 1. If the peak or the top founder shifts under the mixed model, report the mixed-model result.

sl-test-v2-93d357403f14.reason: It changes how qtl_pos_cM is obtained (grid rather than marker positions, handling of multiple peaks) and supplies the significance and precision reasoning the task is graded on.
sl-test-v2-93d357403f14.text: Do not report only the argmax marker. The library reports that the population has about 120 RILs; with that size and a 7-df founder model the LOD peak may be broad or there may be more than one peak, and a marker-only scan restricts the position to marker locations. Scan a pseudomarker grid (for example 1 cM) between markers; get a significance threshold by permutation (shuffle phenotypes with batch kept attached to the phenotype, about 1000 permutations, genome-wide maximum LOD); and compute a 1.5-LOD support interval or 95% Bayes credible interval on chromosome 1. If chromosome 1 shows two separated peaks, fit a two-QTL model or a conditional scan with the top QTL as a covariate before choosing a position. Give the position as the peak of the full 8-founder (or mixed-model) LOD curve and quote the interval in the reasoning.

sl-test-v2-464672bec552.reason: It guards the high_founder call against a noise-driven coefficient and prescribes a specific cross-check that could change which founder is reported.
sl-test-v2-464672bec552.text: Founder-effect estimates at the QTL can be unstable or extreme when a founder haplotype is rare at that locus. With about 120 RILs each of 8 founders is expected in only about 15 lines and may be present in far fewer, so a sparsely represented founder can get the largest fixed-effect coefficient by chance. At the peak, sum the founder haplotype probabilities across RILs to get the expected number of lines per founder, look at the standard errors of the founder coefficients, and compare the fixed-effect coefficients with shrunken estimates (BLUPs, e.g. qtl2 scan1blup or an equivalent random-effect/ridge fit). Report a founder as high only if it stays on top under the shrunken estimates and is clearly separated from the runner-up; state in the reasoning any tie, or any founders that share the same SNP haplotype in the region and so cannot be distinguished.

sl-test-v2-81bf286e3fb1.reason: A sign or contrast misreading would give the wrong founder even after a correct scan; the raw group-mean check is cheap and decisive.
sl-test-v2-81bf286e3fb1.text: The high-effect founder is the one with the highest positive effect on the phenotype, not the one with the most extreme coefficient regardless of sign. Coefficients are also easy to misread under different contrasts: a sum-to-zero parameterisation (qtl2 scan1coef with zerosum=TRUE) gives 8 effects that sum to zero plus an intercept, whereas a reference-founder parameterisation gives effects relative to one omitted founder. As a contrast-free check, at the peak assign each RIL to its most likely founder haplotype (probability above 0.5), compute the raw mean phenotype per founder group, and confirm that the founder with the highest group mean is the founder with the largest positive coefficient before reporting it.

sl-test-v2-1edd3b3b34e0.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-1edd3b3b34e0.text: WARNING SIGN: 20kb bins 10 and 11 have mappability 0.42/0.46 but ~2.8-3.1x mean row coverage in every replicate (row coverage vs mappability r=-0.88). MEANS: these bins are artefactual pileups, not real signal; they inflate expected values on diagonals they touch, including dist 9. ACTION: exclude bins 10,11 from expected and balancing (mapping filter >0.5).

sl-test-v2-a86b8020cf59.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-a86b8020cf59.text: WARNING SIGN: sequencing depth differs: case reps ~16.1k/15.1k contacts vs control 10.4k/8.4k at 20kb. MEANS: raw counts not comparable across conditions; O/E must be computed within each replicate. ACTION: per-replicate expected, which makes O/E depth-invariant.

sl-test-v2-e965c0c1df82.reason: Decides the estimand: univariable MR would answer a different question from the conditional effect the task defines, and instrument collinearity determines whether the joint estimate can be trusted.
sl-test-v2-e965c0c1df82.text: The task asks for the DIRECT effect of each protein on disease conditional on the other. Running a separate (univariable) Mendelian randomization for PROTA and for PROTB gives total effects that are contaminated by the neighbouring protein when the two share cis-pQTLs, so it does not answer the question. Fit both proteins jointly (multivariable MR: SNP-disease beta regressed on the SNP-PROTA and SNP-PROTB betas together, using an LD-aware GLS). Joint estimation only works if the SNP effects on PROTA and on PROTB are not collinear across the instruments: check the correlation of the two sets of SNP-protein betas and compute conditional (Sanderson-Windmeijer type) F-statistics for each protein. The library's rule of thumb is that a conditional F below about 10 for either protein signals weak-instrument bias and inflated variance; in that case choose instruments from the union of signals for either protein so that some SNPs separate the two, use weak-instrument-robust inference (e.g. Q-minimisation / LIML-type), and report the conditional F with the estimates.

sl-test-v2-7496f0b20674.reason: How LD is handled changes both the point estimate and its uncertainty; both the no-LD and the all-SNPs shortcuts fail in a single-locus design.
sl-test-v2-7496f0b20674.text: The instruments come from one locus and are in LD, so the correlation reference has to be used, but carefully. Treating correlated SNPs as independent (plain IVW with no LD matrix) double-counts information and gives wrong weights and standard errors. The opposite error is to put all variants into a GLS and invert an ill-conditioned LD matrix, which gives numerically unstable and over-precise estimates. Check the eigenvalues / condition number of the LD matrix restricted to the chosen instruments, and re-run the estimate at several pruning thresholds (library suggestion: r^2 < 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) and with principal components of the weighted LD matrix (keeping ~99% of variance). Use correlated-instrument GLS, theta = (Bx' S^-1 Bx)^-1 Bx' S^-1 by with S = diag(se_y) R diag(se_y), on a pruned set or on PCs. If the point estimate moves or the SE collapses (e.g. by more than 3x) as more correlated SNPs are added, treat that as instability and prefer the more conservative fit.

sl-test-v2-3f44864f79c3.reason: Unharmonised alleles flip signs of SNP effects, which can reverse or cancel the causal estimates; the library points to a concrete mismatch in this dataset.
sl-test-v2-3f44864f79c3.text: Effect alleles are reported by the library to differ between the input files. Its example (not verified by the director, confirm it in the files): the phase 2 protein files code rs200000 with effect allele C, while phase 1, the disease association file and the variant metadata use A. Before any selection, meta-analysis or MR, compare effect_allele/other_allele for every SNP across all protein phase files, the disease association file, the variant metadata and the allele coding of the LD reference, and count mismatches. Where alleles are swapped relative to one chosen reference coding, multiply beta by -1 and use 1-EAF; drop SNPs whose alleles cannot be matched.

sl-test-v2-83b1efb7af50.reason: A misordered, unsigned or allele-inconsistent LD matrix silently corrupts the GLS weights; this check is separate from harmonising the betas and is easy to miss.
sl-test-v2-83b1efb7af50.text: The LD matrix must be the SIGNED correlation matrix, in the same SNP order and the same effect-allele coding as the harmonised summary statistics. Check that the 'snp' order in locus_correlation_EUR.npz matches the order used for the betas, that R is symmetric with unit diagonal and positive semi-definite, and that z-scores are consistent with R (predict each SNP's z from its neighbours through R; large outliers suggest an allele flip or mismatch). Reorder R to the analysis order; if SNP j is flipped relative to the summary statistics, multiply row and column j of R by -1; drop SNPs whose z-scores cannot be reconciled with the LD reference. Do not use r^2 in place of signed r.

sl-test-v2-b3cd58ca378e.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-b3cd58ca378e.text: WARNING SIGN: 20kb bins 10 and 11 have mappability 0.42/0.46 yet the highest coverage in every replicate (log-coverage z about +2.6 to +3.1), and coverage correlates negatively with mappability (r about -0.87). They also give large counts on diagonal 9 (pixels (1,10),(2,11),(10,19),(11,20)). MEANS: these are artefact bins that would inflate the diagonal-9 expected and distort balancing. ACTION: masked bins 10,11 before ICE and from the expected, leaving 11 valid diagonal-9 pixels per replicate.

sl-test-v2-0a2738e06bb7.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-0a2738e06bb7.text: WARNING SIGN: the distance-decay slope differs by condition (control about -1.49, case about -1.23) and depth differs (control 8.4k-10.4k vs case 15.1k-16.1k contacts). Controls have 14-15 zero pixels, all at distance 12 or more, none on diagonal 9. MEANS: pooling replicates or sharing an expected would confound depth and P(s) with the loop. ACTION: expected computed per replicate from diagonal 9 only. No pseudocount was needed.

sl-test-v2-3e8a6d18a5b1.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-3e8a6d18a5b1.text: WARNING SIGN: the gb03 (8,17) result depends on the choice of expected. ICE log2 O/E delta is 1.70 with the diagonal mean, 1.86 with the median, 1.99 with the target left out and 2.16 with a smoothed P(s). Controls range from about -0.65 to 0.0. MEANS: the sign and size of the effect are robust, but the absolute control value is uncertain at about +/-0.3. ACTION: kept the cooltools-style ICE diagonal mean as primary and reported the alternatives. 40kb pixel (4,8), confirmed by coordinates, agrees in direction (ICE delta 0.96). Donut local enrichment is case about 1.61 vs control about 0.03, so this is a focal loop gained in case.

sl-test-v2-a6201a02c887.reason: Determines which protein GWAS phase is used for selection and which for estimation; using the same phase for both, or pooling them, biases theta.
sl-test-v2-a6201a02c887.text: Winner's curse: if instruments are selected by p-value in a protein GWAS and the same sample's betas are then used for estimation, the SNP-protein effects are inflated, which biases the causal estimates (typically towards zero, and by a different amount for each protein). The library reports that the data contain two protein GWAS phases, a 'screening' phase 1 (reported n=12000) and a 'holdout' phase 2 (reported n=8000); confirm this in the metadata. After allele harmonisation, compare phase 1 and phase 2 betas for the selected SNPs: systematic shrinkage in phase 2 indicates winner's curse. The library's recommended design is to select instruments in phase 1 and take the SNP-protein effects used for estimation from phase 2 only (a three-sample design), rather than meta-analysing phase 1 into those betas, or else to apply a formal winner's-curse correction.

sl-test-v2-4974f4d9d275.reason: Without this rescaling, or with the wrong SD, the reported numbers are on the wrong scale even if the MR itself is correct.
sl-test-v2-4974f4d9d275.text: Scale: the target is log-odds per +1 SD of log10 concentration, but the library reports that the protein GWAS betas are per log10(ng/mL) unit (dataset_metadata unit = log10_ng_per_mL; confirm). An MR estimate from those betas is therefore per log10 unit, not per SD. Estimate the SD of log10 concentration for each protein from protein_measurements.tsv and convert: theta_per_SD = theta_per_log10_unit * SD_log10 (equivalently, divide the SNP-protein betas by the SD before MR). Use the same convention for both proteins and report the SDs used.

sl-test-v2-c264c1860b1a.reason: The SD is the conversion factor for the final answer, so any artefact in the measurement records propagates directly into both thetas.
sl-test-v2-c264c1860b1a.text: protein_measurements has a batch column. Shifts in mean or scale between batches inflate the pooled SD of log10 concentration, so a raw pooled SD would mis-scale the per-SD estimates. For each protein compare per-batch mean and SD of log10_concentration (and per-batch control_cv), test for batch differences (e.g. ANOVA), and look for outliers, out-of-range values and duplicated records. If batch effects or QC failures are present, compute the SD after removing them (within-batch centring or a pooled within-batch SD, after excluding failed/outlying records), state the choice, and show how theta changes between the pooled and the within-batch SD.

sl-test-v2-6dfd908d05a2.reason: It can shift the final scale of both estimates; the team should make this choice knowingly and show its sensitivity rather than discover the control_cv column late or ignore it.
sl-test-v2-6dfd908d05a2.text: A judgement call on the SD, flagged by the library as open rather than settled: the observed SD of log10 concentration includes technical assay noise, and the control_cv column gives the assay coefficient of variation. A CV can be converted to a log10-scale technical SD (approximately CV/ln(10) for small CV) and compared with the observed within-batch variance; also check whether CV differs by batch. pQTL betas themselves are not biased by classical measurement error in the protein, so this affects only the per-SD scaling. A noise-corrected SD would be sqrt(SD_obs^2 - SD_tech^2). The task text says only 'per +1 SD increase in log10 concentration' and does not say which SD is meant, so decide deliberately, justify the choice, and report how much the thetas differ between the observed and the noise-corrected SD.

sl-test-v2-7e00cb3fe2f7.reason: Confirms the outcome scale the answer must be on, and adds a heterogeneity check that can reveal invalid instruments or LD mismatch that would otherwise bias the estimates unnoticed.
sl-test-v2-7e00cb3fe2f7.text: The disease GWAS is case-control (library reports 15000 cases / 35000 controls; confirm), so its betas should be log odds ratios. Verify this (beta/se consistent with the reported p-value; values centred on 0 rather than on 1 as odds ratios would be) and keep everything on the log-odds scale: do not exponentiate and do not treat the outcome as linear or liability scale. Separately, a single external LD reference may not match the GWAS samples, which makes fixed-effect GLS over-precise. Compute Cochran's Q for the multivariable GLS fit against its chi-square degrees of freedom; if Q is large, use multiplicative random-effects standard errors and investigate the outlying SNPs (pleiotropy or LD mismatch) instead of trusting the fixed-effect precision.

sl-test-v2-44aae2906ca5.reason: Which roster rows are counted sets the denominator and numerator of both carrier frequencies, and everything downstream (residual risk, couple risk) inherits it. A team that pools all cohort rows gets a different, inflated answer.
sl-test-v2-44aae2906ca5.text: Match the sample to the estimand before estimating any carrier frequency. The task asks for carrier frequency among 'screening-roster adults', but cohort_roster may mix ascertainment routes: rows whose collection is not 'screening', and rows with family_history_tier above 0, are enriched for carriers and inflate the carrier frequency if pooled in. CHECK: tabulate cohort_roster by collection x ancestry x family_history_tier (and any field that marks adults) before computing anything. IF a mix is present: estimate carrier_frequency_afr and carrier_frequency_eur only on the rows that meet the task's 'screening-roster adult' definition, separately per ancestry, and state in the reasoning how many rows were excluded and why. Column names and values quoted here come from the library's reading of the schema; confirm them against the files.

sl-test-v2-5dfa5e4f756b.reason: The calling rule decides who is a carrier. Counting low-VAF artifacts as carriers, or no-calls as negatives, shifts the carrier frequencies and the detection rate, so it changes every reported quantity.
sl-test-v2-5dfa5e4f756b.text: Do not turn assay_observations rows into carrier calls without allele-fraction and missingness QC. True germline heterozygotes sit near VAF 0.5. Very low VAF points to an artifact, paralog reads or contamination. VAF near 1 at a heterozygous site can be an SNV in trans with a deletion on the other allele (apparent homozygosity), not a homozygous call. Blank vaf or log2_ratio values are no-calls, not negatives. CHECK: histogram VAF and alt_reads/depth per target and per batch; cross-tabulate high-VAF SNV calls against the copy-number target's log2_ratio (DRX1_T02); count blank/no-call rows per sample and per target. IF FOUND: require a heterozygous allele balance (roughly 0.3-0.7, with the exact cut-offs justified on calibration_controls) plus a minimum depth; reinterpret SNV-plus-deletion cases; treat no-calls as missing (exclude, impute, or let them lower the detection rate), never as screen-negative.

sl-test-v2-e7e6ec47230a.reason: A paralog artifact cluster would add false carriers, possibly concentrated in one target or batch, and bias carrier frequency upward; filtering it also changes the sensitivity that goes into the detection rate.
sl-test-v2-e7e6ec47230a.text: Paralog/pseudogene or segmental-duplication reads can mismap onto DRX1 and create false heterozygous SNV calls, and median MAPQ alone can miss this because a variant can make paralog reads look uniquely mapped. CHECK: in assay_observations compare paralog_kmer_fraction, segmental_dup_score and mapq_median between alt-supporting calls and reference calls, per target and per batch; look for a cluster of low-VAF calls (about 0.1-0.3) with high paralog fraction or low MAPQ. IF FOUND: treat those calls as artifacts/no-calls rather than carriers, with thresholds validated on calibration_controls and set before looking at ancestry-level results, and reduce the assay's effective sensitivity/specificity for the affected target accordingly.

sl-test-v2-e19d069f3148.reason: A global cut-off under a batch shift miscalls deletion carriers in some batches. If the deletion class differs in frequency by ancestry, that error falls unevenly on AFR and EUR and changes the carrier frequencies and the AFR detection rate.
sl-test-v2-e19d069f3148.text: Exon-deletion calls on the copy-number target (DRX1_T02, read out as log2_ratio) should not use one global threshold across batches or lots, because depth ratios shift by batch. A heterozygous deletion should sit near log2(1/2) = -1 relative to the batch-matched normal median. CHECK: plot log2_ratio for DRX1_T02 by batch, and use calibration_controls (known deletion-class versus normal samples per source_batch) to see where the two clusters fall in each batch. IF a batch shift is present: re-centre log2 ratios per batch against batch-matched normal controls, call deletions with batch-specific cut-offs or a mixture model, and estimate deletion-call sensitivity per batch from the controls.

sl-test-v2-b57fd273c129.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-b57fd273c129.text: PLAN gb05: Quantity = source-population total-effect log OR per calibrated segment-B copy, plus per-copy natural-log expression slope for the supported gene and count of reliable panel carriers. Method: (1) QC breakpoint panel with prestated thresholds from QC field distributions, round copy_index_segment_B to integer copies among reliable samples, count carriers >=1; (2) calibrate B copies and outer dosage (2*bp_alt_fraction) from tag markers (ridge/linear on marker blocks + PCs/ancestry), cross-validated R2 overall and by ancestry, apply expected dosage to full cohort, rescale if shrunk; (3) IPW logistic (w=1/sample_fraction merged on 5 keys) of case on predicted B + predicted outer + age + sex + pc1-3 (+ancestry), sandwich SE, compare unweighted; (4) per gene regress log_expr on calibrated B (true B where available) adjusting outer dosage, case status, batch, tissue, depth, gc, uniqueness; supported gene = B effect survives. Change method if: calibration fails in an ancestry, weights don't merge uniquely, B effect vanishes with outer term, or expression effect is only technical.

sl-test-v2-0a49f512c4eb.reason: Carrier frequency is a per-person quantity. Summing positive rows, or misreading cis pairs as two carriers or as affected, changes the carrier counts and the split of carriers across variant classes that the detection rate depends on.
sl-test-v2-0a49f512c4eb.text: Count persons, not variant rows, and check phase when one person is positive at more than one target. Two variants in the same person (for example the two class_03 sites DRX1_T03 and DRX1_T04, or an SNV plus the exon deletion) can be double-counted as two carriers, or wrongly labelled. In cis they are one carrier allele (a complex allele); in trans the person is compound heterozygous, i.e. affected rather than a carrier. CHECK: for each sample with more than one positive target, inspect phase_set (same phase set means same haplotype block), and measure how often T03 and T04 co-occur, which would point to a single complex allele in linkage disequilibrium. IF FOUND: collapse cis co-occurring variants into one carrier allele; treat confirmed trans pairs as non-carriers for carrier-frequency purposes, or flag them; keep unphased pairs as explicitly ambiguous and say how they were handled.

sl-test-v2-83bba53ad228.reason: Whether carrier frequency is reported as the raw positive rate or as a sensitivity-corrected rate changes carrier_frequency_afr, carrier_frequency_eur and the residual risk. The calibration controls are the only source for that correction.
sl-test-v2-83bba53ad228.text: An observed screen-positive rate is not the true carrier frequency when the assay has imperfect sensitivity or specificity, and sensitivity should not be assumed equal across variant classes, batches or ancestries. CHECK: use calibration_controls (ancestry x reference_category x source_batch) to estimate, under the same final calling rules applied to the cohort, the sensitivity per variant class and batch and the false-positive rate. IF sensitivity or specificity is materially below 1: correct the observed prevalence with a Rogan-Gladen-type adjustment, true = (obs + Sp - 1)/(Se + Sp - 1), or a Bayesian equivalent, and feed the class- and batch-specific sensitivities into the detection rate. Propagate the uncertainty, which matters most for rare classes.

sl-test-v2-9d709307fa59.reason: residual_carrier_risk_afr_negative depends directly on the formula and on which detection rate is used. The shortcut formula and a pooled DR each give a different number, and the error carries into couple_reproductive_risk.
sl-test-v2-9d709307fa59.text: Compute the AFR residual carrier risk with the full Bayes formula and an AFR-specific detection rate. Two common errors: (1) using CF*(1-DR), or CF minus the detected-carrier frequency, which drops the Bayesian denominator; (2) reusing a pooled or EUR detection rate for AFR. The variant classes (reported_group class_01 SNV, class_02 deletion, class_03 sites) can differ sharply in frequency by ancestry, so the detection rate can differ a lot between AFR and EUR. CHECK: compare the frequency of each class by ancestry in both the screening samples and the controls. Then compute DR for AFR as the fraction of AFR carriers whose variants the screen would detect, from AFR class frequencies and class-specific assay sensitivity, and compute residual risk = CF*(1-DR)/(1-CF*DR). Keep CF and DR within ancestry throughout, never transfer the EUR DR to AFR, and report on the probability scale.

sl-test-v2-49923c6d212b.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-49923c6d212b.text: PLAN: Estimate chr1 QTL position (cM) and high-effect founder. Method: join all tables by marker_id/sample_id, sort markers by chr,pos; treat -1 as missing; drop founder-monomorphic markers; hand-written 8-state RIL-selfing HMM (Python, no R available) with error prob 0.005 on 1 cM pseudomarker grid; Haley-Knott 8-founder additive scan with batch covariate; LOCO kinship LMM comparison; chr2 scan and chr2 QTL covariate; 1000 permutations for threshold; 1.5-LOD interval; founder coefs plus ridge-shrunken coefs, expected counts per founder, raw group means. Checks: crossover counts per RIL, conflicting markers, missingness, error-prob sensitivity 0.001-0.01, batch balance, phenotype skew/INT. Change method if: two peaks (two-QTL model), batch effect (covariate), LMM shifts peak (report LMM), founder ties (report).

sl-test-v2-b7b7958f910e.reason: The task defines the partner as a uniformly sampled roster row. Using a single ancestry CF, or only tested partners, changes partner_carrier_frequency_full_roster and therefore couple_reproductive_risk.
sl-test-v2-b7b7958f910e.text: The partner term is a mixture over every partner_roster row, not the screening-roster carrier frequency. The partner roster's mix of ancestry, family-history tier and testing status differs from the screening cohort. CHECK: tabulate partner_roster by partner_ancestry x family_history_tier x testing_status. Assign each row a carrier probability from its own stratum (ancestry, family_history_tier, and testing status/result: the known result where testing is completed, the appropriate prior or post-negative residual risk otherwise), then average over all rows with equal weight to get partner_carrier_frequency_full_roster. Do not drop rows whose testing is not completed. Couple reproductive risk = residual carrier risk of the AFR screen-negative index x that row-averaged partner carrier probability x 1/4. Index and partner are independent, so the mixture is linear, but the partner strata must be computed explicitly rather than replaced by one aggregate ancestry CF.

sl-test-v2-178927e63a43.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-178927e63a43.text: WARNING SIGN: anchor bins 8 and 17 have high GC (0.58, 0.57), and counts rise with GC in every replicate (NB GLM coef ~1.1 per unit of summed GC, consistent across reps). MEANS: a distance-only expected overstates O/E at the anchors by about 0.17 log2. ACTION: expected now comes from a per-replicate NB GLM with distance-diagonal factors plus summed-GC covariate, fit without bad bins 10,11 and without the target pixel.

sl-test-v2-f9ffd5871edf.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-f9ffd5871edf.text: PLAN: Estimate chr1 QTL position (cM) and high-allele founder in 120 8-founder RILs. Audit: sort markers by chr/pos (files are shuffled), check marker ID agreement across files, missing (-1) rates, duplicates, batch effect on y. Method: per-marker single-SNP scan with batch covariate, then founder-haplotype probabilities via simple HMM (8 states, homozygous RILs, founder SNP emission with error) and 7-df haplotype regression LOD scan with batch covariate; permutation threshold; 1.5-LOD interval; founder effects at peak. Change method if batch confounds, if SNP vs haplotype peaks disagree strongly, or if genotype heterozygosity/founder mismatches indicate errors.

sl-test-v2-8444d9e79492.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-8444d9e79492.text: WARNING SIGN: ICE balancing on this 24-bin truncated window gives control O/E of -0.60 vs -0.15 from the GC GLM, while delta is stable (1.87-2.14 across all variants). MEANS: absolute per-condition strengths depend on the normalisation; ICE on a small window is distorted by edge bins and by the loop's own coverage. ACTION: kept the explicit-covariate GLM as primary and report ICE as a sensitivity check.

sl-test-v2-13f5e19bdba3.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-13f5e19bdba3.text: PLAN: Quantities: (1) weighted log OR of case per calibrated segment-B copy in full cohort (n=1900), adjusted for outer-orientation dosage, age, sex, PC1-3; (2) per-gene log expression slope per B copy. Method: define reliable breakpoint calls from QC fields (molecule_count, mapq, entropy, pair_balance, local_complexity), round copy_index_segment_B and 2*bp_alt_fraction to integer dosages in reliable samples; train tag-marker predictors (ridge/regression) of B dosage and outer dosage on reliable panel samples, check out-of-fold accuracy, impute to full cohort; fit logistic regression with inverse sample_fraction weights (design strata clinic x stream x ancestry x age_band x case) and robust SE. Expression: OLS of log_expr on imputed B dosage + outer dosage + tissue, batch, uniqueness, depth, gc, ancestry PCs per gene; pick gene with clear signal. Checks: QC distribution clusters, panel vs cohort overlap, marker collinearity between B and outer, unweighted vs weighted, sensitivity to QC threshold, multimapper confounding. Change method if imputation is poor (then use calibration/regression-calibration) or if QC-failed calls distort the dosage.

sl-test-v2-7e58bd82836a.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-7e58bd82836a.text: WARNING SIGN: phenotype batch effect: batch0 mean y=1.92 (n=52) vs batch1 mean 4.21 (n=68), difference ~2.3 SD-units of within-batch spread. MEANS: batch must be a covariate or it adds noise / confounds if batch correlates with genotype. ACTION: include batch as fixed covariate in all scans; also check batch-genotype association at peak.

sl-test-v2-d97f8a9a9c78.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-d97f8a9a9c78.text: WARNING SIGN: marker rows in all files are in shuffled (non-positional) order; 29 of 220 markers monomorphic among founders; 5.9% genotype missing (-1). MEANS: must sort by chr/pos before HMM; monomorphic markers uninformative. ACTION: sort by position, HMM handles missing as uninformative emission.

sl-test-v2-ea062d4b318d.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-ea062d4b318d.text: WARNING SIGN: gb10 marker rows and npz columns are shuffled across chr1/chr2 (first IDs m2_065, m2_103, m2_107, m2_079). MEANS: file-order HMM is meaningless. ACTION: joined by marker_id/sample_id (sample order matches phenotypes) and sorted by chr,pos_cM before HMM.

sl-test-v2-5dc83cdb4c96.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-5dc83cdb4c96.text: WARNING SIGN: 29 of 220 gb10 markers (19 on chr1) are monomorphic across the 8 founders; -1 is 5% of RIL calls (max 12.5% per marker, 8.6% per RIL). RIL allele freq correlates 0.98 with founder allele freq so 0/1 codes match. MEANS: monomorphic markers carry no haplotype info, -1 should be missing. ACTION: dropped monomorphic markers and treated -1 as missing in the HMM.

sl-test-v2-1d566f64e3d2.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-1d566f64e3d2.text: WARNING SIGN: gb10 phenotype batch effect is large: batch0 mean 1.92 (n=52) vs batch1 mean 4.21 (n=68), about 1 SD. MEANS: batch must be a covariate or it inflates residual and may confound founder effects. ACTION: batch included as additive covariate in null, scan, coefficient fit and permutations.

sl-test-v2-2bc8284fc84a.reason: This decides which dataset each requested quantity is estimated from. Reading the CRISPRi effect of LINC473 guides as transcript-specific would mis-assign a neighbour-gene effect and could flip advance_target.
sl-test-v2-2bc8284fc84a.text: Possible pitfall (from the library's literature review, not yet checked against this data): at a lncRNA locus, dCas9-KRAB CRISPRi silences chromatin over a window that often spreads to a neighbouring or bidirectional-promoter coding gene. A pooled-screen growth effect of LINC473-targeting CRISPRi guides may therefore be partly or wholly caused by concomitant KIN1 repression (a DNA-locus effect) and not by loss of the LINC473 transcript. Check: in the guide-level local expression table, for LINC473-targeting guides compare the KIN1 relative expression with the LINC473 relative expression, quantify how much KIN1 drops when LINC473 is knocked down, and use the guide map's distance-to-neighbour-TSS column to see which guides sit near the KIN1 TSS. If KIN1 is co-repressed: do not read the raw CRISPRi log fold change as the lncRNA-specific effect; base lncrna_specific_lfc on the transcript-directed CasRx data, and estimate neighbor_mediated_lfc from a model of the CRISPRi locus effect that conditions on KIN1 repression. The library reported the file and column names (local_expression.tsv with expr_rel_LINC473 / expr_rel_KIN1, guide_map with dist_neighbor_tss_bp); confirm them against the files. The library's guidance does not cover the single-guide follow-up growth file at all, so that file has had no pitfall review.

sl-test-v2-96c2838c879e.reason: Per-target averaging or single-predictor regression would give a different neighbor_mediated_lfc than a joint dose-response model, and the -0.25 threshold on that quantity enters the advance decision.
sl-test-v2-96c2838c879e.text: Possible pitfall (literature-based, to be checked): CRISPRi guides are not equal-strength perturbations. Knockdown depends strongly on guide distance from the TSS (general expectation: strongest about -50 to +300 bp from the TSS), so guides far from the LINC473 TSS may knock LINC473 down weakly while guides near the KIN1 TSS repress KIN1 strongly. In addition, LINC473 and KIN1 knockdown are likely correlated across guides (shared promoter/chromatin), so a regression of growth on one gene's knockdown alone absorbs the other gene's effect. Check: relate the guide map distances to each TSS (dist_lnc_tss_bp, dist_neighbor_tss_bp as reported by the library) to the measured LINC473 and KIN1 relative expression; compute the across-guide correlation between the two knockdowns and the variance inflation factor of a joint model. If found: model growth as a function of the measured per-guide knockdown rather than averaging per nominal target, and fit one multiple regression with both repression terms, growth ~ (1 - expr_rel_LINC473) + (1 - expr_rel_KIN1), to get partial effects, instead of two separate single-gene regressions. Weak-knockdown guides should inform the slope, not dilute an average. Note a tension in the library's guidance: one source says to report the LINC473 coefficient of this joint CRISPRi model as the lncRNA effect, another says to take the lncRNA-specific effect from the CasRx data. Decide by the task's definitions (lncrna_specific_lfc is a transcript effect, not a local DNA-locus effect; neighbor_mediated_lfc is the KIN1 term in the local-locus model after accounting for LINC473 knockdown), state the choice, and report how well the two LINC473 estimates agree. If the two knockdowns are strongly collinear, report the resulting uncertainty in the split.

sl-test-v2-6d0ba34d4124.reason: lncrna_specific_lfc is defined at 100% knockdown of the dominant transcript; a plain mean over partial-knockdown or off-isoform guides estimates a different quantity, and the -0.08 threshold is close enough to zero that guide selection can change the call.
sl-test-v2-6d0ba34d4124.text: Possible pitfall (literature-based, to be checked): CasRx (Cas13d) guides can cause collateral RNA degradation and can differ in how much of the dominant LINC473 isoform they cover. A guide that only partly overlaps the dominant isoform, or one with collateral activity, gives a misleading transcript-specific growth effect. Check: in the CasRx follow-up table (library reports casrx_followup.tsv with major_isoform_overlap, knockdown_efficiency and growth_lfc per guide), flag low-overlap and low-efficiency guides and look for guides with an anomalously strong growth effect at low knockdown. If found: weight or filter CasRx guides by isoform overlap, model growth_lfc against knockdown_efficiency, and extrapolate to efficiency = 1 to define lncrna_specific_lfc, rather than taking a plain mean over CasRx guides. Fix the filtering rule before looking at how it moves the estimate, and report the estimate with and without the flagged guides.

sl-test-v2-a2755f3d5fcc.reason: The choice of fit changes the magnitude of both extrapolated effects, and both sit against fixed decision thresholds (-0.08 and -0.25).
sl-test-v2-a2755f3d5fcc.text: Possible pitfall (statistical, to be checked): both requested quantities are effects at 100% knockdown, but the data contain only partial knockdowns, and the knockdown measurements themselves (CasRx knockdown_efficiency, local expr_rel values) are noisy. Ordinary least squares of growth on a noisily measured knockdown attenuates the slope (regression dilution), which biases the extrapolated full-knockdown effect toward zero. Check: look at the spread and range of the knockdown values and establish whether each guide has one measurement or replicates (the library states they are single measurements per guide; verify). If measurement error in knockdown is material: consider an errors-in-variables fit (for example Deming or total least squares) for the extrapolation. Director's caveats: an errors-in-variables fit needs a defensible estimate of the measurement-error variance (or variance ratio) and can be unstable with few guides, so report the naive and the corrected estimates side by side, say which is primary and why, and state how the fit behaves at zero knockdown (free or fixed intercept) because that also changes the extrapolated value.

sl-test-v2-34367de3f0f4.reason: Every CRISPRi-based estimate, including the neighbour-mediated effect, rests on these log fold changes; skipping normalisation or matched-control centring shifts all of them.
sl-test-v2-34367de3f0f4.text: Possible pitfall (to be checked): pooled-screen log fold changes are distorted if counts are not normalised and low-count guides are not handled. Raw day10/day0 ratios carry library-size differences between samples, and guides with very low day-0 counts give noisy ratios. Check: in the CRISPRi count table (library reports crispri_counts.tsv with three replicates), compare per-replicate total counts, look for guides with very low day-0 counts (the library suggests about 30 as a rule of thumb; set the cut-off from the observed count distribution), and check replicate concordance. Then apply median or size-factor normalisation, compute log2(day10/day0) per replicate, centre on the matched controls as the task requires, and combine replicates before estimating any effect. Report how many guides were dropped and whether a replicate disagrees with the others.

sl-test-v2-2bfed3f3f214.reason: One off-target guide can dominate a regression fitted on a small number of guides and move either extrapolated effect across its threshold.
sl-test-v2-2bfed3f3f214.text: Possible pitfall (literature-based, to be checked): in CRISPRi non-coding screens a strong growth signal can come from low-specificity or high-GC guides with off-target fitness effects rather than from the intended target. Check: use the guide map's GC-fraction column (guide_gc_frac as reported by the library) and look for individual guides whose CRISPRi log fold change is an outlier relative to other guides with the same nominal target; cross-check against that guide's measured knockdown in the local expression table. A guide with a large growth effect but little measured knockdown of either LINC473 or KIN1 is suspect. If found: remove or down-weight such guides by a rule set in advance, require concordance between knockdown level and phenotype, and show the estimates with and without them.

sl-test-v2-3002d3c4415f.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-3002d3c4415f.text: WARNING SIGN: 297 of 780 breakpoint-panel samples fail QC (local_complexity>0.4: 293; molecule_count<20/mapq<50/entropy>0.25: ~137, nearly the same samples); off-cluster copy_index_segment_B (|x-round(x)|>0.15) is 59% in high-complexity samples vs 6% in clean ones. MEANS: unreliable long-read calls would add noise to calibration and miscount carriers. ACTION: reliable = local_complexity<=0.4 & molecule_count>=20 & mean_mapq>=50 & alignment_entropy<=0.25 & pair_balance>=0.6 (thresholds at gaps in bimodal distributions), n=483; integer B = round(copy index); 195 reliable carriers (B>=1).

sl-test-v2-c01ed8ad438f.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-c01ed8ad438f.text: WARNING SIGN: breakpoint panel has 297 of 780 samples with unreliable calls: 137 with low molecule_count/mapq/high entropy/low pair_balance and 296 with local_complexity>0.35 (160 of them otherwise good); these have mean distance of copy_index_segment_B from nearest integer 0.21-0.25 vs 0.05 in the 483 clean samples. MEANS: unreliable calls give non-integer, noisy dosages and would bias calibration. ACTION: calibration and carrier count use only the 483 samples passing both QC filters; segment-B dosage = rounded copy index (validated by depth_log2_segment_B r=0.97 with clear 0/0.30/0.55 clusters).

sl-test-v2-c4a94a7a2ab1.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-c4a94a7a2ab1.text: WARNING SIGN: among 483 reliable panel samples, integer segment-B copies are strongly associated with outer-orientation dosage round(2*bp_alt_fraction) (B=0: 153/110/25 for outer 0/1/2; B=2: 0/11/11). MEANS: marginal B effect would absorb outer-orientation effect. ACTION: calibrate both B and outer dosage and include both in the clinical and expression models.

sl-test-v2-831c0ced3524.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-831c0ced3524.text: WARNING SIGN: breakpoint panel (780) and expression panel (560 samples, only 42% in breakpoint panel) are subsets of the 1900-person cohort, and cohort is 81% cases with sampling fractions varying ~0.002-0.84 by design strata. MEANS: direct panel analyses are not source-population estimates. ACTION: impute calibrated B dosage from tag markers into the full cohort and use inverse sample_fraction weights for the clinical OR.

sl-test-v2-32a18d9d44d8.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-32a18d9d44d8.text: WARNING SIGN: segment-B dosage and outer-orientation dosage (round(2*bp_alt_fraction)) are correlated but not nested: among clean calls 26 samples carry B with outer dosage 0. MEANS: B and outer dosage must be modelled jointly to separate them. ACTION: include imputed outer dosage as a covariate in clinical and expression models.

sl-test-v2-b5d68fbe6eda.reason: The knockdown fractions are the predictors in the locus model; a biased reference rescales them and therefore rescales the 100%-repression extrapolation.
sl-test-v2-b5d68fbe6eda.text: Possible pitfall (to be checked): local expression is reported relative to reference genes (the library reports RPLP0 and HPRT1 columns in local_expression.tsv). If a reference gene is itself shifted by the locus knockdown or by growth selection, every relative-expression value, and so every knockdown fraction, is biased. Check: confirm that the RPLP0 and HPRT1 relative-expression values stay near 1 across guides with no systematic shift (for example with knockdown strength or between targeting and control guides), and that the two references agree with each other. If one is unstable: derive the LINC473 and KIN1 knockdown fractions using only the stable reference, or a geometric mean of the stable references, and say what was done.

sl-test-v2-ff3c191fafd2.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-ff3c191fafd2.text: PLAN: estimate direct log-odds effect per +1 SD log10 conc of PROTA and PROTB on disease, conditional on each other. Method: harmonise alleles to variant_metadata coding across all files; select instruments by phase-1 p-value (union for either protein), LD-prune with signed R (r2<0.1/0.2/0.3), use phase-2 betas for SNP-protein effects (three-sample, avoid winner's curse); multivariable GLS theta=(Bx'S^-1Bx)^-1Bx'S^-1by with S=diag(se)R diag(se); rescale by within-batch SD of log10 concentration after QC of protein_measurements. Checks: allele mismatches, phase1 vs phase2 shrinkage, LD matrix PSD/condition number, z-vs-LD consistency, conditional F, Cochran Q (random-effects SE if overdispersed), batch ANOVA, CV-based technical SD sensitivity, pruning-threshold and PCA sensitivity. Change method if: conditional F<10 (use robust/union instruments), Q large (RE SEs, outliers), estimates unstable across pruning (prefer conservative).

sl-test-v2-56b42a380e00.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-56b42a380e00.text: PLAN: Estimate DRX1 carrier frequency per ancestry among screening-roster adults (primary: family_history_tier 0 screening rows; cohort is all collection=screening but includes tier-1 rows 58 AFR/35 EUR), assay-corrected via calibration controls. Method: build per-target calling rules (VAF het window, depth, paralog/MAPQ filter for SNVs; batch-recentred log2_ratio for T02 deletion) tuned on calibration_controls by class and batch; derive class/batch sensitivity and false-positive rate; call carriers per person collapsing cis T03+T04; Rogan-Gladen correct per class per ancestry; DR_AFR from AFR class mix x sensitivity; residual = CF(1-DR)/(1-CF*DR); partner term = row-average over partner_roster strata (tested partners use their assay result corrected by PPV/NPV, untested use stratum prior by ancestry x tier); couple = residual x partner x 1/4. Checks: duplicates, no-calls, VAF hist by target/batch, paralog clusters, log2 batch shift, phase, class mix by ancestry. Change method if thresholds give poor control performance or tier-1 inclusion question changes estimand.

sl-test-v2-9b72695b7173.label: gb04 result
sl-test-v2-9b72695b7173.text: RESULT gb04: WF HMM with Ne schedule and asymmetric error (C->T 0.31, T->C 0.01) gives derived-C allele s_hat=0.096 at locus A (95% CI ~0.04-0.165, LRT 11.2 vs s=0) and 0.025 at locus B (LRT 1.3, n.s.). Symmetric 0.16 error fits worse (LL -34.1 vs -30.1) and biases s down to 0.06; ignoring polarization would flip the sign.

sl-test-v2-d1d54ea14727.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-d1d54ea14727.text: WARNING SIGN: segment-B frequency differs by ancestry in reliable panel (mean copies EUR 0.56, EAS 0.39, AFR 0.29) and marker calibration CV R2 is lower in AFR (0.81 vs 0.92 EUR, 0.91 EAS); outer dosage tagged by interval_1 markers (r~0.9), B by interval_2 markers (r~0.65-0.69). MEANS: ancestry confounding possible; tagging somewhat weaker in AFR but concordance after rounding still 100%. ACTION: ridge calibration on all 60 markers + PCs + ancestry for B and outer separately (CV R2 0.906 / 0.958); clinical model adjusts pc1-3 and ancestry_group; AFR flagged.

sl-test-v2-a66bacdcd678.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-a66bacdcd678.text: WARNING SIGN: Per-cell ambient subtraction clipped at zero gives beta -0.244, but donor-level unclipped subtraction gives -0.305 and putting the ambient expectation in the Poisson mean gives -0.288; ambient is 60-82% of activated-cell CXCL10 in high-rho g=2 donors. MEANS: clipping adds positive bias where ambient dominates, attenuating beta. ACTION: final estimate uses donor-level unclipped subtraction / ambient-in-model (~-0.30).

sl-test-v2-9bfc8ff848d4.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-9bfc8ff848d4.text: WARNING SIGN: Within g=1, the 4 high-rho donors (rho~0.29-0.30) have corrected activated CXCL10 rates ~0.011-0.023 vs ~0.005-0.011 in the 4 low-rho donors; Poisson chi2/df=18. MEANS: possible residual ambient or batch effect nearly collinear with genotype; adding rho as covariate moves beta to -0.44. ACTION: kept g-only NB model (batch is collinear with g, rho already modeled via subtraction), reported as main uncertainty.

sl-test-v2-841b7617c003.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-841b7617c003.text: WARNING SIGN: outgroup allele = alt (T) at both loci; alt frequency FALLS at locus A (0.90 -> 0.33) and only mildly at B (0.75 -> 0.58). MEANS: derived allele is ref C; locus A's derived allele rises strongly. ACTION: modelled derived freq = 1 - alt freq at both loci (polarisation by parsimony assumed correct).

sl-test-v2-8b1811b805bf.label: RESULT
sl-test-v2-8b1811b805bf.text: RESULT gb06: per-allele log rate ratio of CXCL10 in activated monocytes ~ -0.30 (SE ~0.06-0.09) after donor-specific HBB-based ambient correction, ISG (IFI6+ISG15) GMM gate, donor pseudobulk NB GLM; uncorrected estimate is ~0. Activated fraction rises strongly with g (0.27,0.52,0.82; logit slope 1.19).

sl-test-v2-6447fff2c843.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-6447fff2c843.text: WARNING SIGN: under the asymmetric aDNA-damage error model (C->T 0.31, T->C 0.01) locus A deterministic fit has a piecewise-s improvement with breakpoint at gen 26 (s1=0.15, s2=0.05, LRT=5.3, 1 extra df, but breakpoint chosen post hoc among 3 candidates); late derived freq ~0.97 is near fixation. MEANS: modest evidence of deceleration, partly saturation and drift in N=100-130 epochs. ACTION: kept constant-s WF HMM estimate (s=0.095, CI 0.04-0.165) because the CI covers both piecewise values and post-hoc breakpoint is not significant after multiple-testing; reported as sensitivity.

sl-test-v2-b7c8c16ac7d6.label: gb04 result
sl-test-v2-b7c8c16ac7d6.text: gb04 result (team-a): haploid WF HMM with Ne schedule and asymmetric C->T damage error (0.31/0.01) gives derived-allele (ref C) s_A=0.095 (95% profile CI 0.040-0.165, LRT vs 0 = 11.3) and s_B=0.025 (CI -0.015-0.065, LRT 1.3). Asymmetric model fits A much better than symmetric 0.16 (logL -30.0 vs -34.1). Symmetric 0.01 gives s_A=0.045, biased low.

sl-test-v2-ac1ff4e92990.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-ac1ff4e92990.text: WARNING SIGN: Activated-cell CXCL10 beta is very sensitive to ambient handling: raw -0.01, ambient-subtracted (HBB-based rho, empty-drop profile) -0.365, ambient scale s=1.5 gives -0.82; fitting s freely on activated cells only gives s=1.26 (beta -0.58, not significant), but a joint fit over activated+resting clusters gives s=0.98 (beta -0.35). MEANS: the ambient model is the crux; the empty-drop profile is validated by the joint fit. ACTION: report s=1 mixture-model estimate ~-0.36 (donor bootstrap 95% CI -0.53 to -0.23).

sl-test-v2-1f076fbb4c0d.label: gb06 result
sl-test-v2-1f076fbb4c0d.text: gb06 result: per-allele log rate ratio of CXCL10 in activated (ISG-high/LST1-low) monocytes is about -0.36 after removing HBB-tracked ambient RNA (empty-drop profile HBB 7.0%, CXCL10 4.9%); raw uncorrected estimate is ~0 because high-contamination donors are concentrated in g=2. Resting-cluster beta is about +0.5.

sl-test-v2-769aaad0efe8.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-769aaad0efe8.text: PLAN: Estimate DRX1 carrier frequencies (AFR, EUR screening roster), AFR residual risk after negative screen, partner carrier frequency for full partner roster, and couple risk = residual_AFR_neg * partner_freq * 1/4. Method: use calibration controls (truth reference_category by ancestry and batch) to build per-target calling rules (VAF/alt reads for sequence targets, log2_ratio/split reads for CNV target, QC on mapq/paralog/segdup, phase for class_03 two-site target), estimate sensitivity/specificity per ancestry x batch, call screening samples, correct observed positive rate for sens/spec (Rogan-Gladen), residual = f(1-sens)/(1-f*sens - (1-f)(1-spec)... ). Partner: only 179/500 tested, testing depends on family history tier, so estimate stratum (ancestry x FH tier) frequencies and reweight to full roster. Checks: duplicates, id linkage, batch effects, ancestry-specific calibration, class_03 cis/trans phase, missingness. Change method if calibration shows batch/ancestry-dependent performance or if per-target rules fail.

sl-test-v2-ecc17cca72e2.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-ecc17cca72e2.text: PLAN: Estimate direct log-odds effect per +1 SD log10 concentration for PROTA and PROTB conditional on each other via multivariable MR (LD-aware GLS IVW, Sigma = diag(seY) R diag(seY)) using 80-SNP locus. Exposure betas from phase2 holdout (allele-harmonised to variant_metadata), instrument selection by phase1 p-values (p<5e-8 for either protein), to avoid winner's curse. Rescale per-log10 to per-SD using within-batch SD from QC-passing batches (exclude high-CV batch_3, dedupe). Checks: allele harmonisation, phase1 beta vs p consistency, residual/outlier (pleiotropy) diagnostics with Cochran Q, conditional F, sensitivity to selection threshold, LD pruning, SD choice. Change method if heterogeneity large (robust/outlier removal) or if results shift a lot with threshold.

sl-test-v2-fa127d46d628.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-fa127d46d628.text: WARNING SIGN: phase1 protein betas are ~1.6x larger than implied by their own p-values for all SNPs with |z|>~5 (e.g. rs200024 PROTA beta/se=58.5 vs p-implied z=36.6), while phase2 z matches p exactly and scales as sqrt(8000/12000) of p-implied phase1 z. MEANS: phase1 betas are inflated (winner's curse/selection-biased screening estimates). ACTION: use phase1 only for instrument selection; take exposure betas from phase2 holdout.

sl-test-v2-7e84df772290.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-7e84df772290.text: WARNING SIGN: 19 of 80 SNPs in protein_PROTA_phase2 and protein_PROTB_phase2 report the opposite effect allele vs variant_metadata/disease file (clean swaps, e.g. rs200024 T/G). MEANS: unharmonised betas would flip sign for those instruments. ACTION: flip phase2 beta sign for swapped SNPs before MR.

sl-test-v2-5b8241349b29.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-5b8241349b29.text: WARNING SIGN: protein_measurements batch_3 has control_cv 0.314 vs 0.082/0.089 and SD 0.637 (PROTA) / 0.496 (PROTB) vs ~0.25/0.20 in batches 1-2; batch means also differ (PROTA 1.99 vs 2.50); one exact duplicate row. MEANS: pooled SD (0.47/0.37) is inflated by batch shifts and the failed batch, which would bias per-SD scaling. ACTION: SD = pooled within-batch SD of batches 1-2 after dedup.

sl-test-v2-1e144eaab50f.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-1e144eaab50f.text: WARNING SIGN: protein phase-2 files (PROTA and PROTB) have 19/80 SNPs with effect/other allele swapped vs variant_metadata, phase1 and disease files (e.g. rs200000 effect C). MEANS: raw phase-2 betas for those SNPs have the wrong sign. ACTION: flip beta sign for those 19 SNPs in phase 2 before any comparison/MR.

sl-test-v2-503611337d32.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-503611337d32.text: WARNING SIGN: disease association has strong signals with no protein association (rs200066-rs200069, disease z up to 47) and rs200027/rs200028 disease z 39.5/65.6 above neighbours. MEANS: independent pleiotropic/other-gene disease signal in the locus; including those SNPs would bias GLS MR. ACTION: restrict to protein instruments and check residual outliers; remove those with large standardized residuals.

sl-test-v2-87935d8f32f0.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-87935d8f32f0.text: WARNING SIGN: protein_measurements batch_3 has control_cv 0.314 (vs 0.082/0.089 in batches 1-2) and SD of log10 conc 0.64 (PROTA) / 0.50 (PROTB) vs ~0.25/~0.20 in batches 1-2; batch means differ (ANOVA p~1e-71/1e-80); pooled SD 0.470/0.373. MEANS: pooled SD is inflated by batch shifts and a failed high-noise batch. ACTION: exclude batch_3 as QC failure and use pooled within-batch SD from batches 1-2; report sensitivity.

sl-test-v2-69a93d10619f.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-69a93d10619f.text: WARNING SIGN: clinical log OR per imputed segment-B copy is -0.267 (SE 0.20) with inverse sampling-fraction weights but +0.111 unweighted; cohort is 81% cases with case sampling fractions up to 0.84 vs control fractions down to 0.002. MEANS: ascertainment by clinic/stream/ancestry/age/case distorts the estimate; source-population target requires design weights. ACTION: use weighted logistic (weights 1/sample_fraction, robust SE) as primary.

sl-test-v2-ae33a9a50424.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-ae33a9a50424.text: WARNING SIGN: GENE1 has mean multimapper_fraction 0.38 (others 0.05-0.11) and shows a B-copy slope 0.44; GENE2 (unique 0.93) slope 0.32; GENE4 tracks outer dosage (0.42) not B. MEANS: GENE1 signal may be a multimapping/paralog read artifact of extra copies rather than true expression. ACTION: test whether GENE1 slope depends on multimapper/unique fraction before choosing the supported gene.

sl-test-v2-b85b6612226d.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-b85b6612226d.text: WARNING SIGN: gb05 clinical log OR per calibrated segment-B copy changes sign under sampling weights: unweighted (B+outer+age,sex,PCs,ancestry) +0.114 vs IPW (w=1/sample_fraction, all 1900 rows matched exactly one design cell) -0.286 (SE 0.19); without the outer term IPW B is -0.126; cohort case fraction 0.81 vs weighted source prevalence 0.32. MEANS: outcome- and stratum-dependent sampling biases the unweighted OR beyond the intercept, and outer orientation confounds B. ACTION: report IPW model with both B and outer dosage, sandwich SE; B rescaled by CV calibration slope 1.045 gives -0.274.

sl-test-v2-18f686f57557.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-18f686f57557.text: WARNING SIGN: gb05 IPW per-ancestry B log OR is heterogeneous: EUR +0.31 (SE 0.28), AFR -0.31 (0.43), EAS -1.06 (0.31). MEANS: possible effect heterogeneity or ancestry-specific tagging; pooled estimate is a population average. ACTION: kept pooled ancestry-adjusted IPW estimate as the source-population total effect, flagged as weakest point.

sl-test-v2-4bb7a8d3b08e.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-4bb7a8d3b08e.text: PLAN: Estimate (1) lncrna_specific_lfc = growth at 100% knockdown of dominant LINC473 isoform, from CasRx data by regressing growth_lfc on effective dominant-isoform knockdown (knockdown_efficiency*major_isoform_overlap) with plate terms, checking plate confounding; (2) neighbor_mediated_lfc = KIN1 coefficient from regressing CRISPRi screen guide LFC (day10/day0, depth-normalized, centered on matched NTCs) on LINC473 and KIN1 knockdown (1-expr_rel) across targeting guides. Checks: NTC GC-content bias (match controls by GC), replicate concordance, housekeeping expression, plate effects in follow-up vs screen, collinearity of LINC473/KIN1 knockdown. Change method if GC or plate batch effects bias the estimates.

sl-test-v2-07e7ca1eb968.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-07e7ca1eb968.text: WARNING SIGN: gb10 chr1 markers m1_056 (51.4 cM) and m1_058 (53.2 cM) have about 16-18% RIL-vs-HMM mismatch and their founders.tsv alleles are opposite to the RIL alleles for all 8 founders (allele coding flipped for those markers), distorting the haplotypes from 47 to 54 cM, right next to the first chr1 peak (45 cM). MEANS: the founder-genotype errors corrupt the probabilities near the QTL. ACTION: drop both markers (after dropping them, the leave-one-out founder concordance is clean everywhere else); then rerun everything.

sl-test-v2-272165d51788.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-272165d51788.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that the two anchor bins (8 and 17) have unusually high gc_content compared with the other bins, and that contact counts depend on GC in every replicate. Check whether that holds in your data, and whether any dependence of your balanced values on the GC of the two bins remains after ICE (for example among the diagonal-9 pixels you average for the expected). Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-59aeb2af19e5.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-59aeb2af19e5.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team observed that ICE balancing on this truncated 24-bin window can be distorted by edge bins (which see only part of their contacts) and by the loop pixel's own contribution to the coverage of bins 8 and 17. Check in your data how the balancing weights of bins 8 and 17 and of the edge bins compare with the rest, and whether those weights change if the target pixel is left out of the balancing. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-af905541c494.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-af905541c494.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team left the target pixel (8,17) out of the data used to build the expected, whereas your primary expected is the diagonal-9 mean with that pixel included among only 11 valid pixels. You recorded that your result moves when the target is left out. Check how much of the diagonal-9 mean in each replicate comes from the target pixel itself, and state which definition of 'expected' you judge the task to mean and why. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-9c4e58399789.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-9c4e58399789.text: WARNING SIGN: In calibration controls, T02 (exon10-11 deletion) calls with log2<-0.3 occur in 68/720 'none' controls; 39 of these have segmental_dup_score>0.75 while all true class_02 deletions have segdup<0.5. MEANS: high segdup score marks paralog-driven false deletion calls. ACTION: T02 calls with segdup>=0.6 are treated as negative, and the remaining false-positive rate is estimated from controls and corrected for.

sl-test-v2-307194fe84d6.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-307194fe84d6.text: PLAN: lncrna_specific_lfc from CasRx: use only high major_isoform_overlap guides (dominant-isoform targeting), regress growth_lfc on knockdown_efficiency and extrapolate to efficiency=1; report naive and errors-in-variables. neighbor_mediated_lfc from a joint CRISPRi multiple regression of matched-control-centered log2(day10/day0) on knockdown fractions (1-expr_rel_LINC473) and (1-expr_rel_KIN1) over locus guides, take the KIN1 coefficient (effect at 100% KIN1 repression after accounting for LINC473). Checks: library-size normalize counts, drop low day0 guides, NTC centering, reference-gene stability (RPLP0/HPRT1 ~1), TSS-distance vs knockdown, collinearity/VIF of the two knockdowns, flag low-overlap/collateral CasRx guides and high-GC off-target CRISPRi guides. Change method if references unstable or if collinearity makes the split undefined.

sl-test-v2-87c8a361b1ee.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-87c8a361b1ee.text: WARNING SIGN: T02 deletion sensitivity differs by ancestry: 142/300 AFR vs 248/300 EUR true class_02 controls have log2<-0.3 (AFR mean log2 -0.25 vs EUR -0.45). MEANS: the screen misses about half of AFR deletion carriers, so the naive positive rate underestimates AFR carrier frequency and residual risk after a negative screen is high. ACTION: use ancestry-specific (and batch-specific) calibration matrices and a misclassification-corrected EM estimate.

sl-test-v2-64b19f71b79a.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-64b19f71b79a.text: WARNING SIGN: Allele dropout at sequence sites: 40/260 AFR and 26/260 EUR class_01 controls show VAF<0.05 at T01, and 59/480 class_03 controls are het at only one of T03/T04. Also 36 'none' controls are het at both T03 and T04, but T04 has phase_set PS2 (a different phase set). MEANS: sensitivity is below 1. Class_03 is called if either site is het, unless both are het in different phase sets. ACTION: encode this rule and correct for its sensitivity.

sl-test-v2-5eb82308a208.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-5eb82308a208.text: WARNING SIGN: Batch confounding: every screening cohort sample is on lot_A17 and every partner sample is on lot_C42; controls are balanced across both lots. MEANS: calibration must match each lot (e.g. AFR class_01 VAF is lower in C42). ACTION: use batch x ancestry calibration matrices.

sl-test-v2-ce7dbc8c873e.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-ce7dbc8c873e.text: WARNING SIGN: Only 179/500 partners have assay data (testing_status completed), and completion depends strongly on family_history_tier (FH1 84/100 completed vs FH0 95/400). MEANS: the carrier rate among tested partners is biased toward FH1 if carrier rate differs by tier. ACTION: estimate carrier frequency per ancestry x FH stratum and reweight to full-roster stratum counts (MAR given ancestry and FH).

sl-test-v2-09f2a95cfb4b.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-09f2a95cfb4b.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that only 11 valid pixels remain on diagonal 9 once bins 10 and 11 are masked, that the result moves with how the diagonal-9 expected is defined (mean, median, target left out, smoothed across distances), that the distance-decay slope differs between case and control, and that control replicates have zero pixels at long range. Check whether these hold in your data, how many pixels actually determine the distance-9 factor in your GLM, and whether the long-range zeros or the differing decay affect the fit. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-f721e45c60f4.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-f721e45c60f4.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team corrected per-bin bias by balancing each replicate rather than with a single covariate, and found that bin coverage is strongly related to mappability, driven by bins 10 and 11. Your GC effect is one linear coefficient shared across all distances and fit on about 250 pixels. Check whether that coefficient is stable when it is estimated without the influence of particular bins (for example the edge bins or bins neighbouring 10 and 11), whether it is separable from mappability and re_sites in these 24 bins, and whether residual per-bin bias remains at bins 8 and 17 after your model. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-017da1f8c318.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-017da1f8c318.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team used two cross-checks you did not record: a local (donut) background around pixel (8,17) to tell a focal loop from broader domain enrichment, and the 40 kb pixel covering the same coordinates as a consistency check on the 20 kb estimate. Check whether your expected and your per-condition values are consistent with those two views in your data. Also state whether you judge that the task's 'expected' should include or exclude the target pixel, and why. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-1f71e70b3a5c.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-1f71e70b3a5c.text: WARNING SIGN: chr1 QTL is weak (8-founder haplotype LOD 4.27 at 45.7cM vs genome-wide 95% permutation threshold 5.05; 5.4 after adding the chr2 peak as covariate) and high founder unstable: effects F4 +1.18, F5 +1.17, F2 +1.12 (centered); bootstrap top founder F2 85/200, F4 70/200; bootstrap peak IQR 36.7-46.8cM. MEANS: position ~43-46cM is fairly consistent but founder identity among F2/F4/F5 is not resolved. ACTION: report F4 (top in base, chr2-adjusted, outlier-dropped models and single-founder contrast LOD 1.48 vs F2 0.77), with low confidence.

sl-test-v2-b8be37417c08.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-b8be37417c08.text: WARNING SIGN: phenotype outlier RIL076 y=-3.59 (batch 0, next lowest -1.01); dropping it moves the chr1 peak from 45.7 to 43.3cM and raises LOD from 4.27 to 5.22. MEANS: one point has a moderate influence. ACTION: ran a sensitivity check; F4 stays top; report 44.5cM, between the two peaks.

sl-test-v2-4ff1a6d50484.label: gb10 result
sl-test-v2-4ff1a6d50484.text: gb10 chr1 QTL (team-b): HMM founder-probability scan with batch covariate puts the peak at 43-46cM (report 44.5); best high-allele founder F4, with F2 and F5 nearly tied; signal is marginal relative to the permutation threshold.

sl-test-v2-06d90f4ab380.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-06d90f4ab380.text: WARNING SIGN: in the expression panel, mean imputed segment-B dosage differs by tissue_source (tissue_A 0.22, tissue_B 0.68, tissue_C 0.47) and GENE2 baseline expression differs by tissue; GENE2 slope is ~0.40 within batch without tissue adjustment vs 0.32 with. MEANS: tissue confounds the expression-dosage association. ACTION: adjust for tissue_source and expr_batch (plus technical covariates); GENE2 slope stable 0.30-0.32 across adjusted specifications.

sl-test-v2-3bb11b4c5128.label: RESULT
sl-test-v2-3bb11b4c5128.text: Result gb05 Locus Q: 483 reliable breakpoint calls, 195 segment-B carriers; full-cohort design-weighted log OR per imputed B copy = -0.267 (robust SE 0.20, bootstrap 95% CI -0.63 to 0.15) adjusted for outer dosage, age, sex, PCs; GENE2 (cleanly mapped) log fold-change 0.321 per B copy; GENE1 B signal judged multimapping artifact (its multimapper fraction rises with B, r=0.38).

sl-test-v2-416745a755a0.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-416745a755a0.text: WARNING SIGN: gb05 expression: GENE1 (mean multimapper_fraction 0.38) has multimapper_fraction rising with calibrated B (slope 0.028, p=4e-13) and its B slope drifts 0.58 crude -> 0.44 after tech adjustment, with B x multimapper interaction 0.39; GENE4 B effect vanishes once outer dosage is added (0.35 -> 0.09 -> 0.01), so it is an outer-orientation gene; tissue_source is correlated with B (mean pB tissue_A 0.21, tissue_B 0.69); log_expr differs by case (GENE2 +0.17, p=6e-6). MEANS: GENE1 signal is partly a mapping artefact, GENE4 is outer-driven, and tissue and case confound expression. ACTION: chose GENE2 (unique reads, multimapper unrelated to B) as the supported gene; slope from OLS of log_expr on B+outer+case+age+sex+PCs+ancestry+tissue+batch+depth+gc+multimapper = 0.308 (SE 0.012), stable across 0.286 IPW to 0.313 true-B subset.

sl-test-v2-e8c09062152e.label: gb05 result
sl-test-v2-e8c09062152e.text: gb05 result (team-a): 195 reliable breakpoint-panel carriers of >=1 segment-B copy (483 reliable of 780); IPW source-population log OR per calibrated B copy adjusted for outer dosage, age, sex, PCs, ancestry = -0.274 (SE ~0.19, calibration-slope rescaled; -0.286 unrescaled); GENE2 expression log FC per B copy = 0.308; target_support_code = 1.

sl-test-v2-e4833e8b2338.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-e4833e8b2338.text: WARNING SIGN: at the gb10 chr1 peak (45 cM) the top fixed-effect founder F5 has only 7.4 expected lines (6 hard-called) with SE 0.77; F4 (14.5 lines) and F2 are close behind (F5 4.03, F4 3.32, F2 2.97, batch-adjusted). Under ridge shrinkage the top founder flips from F5 to F4 at moderate-strong shrinkage, and F5 lines are batch-imbalanced (33% batch1 vs 64% overall). MEANS: the founder call depends on rare-founder noise and on batch adjustment. ACTION: estimate the shrinkage by ML (BLUP), check founder SNP sharing at the locus, and report F2/F4/F5 grouping and uncertainty.

sl-test-v2-1b292d466afd.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-1b292d466afd.text: WARNING SIGN: 3 of 14 NTC guides (g067,g068,g069) have screen LFC -0.24 to -0.43 vs +0.21..+0.40 for the other 11; 2 ANKRD42 guides (g055,g061) are similarly depleted; 5 targeting guides with strong measured knockdown (g003,g008,g015,g040,g050) grow like NTCs (+0.23..+0.30). Replicates agree (r>0.98) so it is not count noise. MEANS: guide-level outliers (likely toxic/off-target or mislabelled guides) would bias a naive NTC mean and OLS. ACTION: centre on clean-NTC median and use robust (Huber) regression plus an explicit outlier-excluded fit; compare.

sl-test-v2-c88b839e5a79.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-c88b839e5a79.text: WARNING SIGN: guide GC content shifts screen LFC: clean high-GC NTCs median ~+0.27 vs low-GC NTCs ~+0.34; ANKRD42 high-GC ~+0.24 vs low-GC ~+0.33 (≈-0.08 per high-GC). The LINC473 distal guides (g027-g036) are all low GC while proximal LINC473 and KIN1 guides are high GC. MEANS: matched-control comparison must be GC-matched or the LINC473-only signal is confounded with GC. ACTION: include guide_gc_frac as covariate, fitted using NTC and ANKRD42 (no local knockdown) guides.

sl-test-v2-217fe10aab03.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-217fe10aab03.text: WARNING SIGN: CasRx plate C guides with tiny major-isoform overlap (0.03-0.14) show growth -0.07..-0.18, scaling with knockdown_efficiency, as strong as plate A guides with overlap ~0.95. Plate is fully confounded with overlap class. MEANS: growth tracks a plate/off-target or total-knockdown effect, not dominant-isoform knockdown; naive pooled regression on kd is biased. ACTION: model growth ~ kd*overlap (effective dominant-isoform kd) + kd*(1-overlap) + plate terms and compare specifications.

sl-test-v2-0a58b6d155d7.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-0a58b6d155d7.text: WARNING SIGN: after harmonisation, phase-2 protein betas are ~0.60 (PROTA) and ~0.63 (PROTB) of phase-1 betas, and the ratio is the same for SNPs with phase-1 z>30 as for z 6-15 (corr of betas 0.99).
