MEANS: phase-1 betas are systematically inflated (winner's-curse-like / scale inflation, not only selection noise), so using phase-1 betas shrinks theta (~0.17/0.28 per SD vs ~0.25/0.41 with phase 2). ACTION: select instruments on phase 1, take SNP-protein betas from phase 2 only.

sl-test-v2-2cf98c2aa088.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-2cf98c2aa088.text: WARNING SIGN: In calibration 'none' controls, 36/720 (5%) show both DRX1_T03 and T04 heterozygous (VAF~0.49) but always on different phase sets (T03 PS1, T04 PS2), whereas all 362 class_03 control pairs are cis (PS1/PS1); screening cohort has 41 such PS2 pairs and 16 cis pairs. MEANS: a T03+T04 trans/unphased pair is not a class_03 carrier allele per the controls; counting it would inflate class_03 frequency. ACTION: call class_03 positive only if T03 and/or T04 positive on the same phase set (cis or singleton); PS-discordant pairs called negative; specificity then re-estimated on controls.

sl-test-v2-fcdb0e5e4d86.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-fcdb0e5e4d86.text: WARNING SIGN: multivariable GLS shows huge heterogeneity (Q=3462 on 9 df for r2<0.1 pruned set; Q=9207/73 df for PCA fit); disease z at rs200068 is 47 with near-zero PROTA/PROTB effects, and rs200028 disease z 65.6 exceeds what proteins predict. MEANS: extra disease-causal (pleiotropic, protein-independent) variants in the locus bias theta and make fixed-effect SEs meaningless. ACTION: model the pleiotropic signals explicitly (stepwise add LD-propagated direct-effect columns R[:,j]) in an all-SNP LD-aware GLS until Q is consistent with df, and cross-check with pruned sets excluding outliers.

sl-test-v2-b4acdbb1d4e4.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-b4acdbb1d4e4.text: WARNING SIGN: DRX1_T02 deletion calls (log2<-0.3, always with split_reads>=4) occur in 68/720 'none' controls; 39 of them have segmental_dup_score>0.6 while all 390 true class_02 deletions have segdup<=0.461; screening cohort has 42 deletion calls with segdup>0.6. MEANS: segmental-duplication artifact mimicking the exon10-11 loss. ACTION: require segdup<0.55 for a deletion call; residual 29/720 (~4%) false positives remain indistinguishable, so Rogan-Gladen correct with that specificity.

sl-test-v2-12a3327af75f.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-12a3327af75f.text: WARNING SIGN: Deletion (class_02) sensitivity differs sharply by ancestry: AFR controls 52% (lot_A17) / 43% (lot_C42) vs EUR 85% / 80%; class_01 sensitivity also lower in lot_C42 (~78-85%) vs lot_A17 (~91-94%). No log2 batch shift (medians ~0 in both lots), no low-VAF paralog cluster. MEANS: detection rate must be ancestry- and batch-specific; screening cohort is all lot_A17 and partners all lot_C42. ACTION: use ancestry x batch x class sensitivities from controls.

sl-test-v2-74ac0bcd0ce9.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-74ac0bcd0ce9.text: WARNING SIGN: The partner positive-call rate differs a lot by intake_site x collection_wave: site_A wave_2 1/39 vs site_B wave_2 20/57 and site_A wave_1 7/25. Testing completion also depends on site x wave x FH: site_B is 100% tested, but site_A wave_1 FH0 has only 14/280 tested. MEANS: reweighting by ancestry x FH alone is not enough, because missingness is tied to site/wave strata that have different carrier rates. ACTION: reweight partner carrier estimates by site x wave x FH (x ancestry) strata, using per-sample ancestry-specific calibration in a stratified EM.

sl-test-v2-69fb198601c6.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-69fb198601c6.text: WARNING SIGN: gb10 genome-wide permutation threshold (1000 perms, batch kept with phenotype, chr1+chr2, 8-founder HK) is 5.23 at 5%; chr1 peak LOD 5.18 (p about 0.06), 5.46 with chr2 covariate; chr2 LOD is about 4.5-5.3 along the whole chromosome (1.5-LOD interval 0-100 cM). MEANS: the chr1 QTL is only borderline significant, and the chr2 signal looks diffuse/polygenic rather than one locus. ACTION: kept the 45 cM peak (stable under LMM, covariates, eps, INT); ran an LMM with chr2 kinship as the main structure control; present the chr2 covariate as a sensitivity check.

sl-test-v2-bdc966671f96.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-bdc966671f96.text: WARNING SIGN: family_history_tier 1 screening rows (58 AFR, 35 EUR) have ~2x the screen-positive rate (AFR 19% vs 10%, EUR 20% vs 8.5%); corrected CF tier0 AFR 0.081/EUR 0.065 vs tier1 0.20/0.19. MEANS: pooling tiers inflates the population CF (AFR all-tier 0.099). ACTION: CF estimand = tier 0 screening rows; tier-specific CFs used as priors for partner strata.

sl-test-v2-7739a19a4869.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-7739a19a4869.text: WARNING SIGN: Tested partners (lot_C42) screen positive more often than cohort (AFR tier0 8/45=18% vs 10%). MEANS: tested partners may be selected, or small-sample noise; stratum priors drawn from cohort may understate partner risk for tested rows. ACTION: tested rows use their own assay result (PPV/NPV with lot_C42 Se/FP), so selection only affects the prior; untested rows use cohort tier-matched CF.

sl-test-v2-a7f6a0181ef4.label: RESULT
sl-test-v2-a7f6a0181ef4.text: RESULT gb07: tier0 CF AFR 0.0808, EUR 0.0654; AFR DR 0.68 (deletion Se 0.52), AFR negative residual 0.0289; partner roster row-mean carrier prob 0.131; couple risk 0.00095.

sl-test-v2-2bbba9298b16.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-2bbba9298b16.text: WARNING SIGN: CasRx dominant-isoform coefficient moves a lot with specification: -0.006 (eff only), -0.158 (eff+off-isoform, no plate), -0.048 (with plate), -0.090 (no intercept). MEANS: plate is confounded with isoform overlap and an off-isoform/collateral term (-0.31 per unit non-dominant kd) dominates; the estimate is only identified with an external plate calibration. ACTION: fixed plate offsets from the guide_followup plates (A -0.048, B -0.015, C +0.012; slope 0.971 vs screen, which reproduce the CasRx plate offsets exactly) and refit: dominant-isoform effect -0.050 (se 0.005), stable under leave-one-plate-out (-0.049 to -0.051). Kept intercept (-0.027, se 0.003) as a nonspecific CasRx term.

sl-test-v2-82a6574c4872.label: gb08 result
sl-test-v2-82a6574c4872.text: gb08 result: in the CRISPRi screen (centred on clean NTC median, GC covariate, 10 outlier guides removed) the KIN1 knockdown coefficient is about -0.75 and the LINC473 transcript knockdown coefficient is about +0.05 (null). CasRx with plate calibration from guide_followup gives a dominant-LINC473-isoform effect of about -0.05. advance_target=0.

sl-test-v2-58d6708a3bff.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-58d6708a3bff.text: WARNING SIGN: on the final 47-SNP set (excluding SNPs with r2>=0.05 to protein-independent disease peaks rs200028, rs200050, rs200068) the LD-aware conditional F is 14.2 for PROTA and 9.4 for PROTB (bx correlation 0.25). MEANS: PROTB is borderline weak conditional on PROTA, so its estimate has more variance and possible weak-instrument bias. ACTION: used second-order weights (include phase-2 bx SE in the covariance), giving theta_A=0.293 (SE 0.021) and theta_B=0.209 (SE 0.027) per SD with Q=49 on 45 df; I report PROTB as the less certain estimate.

sl-test-v2-0ac14f2cf8b4.label: gb09 result
sl-test-v2-0ac14f2cf8b4.text: Result gb09 team-a: direct log-odds per within-batch SD (batches 1-2; SD_A=0.2527, SD_B=0.2017 log10 units) were theta_PROTA=0.293 and theta_PROTB=0.209, from multivariable LD-aware GLS using phase-2 harmonised betas, after excluding SNPs in LD (r2>=0.05) with disease-only peaks rs200028/rs200050/rs200068 (Q=49/45 df).

sl-test-v2-77cee1d1f675.label: RESULT
sl-test-v2-77cee1d1f675.text: Final gb07 team-b estimates: AFR carrier 0.0926, EUR 0.0703, AFR screen-negative residual 0.0339, partner full-roster carrier 0.2215 (site x wave x FH reweighted; range 0.20-0.27 across stratifications), couple risk ~0.00188.

sl-test-v2-441964840049.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-441964840049.text: WARNING SIGN: disease marginal z-scores decay much faster with distance than the EUR LD matrix (AR(1) rho=0.749) implies, e.g. around disease-only peak rs200068 (z=47.1) neighbours are 20.3/25.7 (ratio ~0.45-0.55) and lag-3 ~0, while protein phase2 z around rs200024 decay at ~0.75 matching R; GLS MR with R gives Q=10000 on 78 df and theta swings 0.02-0.40 by pleiotropy set. MEANS: LD reference fits protein GWAS but not disease GWAS (LD mismatch), so marginal-scale MR with shared R is invalid. ACTION: switch to joint-effect MVMR: protein joint effects from EUR R at 6 conditionally independent leads, disease modelled with its own AR(rho) LD estimated by profile fit, disease-only variants (rs200028, rs200050, rs200068...) modelled as pleiotropic joint effects.

sl-test-v2-5c33955cf7be.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-5c33955cf7be.text: Director Q1 (donut, 40kb, target in expected): On distance-normalised 20kb O/E, pixel (8,17) is log2 1.92/2.11 in case reps while its donut (7x7 minus 3x3, 26 pixels) is ~0.02/0.08, so case enrichment is focal (pixel/donut 1.91/2.03), not domain-wide; control pixel/donut is 0.15/-0.35. The 40kb pixel (4,8) covering the same coordinates gives case 1.19/1.05, control 0.22/0.05 (GC GLM), the same direction but diluted, as expected when one 20kb loop pixel is averaged with three background pixels. The target should be left out of its own expected: with it, case r1 diag-9 mean falls from LOO 1.92 to 1.60, because the loop pulls down its own O/E. No method change.

sl-test-v2-2a865532985d.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-2a865532985d.text: Director Q2 (diag-9 support, long-range zeros, decay): Confirmed 15 diag-9 pixels, 11 valid after masking bins 10/11, so 10 pixels set the GLM d_9 factor once the target is left out (the GC coefficient is shared across all ~250 pixels). The diag-9 variants differ: case mean-LOO 1.92/2.11 vs median-LOO 2.20/2.21. The case diag-9 neighbour (9,18)=39/29 is part of the loop footprint and raises the mean. Zeros occur only at dist>=12, mostly in controls, and do not affect d_9: fits with dist<=15 or with nonzero pixels only give the same log2 O/E to within 0.01. Decay slope differs (case -1.24, control -1.45), which per-replicate expected handles. A smoothed log-distance quadratic expected gives case 1.71, control -0.48, delta 2.19. No method change; the control absolute value is the least certain number.

sl-test-v2-4d7f238702a4.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-4d7f238702a4.text: Director Q3 (GC coefficient stability, per-bin bias): Leave-one-bin-out over the 20 good non-anchor bins keeps the GC coefficient at 0.73-1.63 (base 1.11-1.32, se ~0.25), with target log2 O/E ranges case r1 1.57-2.22 and ctrl r2 -0.58 to -0.35. Among the 22 good bins GC is uncorrelated with mappability (r=0.02) and weakly correlated with re_sites (0.30). A joint gc+lmap+lre fit keeps the GC coefficient at 0.81-1.23 and changes the target by <=0.09. Residual per-bin bias after the GC model is bin8 -0.04/-0.04/0.07/-0.18 and bin17 -0.23/-0.20/0.01/-0.05, against a bin sd of 0.10-0.18. A full per-bin fixed-effect (balancing-equivalent) NB GLM gives case 1.97, control -0.26, delta 2.23. No method change; delta lies between 1.98 and 2.23 across all bias models.

sl-test-v2-8e8de2e67a39.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-8e8de2e67a39.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team applied barcode-level QC, fixed before looking at genotype, that flagged total-UMI outliers and droplets whose HBB is far in excess of what ambient contamination could explain (red-blood-cell-contaminated droplets), and estimated contamination only after setting those aside. Your notes record duplicate checks but no barcode QC, and your contamination model assumes all HBB in a cell is ambient. Check whether such barcodes exist in your data, how many there are per donor and per genotype, and whether your per-donor contamination estimates move when they are set aside. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-d14cdcd37267.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-d14cdcd37267.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team defined the activated state from the ISG markers only after removing the ambient contribution to those markers, on the grounds that the ambient profile itself contains ISG transcripts and contamination differs between donors. Your clustering used an ISG/LST1 score with no recorded ambient adjustment, and the two teams ended with different numbers of activated cells. Check whether the cluster assignment of any cells, especially in the high-contamination donors, changes when the ambient contribution to the gating markers is accounted for, and which donors those cells belong to. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-7972c97a082c.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-7972c97a082c.text: REPLY Q1 (target in expected): in case the (8,17) pixel is 23-25% of the summed balanced diagonal-9 signal over 11 valid pixels, against about 9% for a typical pixel. In control it is 6-8%. Including it raises the case expected by about 0.25 log2 but barely moves control, so it shrinks delta. A leave-one-out (background) expected is the right definition. Method revised: delta goes from 1.70 to 1.99 with the expected change alone.

sl-test-v2-e70734796d28.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-e70734796d28.text: REPLY Q2 (GC): bins 8 and 17 have GC 0.58/0.57, ranking 5th and 7th of 24 (z about +1), so they are elevated but not extreme. Raw coverage correlates with GC (r 0.50-0.59). After ICE the residual pixel-level GC slope is 0.1-0.7 log2 per unit of GC-sum. The target's GC-sum is 0.114 above the diagonal-9 mean, which gives at most 0.01-0.08 log2 bias, similar in both conditions. It does not change the method.

sl-test-v2-53bd26d60b2c.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-53bd26d60b2c.text: REPLY Q3 (ICE weights): edge bins 0,1,22,23 have about 0.55-0.85 of the median weight. Masking them changes per-replicate leave-out log2 O/E by 0.02-0.26 and delta by -0.1. Removing the (8,17) pixel from balancing lowers the weights of bins 8 and 17 by 8-9% in case but only 1.4-1.9% in control. So the loop pixel is partly absorbed as bias in case only. The method was revised to balance with the target pixel excluded. Final: case 1.93, control -0.29, delta 2.22. A smoothed P(s) under the same balancing gives delta 2.41.

sl-test-v2-e4a2061a0499.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-e4a2061a0499.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that the way the ambient expectation is removed (per cell with clipping at zero, per donor without clipping, or as a term in the model mean) changes the estimate, and that ambient makes up the majority of activated-cell CXCL10 counts in the most contaminated donors. Check in your mixture-mean fit what share of each donor's expected CXCL10 count is the ambient term, how much information the most contaminated donors actually contribute to the genotype coefficient, and whether the coefficient is stable to the dispersion and to how those donors are weighted. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-549c908d3856.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-549c908d3856.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team counted activated cells per donor and applied (and varied) a minimum number of activated cells for a donor to enter the pseudobulk fit, because the activated fraction is small in some genotype groups. Your notes do not record such a check. Tabulate activated cells per donor in your data and check whether any donor enters your fit on very few cells. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-ae53bc6cd694.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-ae53bc6cd694.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team estimated a separate contamination fraction for each donor, whereas your notes describe contamination as two donor groups and your plan mentioned a per-cell estimate. State at which level (cell, donor, donor group) the contamination fraction in your final model is estimated, how precisely HBB counts pin it down at that level, and whether the genotype coefficient moves when the level is changed. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-7b51e82f0c09.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-7b51e82f0c09.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team did not take the HBB-derived contamination scale on trust: they let a multiplier on the ambient CXCL10 term be estimated from the data, once in activated cells only and once jointly with the resting cells, and found the genotype coefficient very sensitive to that multiplier. Your notes record no test of the ambient scale. Check in your data what multiplier the counts themselves support, in the activated stratum alone and when the resting stratum is included, and how your coefficient responds across a plausible range. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-f1bdd231e3d9.label: gb10 result
sl-test-v2-f1bdd231e3d9.text: gb10 chr1 QTL result (team-a): an 8-founder HMM (2 flipped markers m1_056/m1_058 and 29 monomorphic markers dropped) with a batch-adjusted HK scan peaks at 45 cM (LOD 5.18; LMM with chr2 kinship 44.1 cM; 1.5-LOD interval about 40.5-61 cM, narrowing to 40.5-48 with a chr2 covariate). F5 is the top founder in the fixed effects, REML-BLUP and the LMM, and in 75% of 500 bootstraps; F4 is runner-up (16%) and overtakes F5 only with the chr2 covariate plus shrinkage. A conditional scan shows no strong second chr1 QTL (distal conditional LOD at most 3.2).

sl-test-v2-df6a023cdd0b.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-df6a023cdd0b.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team fitted the same ambient-corrected model in the resting cluster and used it as a check on whether the ambient correction is complete. Check what your corrected CXCL10 rates look like in the resting stratum across donors and contamination levels, and whether that pattern is what you would expect if the ambient removal were right. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-b84f931825dd.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-b84f931825dd.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team defined the activated state from ISG and LST1 jointly and obtained a different number of activated cells from you. You recorded that ISG-high and LST1-low agree for most but not all cells. Check the cells where your ISG gate and LST1 status disagree: which donors and genotypes they come from, what their CXCL10 and contamination look like, and whether your estimate moves when they are assigned the other way. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-24858439ec9e.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-24858439ec9e.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team estimated the endogenous rate and the ambient term together in one donor-level negative-binomial mean model, rather than subtracting first and fitting afterwards. You recorded strong overdispersion between donors, yet your ambient-in-mean version was a Poisson fit, and your headline figure combines it with a subtract-then-fit version. Check how donors whose corrected count is near or below zero are handled in each version, whether the two versions weight the heavily contaminated donors the same way, and which single version you judge correct and why. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-73ab8e90d7e9.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-73ab8e90d7e9.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team ran leave-one-donor-out and a donor bootstrap, and described contamination as falling into two donor groups rather than varying donor by donor. Your notes record neither a leave-one-out check nor how precisely each donor's rho is determined. Check whether any single donor drives your coefficient, how noisy the donor-specific rho values are given the HBB counts behind them, and whether the coefficient moves if rho is shared within the two contamination groups. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-223615fa36f2.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-223615fa36f2.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your case against the symmetric 0.16 error model rests on locus A gen 6 (36/40 = 0.90 > 0.84) being 'impossible', but for 40 reads at a true rate of 0.84 the chance of 36 or more is about 0.21. Refit all three error models (asymmetric 0.31/0.01, symmetric 0.16, symmetric 0.01) with identical HMM settings and report the log-likelihood for locus A, for locus B, for both jointly, and for locus A with the gen-6 sample left out. Does the preference for the asymmetric model survive at locus B and without that one sample, and does the result change your method or the uncertainty you attach to s?

sl-test-v2-b7b98b370504.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-b7b98b370504.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team checked the input for duplicate barcode IDs and duplicate rows before analysis, and did not remove cells by UMI or HBB thresholds. Your notes record cell QC but no duplicate check. Check whether duplicates exist in your data, and report how many cells per donor and genotype your QC removed and whether removal is balanced across the contamination groups. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-60b9dbadb5a3.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-60b9dbadb5a3.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You name the 0.31/0.01 split as your weakest point but only report it. Profile the likelihood over the split itself (C->T rate free, T->C = 0.32 minus it, shared by both loci, s and starting frequency re-optimised at each value) and report the likelihood-supported range of the split and the s_A estimate at each end of that range. Locus A's late T fractions (0.33-0.45) sit at the assumed 0.31 floor, so state how far s_A moves when the floor moves within its supported range. Does this change your point estimate or widen your interval?

sl-test-v2-ee66f4f84ef6.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-ee66f4f84ef6.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your piecewise-s test (break at generation 26, s 0.15 then 0.05, LRT 5.3) was run in the deterministic fit and only under the asymmetric error model. Repeat it inside the drift HMM with the Ne schedule, under each error model, and add a goodness-of-fit test of the constant-s model (for example simulating trajectories and read counts from the fitted model and comparing a fit statistic). Is the deceleration still present with drift modelled, and does it appear only under the error model that puts the late samples on the error floor? Does the result change whether constant s is adequate and which interval defines the s you report?

sl-test-v2-a8b88b3638e2.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-a8b88b3638e2.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your notes do not say how the hidden chain starts or how N enters. Report s_A and its interval under (a) the chain started at generation 0 versus at generation 6, (b) a flat prior on starting frequency versus a starting frequency estimated as a free parameter, and (c) drift variance p(1-p)/N versus p(1-p)/(2N) and N halved. Does any of these move s_A by more than a small fraction of its confidence interval, and if so does it change the method?

sl-test-v2-714afdcfcfd2.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-714afdcfcfd2.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your case against the symmetric 0.16 error model rests on locus A gen 6 (36/40 = 0.90 > 0.84) being 'impossible', but for 40 reads at a true rate of 0.84 the chance of 36 or more is about 0.21. Refit the asymmetric 0.31/0.01, symmetric 0.16 and symmetric 0.01 models with identical HMM settings and report the log-likelihood for locus A, for locus B, for both jointly, and for locus A with the gen-6 sample left out. Does the preference for the asymmetric model survive at locus B and without that one sample, and does the result change your method or the uncertainty you attach to s?

sl-test-v2-144c06592699.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-144c06592699.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You tested T->C rates from 0.001 to 0.1 but did not record what s did, and your interval for s (0.04-0.165) holds the split fixed. Profile the likelihood over the split (C->T free, T->C = 0.32 minus it, shared by both loci, other parameters re-optimised) and report the supported range of the split and s_A at each end. Locus A's late T fractions (0.33-0.45) sit at the assumed 0.31 floor. Does the spread of s_A over the supported splits change your point estimate or your stated interval?

sl-test-v2-515590f70f45.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-515590f70f45.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your record lists no pitfall checks and no test of constant selection. Inside your HMM, compare constant s with piecewise s at the Ne-schedule boundaries (generations 18/19, 26/27, 37/38) for locus A by likelihood ratio, correcting for the number of breakpoints tried, and compare the HMM estimate with a deterministic no-drift fit. Is there evidence that s differs between the early rise and the late samples near the error floor, and does it change whether a single s is the right quantity to report?

sl-test-v2-fab8c06469f2.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-fab8c06469f2.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: State three modelling choices your notes leave open and report s_A under the alternative for each: (a) whether your HMM's s is the per-generation fitness advantage (w = 1 + s) or a logit slope, (b) whether the chain starts at generation 0 or generation 6 and with what prior on starting frequency, (c) whether drift variance uses N or 2N. Does any alternative move s_A by more than a small fraction of its interval, and does that change the method?

sl-test-v2-7210ec9d72a7.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-7210ec9d72a7.text: WARNING SIGN: even with disease-specific AR(rho) LD and 9-12 modelled disease-only variants, residual heterogeneity remains (Q~225-370 on ~67 df) and theta_PROTA ranges 0.29-0.41, theta_PROTB 0.20-0.31 per SD across rho 0.35-0.75. MEANS: residual LD mismatch/pleiotropy is not fully captured; point estimates carry model uncertainty well beyond the nominal SE (~0.015). ACTION: report central value across best-fitting specifications (rho 0.5-0.75 joint models and the EUR-R full GLS with stepwise pleiotropy): PROTA ~0.34, PROTB ~0.23 per SD (SD = within-batch SD from batches 1-2: 0.253 PROTA, 0.202 PROTB log10 units).

sl-test-v2-f1a4b0f4c1ec.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-f1a4b0f4c1ec.text: WARNING SIGN: LINC473-targeting CRISPRi/follow-up guides that knock LINC473 down ~80% (expr_rel 0.20) but leave KIN1 intact (expr_rel 0.82-0.89) show only -0.08 to -0.18 growth, while LINC473 guides that co-repress KIN1 (expr_rel 0.12-0.21) show -0.54 to -0.68; in the single-guide follow-up growth correlates with KIN1 knockdown r=-0.98 and with LINC473 knockdown r=-0.08. MEANS: the LINC473-locus pooled growth phenotype is driven almost entirely by concomitant KIN1 repression (chromatin spreading), not loss of the LINC473 transcript. ACTION: did not read raw CRISPRi LFC of LINC473 guides as the lncRNA effect; used a joint regression growth~(1-exprLINC)+(1-exprKIN) for the KIN1 term and CasRx transcript-directed data for the lncRNA term.

sl-test-v2-c67e4dfc29c9.label: WARNING SIGN
sl-test-v2-c67e4dfc29c9.text: WARNING SIGN: CasRx guides with low major_isoform_overlap (0.03-0.14) show growth effects as strong or stronger (-0.16 to -0.18) than high-overlap guides at matched knockdown, and all sit on plate_C. MEANS: likely collateral/off-target activity, not dominant-transcript effect; including them biases the transcript-specific estimate. ACTION: restricted the CasRx growth~knockdown_efficiency fit to high-overlap (>=0.5) guides and extrapolated to efficiency=1.

sl-test-v2-bdc7ef8a97dd.label: RESULT
sl-test-v2-bdc7ef8a97dd.text: RESULT: lncrna_specific_lfc ~= -0.18 (CasRx high-overlap guides, growth_lfc vs knockdown_efficiency extrapolated to 1; naive -0.176, Deming -0.177, through-origin purest guides -0.187). neighbor_mediated_lfc ~= -0.65 (KIN1 coefficient of joint pooled CRISPRi regression, intercept~0, VIF~1.1; followup validation bKIN=-0.77). advance_target=0 because neighbor_mediated_lfc (-0.65) is not > -0.25 even though lncrna_specific (-0.18) <= -0.08.

sl-test-v2-1fffd96bc31c.label: REFEREE TEST
sl-test-v2-1fffd96bc31c.text: gb03 referee: X (ICE per-bin balancing, target excluded, delta 2.22) and Y (NB GLM distance+GC-sum, delta 1.98) agree on masking bins 10/11 and leave-one-out diag-9 expected; they differ only in the bias model. Leave-one-pixel-out NB prediction of 136 non-target anchor-row pixels (bins 8/17, dist 2-15, 4 reps) gave mean deviance 1.58 for GC-only vs 1.72 for per-bin factors, sign-flip p=0.17; AIC favoured GC in controls, per-bin in case_r1, tie in case_r2. The data do not discriminate the two bias models; delta is about 2.0-2.2 either way.

sl-test-v2-94cc6bbc313c.reason: The choice of expected defines the reported quantity; a global or mis-matched expected turns log2(O/E) into a measure of distance decay rather than loop enrichment.
sl-test-v2-94cc6bbc313c.text: The expected value in observed/expected must be distance-matched. Confirm from the data that the pixel (bin 8, bin 17) at 20 kb sits on the diagonal dist_bin = 9, and that the dist_bin column equals bin_j - bin_i. The expected for that pixel is then computed from pixels on that same diagonal only, within the same replicate, after the same normalization as the observed value (the cooltools expected_cis convention). Do not use a whole-matrix mean, pool several diagonals into one average, or borrow an expected from another replicate or another resolution.

sl-test-v2-211268f80d9c.reason: The order of operations (log then average, per replicate) changes the numbers, and the task defines the quantities as means of per-replicate log2(O/E); depth or P(s) differences between conditions would otherwise leak into delta.
sl-test-v2-211268f80d9c.text: Compute everything per replicate first, then average. The four replicates (two control, two case) can differ in sequencing depth and in the shape of the distance-decay curve P(s), so comparing raw counts or pooled matrices confounds depth or P(s) differences with loop differences. Check total counts and log-log P(s) slopes for each replicate. Compute the expected within each replicate (O/E then normalizes itself for depth), take log2(O/E) per replicate, and take the arithmetic mean of the two log2 values per condition; delta is the case mean minus the control mean. The mean of log2(O/E) is not the same as log2 of the mean O/E or log2 of O/E on summed replicates, so do not sum replicates first. Look at the target pixel's count in every replicate and at zeros on its diagonal: a zero gives -inf, so use a pseudocount only if a zero actually occurs, and state it. Report the spread between replicates within each condition; a joint normalization across replicates (multiHiCcompare-style loess) can serve as a sensitivity check.

sl-test-v2-043a312ac616.reason: Whether the reported loop strength is computed on raw or bias-corrected counts can change all three numbers; the bin covariates are supplied in the data and should not be ignored without a check.
sl-test-v2-043a312ac616.text: Raw Hi-C counts carry per-bin visibility biases. The 20 kb bin annotation file gives gc_content, mappability and re_sites (restriction-site density) for each bin, so O/E computed on raw counts may reflect bias at the two anchor bins rather than looping. Per replicate, correlate bin coverage (row sums) with gc_content, mappability and re_sites, and compare the row sums of bins 8 and 17 with the other bins. If bias is present, correct for it before computing O/E: either balance each replicate's matrix (ICE/Sinkhorn, cis-only, excluding the shortest 1-2 diagonals) or fit an explicit Poisson/negative-binomial model with log(gc), log(mappability) and log(re_sites) as covariates. Compute observed and expected on the same corrected scale, and report both the raw and the corrected values.

sl-test-v2-1e27f684be6c.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-1e27f684be6c.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that cohort_roster rows are not all of one kind: they differ in family_history_tier, and the screen-positive rate is not the same across tiers within each ancestry. Your checks list a tier breakdown of screening carrier rates, but your record does not say which rows went into carrier_frequency_afr and carrier_frequency_eur. Tabulate cohort_roster by collection x ancestry x family_history_tier (and any field that marks adults), check whether the tiers differ in your data, and state which rows you judge the task to mean by 'screening-roster adults' and why. Does it change your method, including the prior that goes into the AFR screen-negative residual risk?

sl-test-v2-ba6df3c95a2e.reason: Bad bins left in the matrix shift the balancing weights and the diagonal-9 expected, and a flagged anchor bin would change how far the result can be trusted.
sl-test-v2-ba6df3c95a2e.text: Low-quality bins and short-range diagonals distort both balancing and the expected. Flag bins with low mappability or with log-coverage far below the median (about 5 MAD or more), mask them (set to NaN) and leave them out of the per-diagonal expected averages. Check specifically whether bin 8 or bin 17 is itself flagged. The shortest diagonals (distance 0-1 bins) carry self-ligation and undigested-fragment artefacts and should be ignored when balancing (the cooltools default is ignore_diags=2); note that the contact table has no main diagonal (dist_bin starts at 1), so adapt the balancing accordingly.

sl-test-v2-dbddb0791465.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-dbddb0791465.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team treated the partner term row by row: a tested partner row carries its own assay result (read with lot_C42 calibration), and an untested row carries a prior that does not come from the tested partners. You recorded that 280 of 500 partner rows sit in one site x wave x family-history stratum where only 14 were tested, and that your figure rests on missing-at-random within strata. Check (a) how much of your full-roster estimate comes from those 14 rows, (b) whether the tested rows in that stratum look like a random draw from it on every roster field you have (ancestry, tier, any reason-for-testing field), and (c) whether the carrier rates you infer for tested partners are compatible with the screening-roster rates for the same ancestry and family-history tier after allowing for the different reagent lot. Does it change your method for the untested rows?

sl-test-v2-578d422a46ec.reason: With about 15 pixels per diagonal, the choice between plain mean, median, target-excluded mean and smoothed expected can visibly move the answer, so the choice must be deliberate and its sensitivity reported.
sl-test-v2-578d422a46ec.text: The 20 kb matrix has only 24 bins, so the diagonal at distance 9 has only about 15 pixels (fewer after masking). The expected there is noisy, is pulled up by the target pixel itself if that pixel is enriched, and can be skewed by other loops, domain structure, edge bins or bad bins. Count the valid pixels on diagonal 9 in each replicate and compare the diagonal mean with the median, with and without the (8,17) pixel; also compare with a smoothed P(s) (log-log regression or loess across diagonals; cooltools smooths P(s) by default). These are still distance-matched expecteds, so they do not conflict with the rule against pooling diagonals into a single mean. Choose and justify one definition of the expected as primary before comparing conditions, state which one was used, and report how much the three quantities move under the alternatives.

sl-test-v2-c8e4ae7d4900.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-c8e4ae7d4900.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: you named the per-ancestry heterogeneity of the B log OR (EUR +0.31, AFR -0.31, EAS -1.06) as your weakest point but only reported it. Refit the marker-to-B calibration separately within each ancestry group (or with ancestry-by-marker terms), compare those predicted dosages with your pooled ones, and then test the B-by-ancestry interaction formally in the weighted model, also once unweighted and once without the outer term. Does the heterogeneity come from tagging, from the weights, or from the outer adjustment, and does the result change your method?

sl-test-v2-fbd5875893d4.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-fbd5875893d4.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that DRX1_T02 deletion sensitivity in the controls differs between the two reagent lots within the same ancestry, as well as between ancestries, and that some deletion-like calls in 'none' controls survive the segmental-duplication filter and cannot be told apart from true deletions. Your recorded AFR deletion sensitivity pools controls from both lots. Check whether deletion sensitivity and the remaining false-positive rate differ by lot within ancestry in your data, and whether the AFR detection rate behind your residual risk uses only the lot the screening roster was run on. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-37eabe575882.reason: It determines how the reported numbers should be interpreted and guards against describing a domain-wide change as a loop change.
sl-test-v2-37eabe575882.text: A diagonal (global) expected marks every pixel inside a contact domain as enriched, so a high O/E is not by itself evidence of a focal loop. Loop callers (HiCCUPS, cooltools dots) compare the pixel with a local background instead. As QC, compute the enrichment of the (8,17) pixel against a donut neighbourhood (for example a ring of pixels 1-3 bins away, excluding the peak's own row and column) and compare it with the diagonal-expected O/E in each replicate. If the two diverge, keep the diagonal-expected O/E as the primary result, because the task asks for observed/expected, and report the local enrichment as QC. State whether any case-control difference looks like a focal loop change or a broad domain-level change.

sl-test-v2-909d3a8e478b.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-909d3a8e478b.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the task asks for a 'total-effect' odds ratio, and your weighted B estimate is -0.13 without the outer-orientation term and -0.27 with it. In the reliable panel, tabulate integer B copies against integer outer dosage and report the outer coefficient with its interval from the joint model, then state from that evidence whether outer orientation acts as a separate confounder of B or as the background on which B copies sit, and therefore which of the two models estimates a total effect of B. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-c7d2c5c22a0e.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-c7d2c5c22a0e.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that in partner_roster the positive-call rate among tested partners differs a lot between intake_site x collection_wave strata, and that testing completion also depends on site x wave x family-history tier (one site is fully tested, while the largest stratum has very few tested rows). Your partner strata use ancestry x tier and testing result only. Tabulate partner_roster by intake_site x collection_wave x family_history_tier x testing_status, check whether this holds in your data, and check whether a prior for untested partners taken from the screening cohort by ancestry x tier agrees with the tested partners in the same site x wave stratum. Does it change your method for the untested rows?

sl-test-v2-6a67f0d68e22.reason: The task supplies 40 kb data that is otherwise unused; it is the available independent check on the 20 kb estimate, and an off-centre peak would change how the result is qualified.
sl-test-v2-6a67f0d68e22.text: Measured loop signal depends on resolution, and a loop anchor that is split across two 20 kb bins or sits one bin off shifts the enrichment at the named pixel. Inspect the 3x3 neighbourhood around (8,17) at 20 kb in each replicate to see whether the peak is centred on that pixel. Cross-check with the 40 kb data: find the 40 kb pixel that contains the two 20 kb bins by matching genomic coordinates in the two bin annotation files (the library suggests 40 kb bins 4 and 8, but this is unverified, so confirm by coordinates rather than by index arithmetic), and check that the case-control direction agrees. Expect a smaller fold change at 40 kb. Still report the 20 kb (8,17) pixel as the task asks; record any peak offset or disagreement between resolutions in the QC.

sl-test-v2-775ed5f6cbeb.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-775ed5f6cbeb.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the sign of your B log OR flips between the unweighted and the weighted fit, and the weights span roughly 1.2 to several hundred. Compute the effective sample size of the weighted fit, the share of total weight carried by the ten heaviest rows, and the B estimate when those rows are removed one at a time and when weights are capped or stabilised. Does the weighted sign rest on a handful of heavily weighted controls, and does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-0f278ab7c4d5.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-0f278ab7c4d5.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the two teams did not use the same cohort_roster rows for the carrier frequencies. You excluded the family_history_tier 1 rows although every cohort row has collection = screening; the other team did not record such an exclusion. Check whether the roster or the task text gives any basis, other than the difference in positive rate, for saying tier-1 rows are not 'screening-roster adults' (for example a field for ascertainment route, referral, or age), and state which reading of the estimand you judge the task to mean and why. Check also whether the AFR screen-negative residual risk should use the same row set as carrier_frequency_afr. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-a2dbd6f71a0d.reason: raised when two earlier teams disagreed; check it on the data
sl-test-v2-a2dbd6f71a0d.text: WARNING SIGN TO CHECK: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that the two anchor bins (8 and 17) have unusually high gc_content compared with the other bins, and that contact counts depend on GC in every replicate. Check whether that holds in your data, and whether any dependence of your balanced values on the GC of the two bins remains after ICE (for example among the diagonal-9 pixels you average for the expected). Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-6d3d4633f860.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-6d3d4633f860.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your choice of GENE2 rests on GENE1's multimapping profile, yet GENE1 keeps a B slope of 0.44 with a B-by-multimapper interaction of 0.39. Evaluate the GENE1 slope at the multimapper fraction typical of the other genes (and in your low-multimapper subset) and compare it with the GENE2 slope; separately, test a B-by-case interaction for GENE2 to see whether your sample-level slope (0.308) and your source-population-weighted slope (0.286) differ for a real reason, given that the task attaches 'full-cohort source-population' to the expression support too. Does either result change your method?

sl-test-v2-65a4a35201cf.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-65a4a35201cf.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found allele dropout at DRX1_T01 in class_01 controls (VAF near zero in true carriers) at a rate that differs between AFR and EUR, and corrected class proportions jointly with an ancestry x batch misclassification matrix instead of one class at a time. Check in your controls whether class_01 sensitivity differs by ancestry as well as by lot, whether your het window (VAF 0.3-0.7, depth >= 20) loses true carriers beyond the dropout cases, and whether any control of one class is called as another class or as two classes, which a per-class correction would not account for. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-101b4cff5122.reason: raised when two earlier teams disagreed; check it on the data
sl-test-v2-101b4cff5122.text: WARNING SIGN TO CHECK: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team observed that ICE balancing on this truncated 24-bin window can be distorted by edge bins (which see only part of their contacts) and by the loop pixel's own contribution to the coverage of bins 8 and 17. Check in your data how the balancing weights of bins 8 and 17 and of the edge bins compare with the rest, and whether those weights change if the target pixel is left out of the balancing. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-56ca2d79abaa.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-56ca2d79abaa.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the task asks for a 'total-effect' odds ratio, and you fitted B jointly with the outer-orientation dosage; you also found 26 B carriers with outer dosage 0. Report the weighted B estimate with and without the outer term side by side, the outer coefficient with its interval, and the B-by-outer table in the reliable panel, then state from that evidence whether conditioning on outer dosage gives a total effect of B or a partial one. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-0f5856df7e4d.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-0f5856df7e4d.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your record gives one pooled B log OR and adjusts for PCs but not ancestry_group, and it shows calibration accuracy by ancestry but no clinical estimate by ancestry. Fit the weighted model within each ancestry group and test the B-by-ancestry interaction, and repeat with the calibration fitted within ancestry. Is the pooled sign shared by the groups, and do the weights (with the effective sample size and the share of weight on the ten heaviest rows) or the tagging drive any difference? Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-8cc59c7697b6.reason: raised when two earlier teams disagreed; check it on the data
sl-test-v2-8cc59c7697b6.text: WARNING SIGN TO CHECK: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team left the target pixel (8,17) out of the data used to build the expected, whereas your primary expected is the diagonal-9 mean with that pixel included among only 11 valid pixels. You recorded that your result moves when the target is left out. Check how much of the diagonal-9 mean in each replicate comes from the target pixel itself, and state which definition of 'expected' you judge the task to mean and why. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-fc505d531c4d.reason: raised when two earlier teams disagreed; check it on the data
sl-test-v2-fc505d531c4d.text: WARNING SIGN TO CHECK: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that only 11 valid pixels remain on diagonal 9 once bins 10 and 11 are masked, that the result moves with how the diagonal-9 expected is defined (mean, median, target left out, smoothed across distances), that the distance-decay slope differs between case and control, and that control replicates have zero pixels at long range. Check whether these hold in your data, how many pixels actually determine the distance-9 factor in your GLM, and whether the long-range zeros or the differing decay affect the fit. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-a80f9e1669d1.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-a80f9e1669d1.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your calibration assumes the 483 reliable samples are representative of the panel, but local_complexity describes repeats around the breakpoint and could depend on the genotype itself. Using depth_log2_segment_B, which exists for all 780 samples, compare the depth-based copy distribution (and case status and ancestry) between reliable and QC-failed samples, and among the 483 count how many copy_index values lie within 0.2 of a rounding boundary and whether depth agrees with the rounded call there. Does QC failure depend on segment-B dosage, and does that change the calibration or the carrier count?

sl-test-v2-11b4c84d5a5d.reason: raised when two earlier teams disagreed; check it on the data
sl-test-v2-11b4c84d5a5d.text: WARNING SIGN TO CHECK: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team corrected per-bin bias by balancing each replicate rather than with a single covariate, and found that bin coverage is strongly related to mappability, driven by bins 10 and 11. Your GC effect is one linear coefficient shared across all distances and fit on about 250 pixels. Check whether that coefficient is stable when it is estimated without the influence of particular bins (for example the edge bins or bins neighbouring 10 and 11), whether it is separable from mappability and re_sites in these 24 bins, and whether residual per-bin bias remains at bins 8 and 17 after your model. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-61d4354156e6.reason: question from the director challenging the answer both teams agreed on
sl-test-v2-61d4354156e6.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: your expression model has no case-status term and no sampling weights, although the expression panel is a subset of a cohort that is 81% cases and the task attaches 'full-cohort source-population' to the expression support. Check whether log_expr of GENE2 differs by case status, whether expression-panel membership depends on case, ancestry or design stratum, and how the GENE2 slope moves when case is added, when a B-by-case term is added, and when inverse sample_fraction weights are used; also give the GENE1 slope at a multimapper fraction typical of the other genes. Does any of this change your method or your choice of gene?

sl-test-v2-ac70de2dbd8b.reason: raised when two earlier teams disagreed; check it on the data
sl-test-v2-ac70de2dbd8b.text: WARNING SIGN TO CHECK: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team used two cross-checks you did not record: a local (donut) background around pixel (8,17) to tell a focal loop from broader domain enrichment, and the 40 kb pixel covering the same coordinates as a consistency check on the 20 kb estimate. Check whether your expected and your per-condition values are consistent with those two views in your data. Also state whether you judge that the task's 'expected' should include or exclude the target pixel, and why. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-e6c71d651733.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-e6c71d651733.text: REPLY Q-modelling-choices (gb04 team-b, locus A): s in the HMM is the per-generation haploid fitness advantage w=1+s (s=0.096); the logit-slope parametrisation gives log(1+s)=0.092, the same model. Starting the chain at gen 6 with flat prior gives s_A=0.101; gen 0 with U-shaped 1/x(1-x) prior gives 0.105; drift with 2N instead of N (haploid N) gives 0.095. All shifts <=0.01, well inside the 0.04-0.165 interval; method unchanged.

sl-test-v2-3a8152e85bfc.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-3a8152e85bfc.text: REPLY Q-constant-s (gb04 team-b, locus A): piecewise s at breakpoints 18/19, 26/27, 37/38 gives LRT 0.01, 0.59, 0.31 (1 df each, uncorrected p>0.4; Bonferroni x3 makes it weaker), early/late s e.g. 0.123/0.066 at 26, not significant. Deterministic no-drift fit gives s=0.089, close to HMM 0.096. No evidence s changes between early rise and late samples near the error floor; reporting a single s is appropriate.

sl-test-v2-7f00d0498832.label: PLAN
sl-test-v2-7f00d0498832.text: PLAN: Estimate per-replicate log2(O/E) at 20kb pixel (8,17), dist 9, averaged within condition; delta=case-control. Method: per replicate, mask low-quality bins (low mappability 10,11 / coverage outliers >5 MAD), ICE-balance cis matrix ignoring diag 1 (no diag 0 present), expected = mean of balanced diag-9 valid pixels within same replicate (target included, cooltools convention) as primary; alternatives: median, leave-target-out, log-log smoothed P(s), raw counts, GLM with GC/map/RE covariates. Checks: dist_bin=j-i, depth, P(s) slopes, zeros, bias correlations, 3x3 neighbourhood, donut, 40kb pixel (4,8) by coordinates, ICE weight sensitivity to target exclusion. Change method if balancing leaves residual GC bias or if conclusions flip under expected definitions.

sl-test-v2-5da3a5139c03.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-5da3a5139c03.text: REPLY Q-error-split-profile (gb04 team-b): profiling C->T=e, T->C=0.32-e shared by A and B, joint logL is maximal at the boundary T->C=0 (e=0.32, -60.12) and within 1.92 for e from about 0.255 to 0.32; s_A runs from about 0.078 (e=0.255) to 0.101 (e=0.32), s_B stays 0.024. With the stated ~1% instrument rate, T->C=0.01 (s_A=0.096) is in the supported range. Point estimate kept at 0.096; interval widened slightly to about 0.03-0.17 to include split uncertainty.

sl-test-v2-b9c3ff116ce6.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-b9c3ff116ce6.text: REPLY Q-error-model-comparison (gb04 team-b): logL asym(0.31/0.01) / sym0.16 / sym0.01: locus A -30.06 / -34.14 / -33.39; locus B -30.34 / -30.55 / -31.70; joint -60.40 / -64.69 / -65.09; locus A without gen 6 -27.65 / -29.84 / -30.33. The asymmetric model is preferred at A even without gen 6 (by 2.2 logL), and B can barely tell them apart (B is far from the floor). s_A: asym 0.096 (0.080 without gen 6), sym0.16 0.060, sym0.01 0.043. Method kept; gen-6 leverage (s 0.096->0.080) is noted as extra uncertainty.

sl-test-v2-da5bac324d5b.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-da5bac324d5b.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that the disease marginal z-scores fall off with distance from a peak faster than the EUR correlation reference predicts, while the phase-2 protein z-scores follow the reference. Your LD checks are recorded as finding no problem, but they do not say whether they were run on the disease file separately from the protein files. Check, for the disease statistics alone and for each protein alone, how the z-scores of the neighbours of a strong peak (for example the disease-only peak rs200068, and a protein lead SNP) compare with what the reference predicts at lag 1, 2 and 3. Does the reference describe the disease data as well as it describes the protein data, and does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-72f60a3392e6.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-72f60a3392e6.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team recorded that two of the disease-only peaks lie right next to protein lead SNPs (rs200028 beside rs200024/rs200025, and rs200050 beside rs200047). Your rule removes every SNP with r2>=0.05 to those peaks. List which SNPs the rule removes, and check whether the strongest and the conditionally independent lead SNPs for PROTA and for PROTB are among them. Among the 47 SNPs you keep, which signals actually identify each protein's effect, and are those SNPs independent signals or only the LD tails of removed leads? Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-dd5a81add5ed.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-dd5a81add5ed.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team kept the SNPs near the disease-only peaks and modelled those variants as explicit effects, and it attributes much of the heterogeneity to the correlation reference not fitting the disease data. You rejected stepwise modelling because it did not converge, and your exclusion set and LD threshold were chosen from the data until Q matched its degrees of freedom. Check whether the failure of your stepwise fit to converge is related to how well the reference fits the disease statistics, and whether a Q close to its degrees of freedom on the retained SNPs could arise from having removed the informative region rather than from a correct model. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-420615280364.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-420615280364.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team did not model the disease-only variants; it removed all SNPs in LD with three disease-only peaks (rs200028, rs200050, rs200068) and then found residual heterogeneity consistent with its degrees of freedom using the EUR reference unchanged. Your models keep a residual Q several times its degrees of freedom under every LD model you tried. Check whether, on the SNPs that are not in LD with those three peaks, the disease statistics are consistent with the EUR reference and with your protein model, and whether the misfit you see is confined to the neighbourhoods of the disease-only peaks or is present across the locus. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-a34ed9038825.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-a34ed9038825.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team identified three protein-independent disease peaks, whereas you modelled 9 to 12 disease-only variants and replaced the reference with a one-parameter AR(rho) correlation for the disease data. sl-test-v2-0d8d8860eab6.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-0d8d8860eab6.text: REPLY Q1 (partner untested rows): The site_A wave_1 FH0 stratum (280 rows, 14 tested, 3/14 screen-positive) gives 0.123 of the 0.2215 full-roster partner estimate, which is 56%. The 14 tested rows match their stratum on every roster field: AFR 6/130 and EUR 8/150 tested. There is no reason-for-testing field. The tested rows are the lowest-numbered IDs (0001-0008, 0001-0006), which points to sequential order, not risk-based selection. Tested-partner carrier rates (lot_C42-corrected) do not match screening-roster rates: in site_B, where 100% of partners were tested, FH0 rates are 0.22-0.24 against 0.06-0.07 in screening (binomial p=0.001 for 14/60 vs 0.094). So partner-roster people are not drawn from the screening population, and putting screening-roster priors on untested rows has no support. Within site_A, wave_1 is higher than wave_2 (FH0 3/14 vs 0/21, p=0.056; FH1 4/11 vs 1/18), so stratifying by wave is supported. The method stays the same (site x wave x FH, MAR). Known sensitivity: a screening prior for untested rows gives 0.137, and pooling waves at site_A gives 0.13.

sl-test-v2-1ddbb2af71e0.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-1ddbb2af71e0.text: REPLY Q2 (screening tiers): cohort_roster is all collection=screening; there is no age or adult field. Counts: AFR FH0 342, AFR FH1 58, EUR FH0 365, EUR FH1 35. Tiers differ: corrected carrier rates are AFR 0.074 (FH0) vs 0.204 (FH1) and EUR 0.059 vs 0.191. All 800 rows went into the carrier frequencies, because the task asks for carrier frequency among screening-roster adults and every row is one. The tier-stratified mixture reproduces the pooled values exactly: AFR 0.0926 with residual 0.0339, EUR 0.0703. This is because both tiers share the same lot_A17 calibration. The method is unchanged.

sl-test-v2-14504b5d5947.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-14504b5d5947.text: REPLY Q3 (lot-specific T02): The calibration matrices are already ancestry x lot; the memory note that described them as pooled was wrong. T02 deletion sensitivity for AFR is 0.515 on lot_A17 and 0.423 on lot_C42; for EUR it is 0.843 and 0.790. The leftover none->deletion false-positive rate after the segdup filter is AFR 0.052/0.058 and EUR 0.025/0.036. The AFR screening residual uses only lot_A17 (the lot the screening roster was run on), and partners use lot_C42. The leftover false positives are handled as misclassification inside the EM. The method is unchanged.

sl-test-v2-2c3ae2902ef1.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-2c3ae2902ef1.text: REPLY Q1 (partner site x wave): Tested-partner positive rates differ strongly by intake_site x collection_wave. Observed vs expected positives under the cohort ancestry x tier prior (lot_C42 Se/FP) were: site_A w1 7 vs 3.4 (25/307 tested), site_A w2 1 vs 5.3 (p=0.03), site_B w1 15 vs 8.0 (p=0.017), site_B w2 20 vs 7.8 (p=0.0002); site_B is fully tested. The cohort prior does not fit, so method changed: each site x wave gets a carrier-frequency scale k on the cohort anc x tier class frequencies, with an empirical-Bayes gamma prior (it came out diffuse). Untested rows get the scaled prior and tested rows a PPV/residual under the local prior. Partner row-mean went from 0.131 to 0.210 (0.146 if the two site_A waves are pooled).

sl-test-v2-f03ae8f6980e.label: REPLY

There is no referral, ascertainment or age field, so the only basis for excluding tier 1 was its higher positive rate.
