sl-test-v2-fd0ab2808892.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-fd0ab2808892.text: REPLY Q3 (class_01 dropout/misclassification): class_01 sensitivity is already per ancestry x lot (AFR 0.908/0.785, EUR 0.938/0.862 for A17/C42). Every missed class_01 control has VAF<=0.05 (66/520 dropouts); no control has VAF 0.05-0.3 or >0.7, and none failed only on depth. No control of one class was called as another class or as two classes, so the misclassification matrix is diagonal plus the none->class_02 false positives, and the per-class Rogan-Gladen equals the joint correction. No change.

sl-test-v2-b3c4aa34f700.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-b3c4aa34f700.text: REPLY Q1 (weights): IPW weights range 1.19-194; Kish effective sample size 283 of 1900; the ten heaviest rows (all controls) carry 13% of total weight. Dropping each of them one at a time gives B log OR -0.21 to -0.36, dropping all ten gives -0.34, dropping any of the 8 heaviest design cells gives -0.22 to -0.37, capping at the 99th percentile gives -0.27, and 200 bootstrap resamples give mean -0.28, SD 0.20, P(B<0)=0.91. Capping at the 95th/90th percentile moves the estimate to -0.07/-0.05, but that removes most of the control up-weighting and so returns toward the biased unweighted estimand. The negative sign does not rest on a handful of controls. Method unchanged: subhap_log_or -0.274 (rescaled), imprecise (95% CI includes 0).

sl-test-v2-fb4e711075c6.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-fb4e711075c6.text: REPLY Q2 (expression gene): In the interaction model, GENE1's B slope at the other genes' multimapper fraction (~0.075) is 0.34 (SE 0.08) and at its own low quartile (0.32) is 0.42, compared with GENE2's 0.308 (SE 0.012). GENE1's observed multimapper fraction ranges 0.24-0.55, so 0.075 is an extrapolation. GENE1's multimapper fraction rises with B (0.028 per copy), so its read-level signal is still partly mapping artefact. GENE2 (multimapper fraction 0.054, unrelated to B) needs no extrapolation, so it stays the supported gene. GENE1 may also carry real B dependence; this is flagged. For GENE2 the B-by-case interaction is 0.02 (p=0.43): slope 0.291 in controls and 0.311 in cases. The source-population-weighted slope is 0.284 (SE 0.020), and the case mix implies a population-average slope of 0.298. The 0.308 vs 0.286 gap is noise, not real effect modification. Method unchanged: expression_log_fc 0.308.

sl-test-v2-0c6c128b5da3.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-0c6c128b5da3.text: REPLY Q3 (ancestry heterogeneity): Ancestry-specific ridge calibration gives dosages correlated 0.975-0.995 with the pooled ones, with mean shifts under 0.012 copies. Its cross-validated R2 for B is no better (0.89-0.90 vs pooled 0.90-0.91; AFR 0.74-0.80 vs 0.80-0.81), so it is not adopted. With it, per-ancestry log ORs stay heterogeneous (EUR 0.18, AFR -0.42, EAS -1.13), and the pooled B is -0.40 vs -0.29. The 2-df Wald test for B-by-ancestry is significant everywhere: weighted B+outer chi2 7.7 (p=0.02), unweighted 10.6 (p=0.005), weighted without outer 8.6 (p=0.013), ancestry-calibrated weighted 6.8 (p=0.03). The heterogeneity therefore does not come from tagging, the weights or the outer adjustment; it looks like real effect modification, driven by EAS. Method unchanged: the task asks for one full-cohort source-population estimate, so I report the pooled, ancestry-adjusted IPW coefficient as a population average and flag the heterogeneity.

sl-test-v2-d4271ff52a19.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-d4271ff52a19.text: REPLY Q4 (total effect / outer term): Reliable panel, integer B by outer dosage (outer 0/1/2): B=0: 153/110/25; B=1: 26/103/44; B=2: 0/11/11. Mean B rises with outer (0.15/0.56/0.83), and two B copies never occur on outer 0, so B copies are carried mainly on alternate-outer haplotypes. In the joint IPW model the outer log OR is +0.26 (95% CI -0.08 to 0.60) and B is -0.29 (-0.67 to 0.09); predicted B and outer correlate 0.51 in the cohort. Outer orientation is the older, broader haplotype background and cannot be caused by B copy number, so it is not a mediator of B. It is a common cause through linkage, with its own effect opposite in sign to B. The B-only model (-0.13) mixes the outer effect into B. The total effect of B is the coefficient with outer adjusted, as the task's 'separating' instruction asks. Method unchanged.

sl-test-v2-2eed9252e60d.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-2eed9252e60d.text: Q1 (extra disease-only variants / AR(rho)): residuals from the protein-only model show only three disease-only clusters, centred on rs200028, rs200050 and rs200068, each about +-4 SNPs wide; outside them every residual |z| is <=2.2. Lag-1 decay around the peaks is about 0.45-0.55, against 0.75 in the EUR R, and a single AR(rho) is not supported across the locus. My extra modelled variants were artefacts of the LD model inside those windows, and the windows include protein leads (rs200024-26 have r2 0.1-0.31 with rs200028; rs200047-48 have r2 0.18-0.31 with rs200050), so they could absorb protein-mediated signal. Changes method: yes. I dropped the AR(rho) and pleiotropy modelling and now exclude those neighbourhoods.

sl-test-v2-53aebe4c37e0.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-53aebe4c37e0.text: Q2 (single defensible specification): EUR-R GLS IVW on the SNPs with r2<0.05 to all three disease peaks (n=47), with second-order weights, gives Q=49.0 on 45 df (p=0.32), thetaA=0.293 and thetaB=0.209 per SD. Cut-offs of r2<0.01-0.05 are stable (A 0.285-0.293, B 0.200-0.211). The earlier spread (0.29-0.41) came from the disease-LD/pleiotropy modelling choice and from SNPs next to the peaks; r2<0.1 already gives Q=99 on 57 df and A=0.335. Changes method: yes. The answer is revised from 0.34/0.23 to 0.29/0.21.

sl-test-v2-260dec5c34af.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-260dec5c34af.text: Q3 (conditional F and phase2 SE): on the final 47-SNP set the LD-aware conditional F is about 17.6 for PROTA|PROTB and about 10.2 for PROTB|PROTA (borderline weak). Second-order weights including phase2 beta SEs leave the point estimates unchanged (0.293/0.209) and raise the per-SD SEs to 0.020/0.026. The method was not changed beyond adopting the second-order weights; the weaker PROTB instruments are reported as a limitation.

sl-test-v2-28ff48eacbe3.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-28ff48eacbe3.text: Q4 (EUR consistency away from disease peaks): yes. Off-peak SNPs fit the EUR R and the two-protein model (Q=31.1 on 33 df at r2<0.01; 49.0 on 45 df at r2<0.05). The misfit is confined to the three peak neighbourhoods and is not spread across the locus. Changes method: yes. I adopted exclusion of the peak neighbourhoods with the unchanged EUR R. Final thetaA=0.29, thetaB=0.21 per SD.

sl-test-v2-567c3c3acae5.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-567c3c3acae5.text: REPLY Q1 (QC vs dosage): Using depth_log2_segment_B classified at reliable-panel cluster centres 0/0.295/0.553, QC failure does depend on segment-B dosage: 2-copy calls are 12.1% of the 297 failed samples vs 4.6% of the 483 reliable ones (logit of reliability on depth copy -0.29, p=0.015), driven by local_complexity>0.35. Failure does not depend on case status (82.8% vs 82.0%), and ancestry differs only mildly. Among the 483 reliable samples only 1 copy_index lies within 0.2 of a rounding boundary and its depth agrees, and rounding agrees with depth 100% (195 carriers either way). The ridge calibration trained on reliable samples predicts the depth calls of failed samples with slope 0.99, and a calibration trained on all 780 depth calls gives a cohort Bhat that correlates 0.996 with the original (slope 0.98) and a weighted log OR of -0.237 vs -0.267. Conclusion: genotype-dependent QC is real but only shifts the intercept; it does not change the calibration slope, the OR, or the carrier count (195, defined on reliable samples). Method unchanged.

sl-test-v2-5cbc1a8e749a.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-5cbc1a8e749a.text: REPLY Q2 (expression and case/weights): Expression-panel membership does not depend on case (p=0.59), ancestry, clinic, stream or age band (all p>0.08). GENE2 log_expr has no case effect given B (+0.03, p=0.06), and its B-by-case term is null (0.02, p=0.44); the B slope is 0.300 in controls and 0.321 in cases. The GENE2 slope is 0.321 at base, 0.319 with case, 0.302 main with B-by-case (null), and 0.295 (SE 0.022) with inverse sample_fraction weights. Because selection is ignorable and the slope is homogeneous across case status, the unweighted 0.321 (SE 0.013) is consistent and more efficient. GENE1 with a B-by-multimapper interaction has a slope of 0.33-0.35 at multimapper fraction 0.05-0.11, versus 0.44 at its own mean of 0.38. So GENE1 likely has a real B signal inflated by multimapping, and only GENE2 gives an uncontaminated estimate. Gene choice (GENE2) and the method are unchanged.

sl-test-v2-ccf8b1d83f18.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-ccf8b1d83f18.text: REPLY Q3 (ancestry): There is significant B-by-ancestry heterogeneity in the weighted model (Wald p=0.02; p=0.003 with an O-by-ancestry term too). Weighted B log OR adjusted for outer dosage is AFR -0.30 (SE 0.42, ESS 107, top-10 weight share 0.24), EAS -1.05 (0.30, ESS 50, 0.33) and EUR +0.30 (0.28, ESS 145, 0.21). Unweighted estimates show the same ordering (AFR +0.15, EAS -0.75, EUR +0.43), and so does calibration fitted within ancestry (AFR -0.41, EAS -1.13, EUR +0.18; pooled -0.36). The sign is therefore not shared by all groups, and the difference is not created by the weights or by the tagging. The pooled source-population estimate is the weighted average the task asks for. It is -0.267 (with ancestry fixed effects -0.289; weights trimmed at the 99th percentile -0.258; overall ESS 283, top-10 weight share 0.13). The pooled answer is kept, with the heterogeneity flagged.

sl-test-v2-a0b372a0c9b3.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-a0b372a0c9b3.text: REPLY Q4 (total effect vs outer): Reliable-panel B-by-O table (rows B=0/1/2, cols O=0/1/2): 153/110/25; 26/103/44; 0/11/11. P(B>0|O) is 0.15, 0.51 and 0.69. Weighted full-cohort B log OR is -0.153 (SE 0.18) without O and -0.267 (SE 0.20, CI -0.66 to 0.13) with O. The O coefficient is +0.185 (CI -0.17 to 0.54). With measured dosages in the panel the estimates are -0.19 without O and -0.39 with O. Outer orientation is the broader haplotype background on which the nested B copy arises, so it is an upstream confounder of B through LD. A copy of B cannot cause the orientation, so O is not a mediator. Conditioning on O therefore removes confounding by the outer haplotype and still gives the total effect of B; the unadjusted -0.15 mixes in the positive O association. The task also explicitly asks to separate B from O. Method unchanged.

sl-test-v2-e6d59258cc5a.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-e6d59258cc5a.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team compared, marker by marker, the RIL calls with the allele of the founder haplotype inferred from the neighbouring markers, and found that two chromosome 1 markers lying close to the peak region disagree far more often than any other marker, with the founders.tsv alleles at those two markers looking opposite to the RIL alleles for all 8 founders. Your records show no per-marker check of founder-versus-RIL agreement. Check whether that holds in your data: compute the per-marker mismatch between RIL calls and your inferred haplotypes (leaving the tested marker out), and see whether any markers near the peak stand out and whether your founder haplotype probabilities and founder effects at the peak change depending on how those markers are treated. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-b5e9dd3418af.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-b5e9dd3418af.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that the 8 founders are very unevenly represented at the chromosome 1 peak, that one of the nearly tied candidate founders is carried by about half the number of lines expected for an equal split and that its lines are unevenly spread over the two batches, and that the ranking of the tied founders depends on whether plain fixed-effect coefficients or shrunken (random-effect) estimates are used. Your records rank the founders by point estimates without per-founder line counts or standard errors. Check in your data: the expected number of lines per founder at the peak (sum of haplotype probabilities), the standard error of each founder effect, the batch split of each candidate founder's lines, and whether your ranking of the tied founders is the same under shrunken estimates. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-37f374a8244d.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-37f374a8244d.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: you recorded that the founder you reported is not the founder that comes out on top most often in your own bootstrap, and that the three candidate founders have almost identical estimated effects. The other team's bootstrap and its point estimates pointed to one and the same founder for that team. Check why your two lines of evidence disagree: is the top founder in each bootstrap resample read at a re-estimated peak or at a fixed position, how sharply does your HMM assign each line to one founder at the peak (how many lines have a maximum founder probability above one half, and can the candidate founders be told apart from the local SNP pattern), and do the raw phenotype means of lines hard-called to each candidate founder, adjusted for batch, agree with your coefficients? Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-36bb0a719996.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-36bb0a719996.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found that the chromosome 2 signal is not a localised peak: the 8-founder LOD stays elevated along the whole of chromosome 2 and its support interval spans the entire chromosome, which that team read as diffuse background rather than a single locus, and it therefore also controlled background with a mixed model using kinship computed from chromosome 2. You added the chromosome 2 peak as a single covariate and counted that model among those deciding the founder. Check whether that holds in your data: the shape of your chromosome 2 LOD curve, and whether the ranking of the tied founders at the chromosome 1 peak is the same with no chromosome 2 control, with the single covariate, and with a kinship-based control. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-9e26433b2547.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-9e26433b2547.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: you reported a position that is the midpoint between the peaks of two different analyses (with and without the outlying line), so it is not the maximum of any single LOD curve. The other team reported the maximum of one stated primary model, scanned on a regular 1 cM pseudomarker grid, and quoted a support interval around it. Check which single model you judge to be the primary one for this task and why, where its LOD curve peaks on a regular grid, and whether the choice matters relative to the width of your support interval. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-f43daa1cfad8.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-f43daa1cfad8.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team found a single line with an extreme phenotype value, far below every other line in its batch, and found that leaving that one line out moves the chromosome 1 peak position and changes the LOD by about one unit. Your records show a rank-based transform but no check of the influence of individual lines. Check whether that holds in your data: identify the most extreme phenotype value after batch adjustment, see which founder haplotype that line carries at the peak, and see whether the peak position, the LOD against your permutation threshold, and the ranking of the tied founders change when that line is left out. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-b0301ae5acfe.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-b0301ae5acfe.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team compared the nearly tied candidate founders with one-founder-versus-the-rest contrast models at the peak and with scans run separately within each batch. You recorded that the lines carrying your top founder are few and unevenly spread over the two batches, but no within-batch or one-founder-versus-rest comparison. Check in your data whether the ranking of the tied founders is the same within each batch taken separately, and whether a one-founder-versus-rest contrast at the peak ranks the candidate founders in the same order as your 8-founder coefficients. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-2d7a8e4ebe80.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-2d7a8e4ebe80.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team treated the chromosome 2 peak as a covariate in the models from which it read the founder effects, and found that its chromosome 1 LOD changes by about one unit when that covariate is added. You recorded that your top founder changes when the chromosome 2 covariate is combined with shrinkage, yet you kept the chromosome 2 covariate as a sensitivity check only. Check what in the data decides whether chromosome 2 control belongs in the primary model (for example how much residual variance it removes, and whether chromosome 2 haplotypes are correlated with the candidate founders' haplotypes at the chromosome 1 peak), and state which founder ranking you obtain under the model you judge to be best supported, and why the rule you were given for reporting a founder under shrunken estimates is or is not met. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-9dce3a232627.reason: question from the director after the teams' answers differed
sl-test-v2-9dce3a232627.text: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: the other team kept every marker in its haplotype reconstruction and varied the amount of recombination assumed by the HMM (map expansion), while you removed two chromosome 1 markers next to the peak and varied only the genotyping error rate. Check whether the two markers you removed could instead be kept with their founder alleles recoded, and whether the ranking of the tied founders and the peak position are the same under the three treatments (kept as given, removed, recoded) and under different assumed amounts of recombination in your transition model. Does it change your method?

sl-test-v2-abc069d5052b.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-abc069d5052b.text: REPLY Q1 (chain start, prior, N): asym-error WF HMM for locus A gives s_A=0.095 [0.040,0.165] with chain at gen0 + flat prior; 0.100 [0.045,0.170] starting at gen6; 0.105 [0.045,0.175] with free starting frequency (gen0 or gen6); 0.095 [0.050,0.145] with drift variance p(1-p)/2N; 0.100 [0.025,0.185] with N halved. All shifts are at most 0.01, under 10% of the CI width; only the interval width responds to N. Method unchanged; haploid p(1-p)/N kept.

sl-test-v2-fefa4146a204.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-fefa4146a204.text: REPLY Q2 (C->T/T->C split profile, sum 0.32, s and free p0 re-optimised per locus): joint logL rises monotonically with C->T, from -66.7 at C->T=0 to -56.4 at C->T=0.32 (boundary, T->C=0). The 1.92-unit supported range is C->T of about 0.25-0.32. Across it s_A goes from about 0.083 to 0.110 (free p0), or 0.078-0.100 with a flat prior; at C->T=0.31 s_A=0.10. s_B stays at 0.025 throughout. The point estimate (0.095) stands, but the honest interval is the union over the supported split, about 0.035-0.18. Locus choice A holds at every split value.

sl-test-v2-a902a545d879.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-a902a545d879.text: REPLY Q3 (piecewise s inside drift HMM): with drift and the Ne schedule modelled, the deceleration at locus A disappears under the asym model (break 26: s1=0.124, s2=0.067, LRT 0.57; breaks 18/37: LRT 0.02/0.31). It is larger under the symmetric models, which do NOT put the late samples on the floor: sym0.16 break26 LRT 3.16 (s 0.165 then 0.031), sym0.01 LRT 2.02; none is significant after choosing among 3 breakpoints. Locus B has LRT<0.12 everywhere. Parametric bootstrap GOF (300 WF+binomial sims from the fitted constant-s model, statistic = logL at fitted params): asym A P=0.58, sym16 A P=0.14, sym01 A P=0.50, asym B P=0.83. Constant s is adequate; the earlier deterministic LRT 5.3 came from ignoring drift.

sl-test-v2-0eb464a95d79.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-0eb464a95d79.text: REPLY Q4 (error models refit with identical HMM, flat / free p0): logL A asym -30.02/-27.93, sym16 -34.13/-31.81, sym01 -33.38/-31.33. B asym -30.33/-28.79, sym16 -30.55/-28.72, sym01 -31.69/-29.94. Joint asym -60.35/-56.73, sym16 -64.68/-60.53, sym01 -65.06/-61.27. A without gen6: asym -27.62/-25.88, sym16 -29.83/-27.95, sym01 -30.32/-28.66. So the asym preference survives dropping gen6 but shrinks to about 2 log-units, and locus B cannot tell the models apart. The evidence is moderate, not decisive. Method kept (it is also the only model consistent with both the 0.16 column average and the ~1% instrument rate), but the uncertainty on s_A is widened; the alternative models give s_A 0.045-0.065.

sl-test-v2-b21938f413db.label: REFEREE TEST
sl-test-v2-b21938f413db.text: REFEREE gb06: X (beta -0.34) fixes ambient scale k=1 at the HBB-derived rho; Y (beta -0.54) fits k~1.27. Test: within genotype g=1 (4 high-rho vs 4 low-rho donors), find k that equalizes ambient-corrected rates between rho groups using genes NOT used by Y for k: resting IFI6 k_eq=1.14 (boot 0.86-1.56), resting ISG15 k_eq=1.15 (boot 1.08-1.22), plus resting CXCL10 1.26 (1.06-1.49) and activated CXCL10 1.64. At k=1 resting ISG rates are ~2x higher in high-rho donors, so HBB-based rho under-removes ambient; k=1 is rejected, supporting Y.

sl-test-v2-3d8cbc2f3117.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-3d8cbc2f3117.text: REPLY Q1 (removed SNPs): the r2>=0.05 rule removes 33 SNPs (rs200023-033, rs200045-055, rs200063-073), including the strongest PROTA lead rs200024 (phase1 z 58.5) and the PROTB lead rs200047 (z 49.4). The 47 kept SNPs still contain independent signals: PROTA rs200020 (phase2 z 26.3, but only about 9 expected from the rs200024 tail under the AR(0.749) reference) and PROTB rs200060 (phase2 z 16.6, about 0.6 expected from the rs200047 tail), plus rs200056-062. The kept set therefore identifies both effects (conditional F 14.2/9.4). Method unchanged.

sl-test-v2-29c1ce6447cd.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-29c1ce6447cd.text: REPLY Q2 (LD fit by trait): the reference is exactly AR(1) with r=0.749 between adjacent SNPs. Phase-2 protein z-scores fit it (leave-one-out residual is lowest at rho 0.70-0.75). Disease z-scores taken over all 80 SNPs fit rho of about 0.5 better (rs200068 neighbour ratios at lags 1/2/3 are 0.49/0.22/0.03, against 0.75/0.56/0.42 from the reference). On the 47 SNPs away from the disease-only peaks, however, the disease data fit the reference: a joint model with disease LD AR(0.749) gives Q=49 on 45 df, while AR(0.5/0.54/0.6) gives Q=109/94/74. The mismatch is confined to the disease-only peaks; the protein-mediated disease signal follows the reference. Method unchanged.

sl-test-v2-54c709a9ea67.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-54c709a9ea67.text: REPLY Q3 (stepwise and Q): I refit with a joint-effect model (protein joint effects = R^-1 times marginal; disease LD AR(rho_y) estimated by likelihood; direct-effect columns added stepwise). It needs 13 direct effects, many with alternating signs next to the peaks, before Q is acceptable, and the estimates drift from (0.43, 0.30) to (0.32, 0.27) per SD. That is unstable and absorbs protein signal, which confirms that the peak regions cannot be modelled well. Q close to df on the retained SNPs is not an artefact of removing information: the same rows reject faster-decaying disease LD (Q 74-109) and still contain strong independent protein signals. Answer kept at 0.293/0.209; the plausible range is 0.29-0.43 for PROTA and 0.21-0.30 for PROTB if the peak regions were modelled.

sl-test-v2-96bf951f2808.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-96bf951f2808.text: REPLY to director Q3 (marker mismatch): leave-one-out HMM check confirms chr1 markers m1_056 (51.4cM) and m1_058 (53.2cM) mismatch the inferred founder haplotype at 0.91 vs median 0.054; founders.tsv alleles are inverted there (RIL freq 0.18/0.24 vs founder freq 0.75). Flipping them drops mismatch to 0.05 and changes the chr1 top founder from F4 to F5 (centered effect F5 +2.01 vs F4 +0.99); dropping them gives the same F5 result. Changes method: yes.

sl-test-v2-4cfeb83c07ff.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-4cfeb83c07ff.text: REPLY to director Q2 (position): primary model = batch covariate only, corrected founder alleles, 1cM grid; chr1 peak 46.0cM LOD 5.13, 1.5-LOD interval 41-61cM. Alternatives (chr2 covariate 45, kinship 45, outlier dropped 44, drop bad markers 45.7) all lie well inside the interval; I now report the single-model maximum 46.0 instead of a midpoint.

sl-test-v2-d15cdf2dd7ea.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-d15cdf2dd7ea.text: REPLY to director Q1 (bootstrap vs point estimate): earlier bootstrap read the top founder at a re-estimated peak; resampled peaks wander widely (IQR 35-59cM), where F2 often leads. At the fixed 46cM peak, F5 is top in 168/200 bootstraps. 115/120 lines have max founder prob >0.5 (94 >0.9). Batch-adjusted hard-call means agree with the coefficients: F5 3.72, F4 3.16, F2 2.95. Only 2 of 15 markers in 40-54cM separate F5 from both F2 and F4. The earlier disagreement came mainly from the two inverted markers. Changes method: yes, via the marker fix.

sl-test-v2-1fe79a0b5b5c.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-1fe79a0b5b5c.text: REPLY to director Q4 (founder counts/SE/shrinkage): expected lines at chr1 46cM peak: F1 22.4, F2 12.5, F3 19.1, F4 14.3, F5 7.3, F6 16.7, F7 12.7, F8 15.0. F5 is rare (hard-called n=7, batch0 4 / batch1 3). SEs: F5 0.76, F4 0.56, F2 0.63. Shrunken BLUP keeps the ranking F5 1.29 > F4 0.83 > F2 0.65. Ranking does not depend on shrinkage after the marker fix; no further method change.

sl-test-v2-af37dff6bf03.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-af37dff6bf03.text: REPLY to director Q5 (chr2): chr2 8-founder LOD is diffuse (2.1-5.3 along the whole chromosome), not a localised peak. The chr1 result is the same with no chr2 control (46cM, F5), with the chr2 peak covariate (45cM, F5) and with a chr2-kinship mixed model (h2 0.45; 45cM, F5). Primary model now uses no chr2 control; chr2 used only for sensitivity. Changes the founder decision: no.

sl-test-v2-7d1ab0f90dd4.label: gb10 revised answer
sl-test-v2-7d1ab0f90dd4.text: gb10 chr1 QTL revised (team-b): after correcting the inverted founder alleles at m1_056/m1_058, the chr1 QTL peaks at 46.0cM (LOD 5.13, 1.5-LOD 41-61cM) and the high founder is F5, top in every model checked.

sl-test-v2-4fa763f947a1.label: REFEREE TEST
sl-test-v2-4fa763f947a1.text: Referee test gb07: with calls T01 VAF>=0.2, T02 log2<-0.3 & segdup<0.6, T03/T04 het unless trans phase sets, and the lot_A17 per-ancestry control confusion matrix, the exact joint EM/linear inversion on screening call counts gives CF AFR 0.1028, EUR 0.0783, AFR negative residual 0.0369; per-class Rogan-Gladen (FP from none controls) reproduces 0.0986/0.0767/0.0345 exactly; a team's reported EM values 0.0926/0.0703 could not be reproduced and lie on the opposite side of the MLE. All are within the profile-likelihood 95% CI (AFR 0.05-0.17). Partner full-roster CF from unshrunk site x wave x tier strata on lot_C42 is 0.233 (site x wave 0.277, site x tier 0.128), so it depends strongly on the model.

sl-test-v2-7e3e22dc8e9b.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-7e3e22dc8e9b.text: REPLY Q1 (within-batch / one-vs-rest, gb10 chr1 @45 cM): batch0 (n=52) fixed effects F4 3.98 ~ F5 3.88; batch1 (n=68, only 2.9 expected F5 lines) F5 6.39 > F2 6.02 > F4 5.11. One-founder-vs-rest with batch: F5 +2.17 (t 2.61) vs F4 +1.49 (t 2.60), the same LOD 1.47; adding the chr2 covariate gives F4 t 2.42 / LOD 1.35 vs F5 t 2.03 / LOD 0.96. So F5's lead depends on a handful of batch1 lines, and F4 and F5 are tied. This feeds into the revision.

sl-test-v2-96d28a41d28d.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-96d28a41d28d.text: REPLY Q2 (outlier, gb10): the most extreme low line is RIL076 (batch0, y -3.59, 1.2 SD below the next line in its batch); at 45 cM its haplotype is F7 0.65 / F4 0.32. Dropping it moves the chr1 peak to 43.3 cM and raises the LOD to 5.67 (batch only; above the 5.23 permutation threshold) or 6.43 (batch+chr2). Under batch+chr2 F4 then leads in both the fixed effects and the BLUP (2.57 vs 2.00; BLUP 1.15 vs 0.61). The highest line, RIL049 (z +3.1), has little influence. I kept RIL076 because there is no evidence it is an error, but it is influential and works against F4.

sl-test-v2-68217714d22e.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-68217714d22e.text: REPLY Q3 (chr2 control, gb10): with chr1@45 and batch in the model, the chr2 peak (57.8 cM) removes 19.5% of residual variance (partial F 3.6 on 7 df, p=0.0016). Its haplotypes are almost uncorrelated with the chr1 founder haplotypes (|r| up to 0.19 for F2/F4/F5). So it improves precision without confounding, and it belongs in the primary model. Under batch+chr2: peak 45 cM, LOD 5.46; fixed effects F5 2.38 > F4 2.19 > F2 2.06 (SE about 0.7-0.9); REML BLUP F4 0.85 > F5 0.78 > F2 0.68; bootstrap top BLUP F4 40% / F5 32% / F2 27%. F5 fails the 'stays on top under shrinkage' rule. Revised high_founder to F4, reported as a near tie with F5 and F2.

sl-test-v2-bab103cc99fe.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-bab103cc99fe.text: REPLY Q4 (markers / map expansion, gb10): m1_056 and m1_058 are exactly complement-flipped (RIL allele-1 frequency 0.18/0.24 vs founder 0.75), so recoding them is valid. Recoded and removed give the same results: peak 45-46 cM, F5 > F4 in the batch-only BLUP, F4 > F5 in the batch+chr2 BLUP, at every map expansion from 1x to 3x. Keeping them as given distorts the result (peak 43-45, F2 or F4 on top). Map expansion barely matters. Method kept: recode or remove.

sl-test-v2-be2c191d7767.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-be2c191d7767.text: REPLY (Q1, removed guides): The 5 removed targeting guides g003,g008,g015 (LINC473) and g040,g050 (KIN1) carry strong measured KIN1 knockdown (kK=0.78,0.59,0.77,0.75,0.77) yet near-zero growth (lfc -0.04..-0.10); they contradict the KIN1 model, so the removal rule was model-dependent (not independent). But keeping ALL guides under a robust Huber fit gives KIN1 coefficient -0.81 (OLS all -0.75, clean -0.83). Direction and magnitude unchanged; neighbor effect stays far below -0.25. Does not change the decision.

sl-test-v2-b210b2dfa200.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-b210b2dfa200.text: REPLY (Q2, GC term): After outlier removal the GC covariate rests on only 21 control guides; clean-control GC slope is -0.28 (se 0.065, p=0.0004, nonzero) but the all-control slope is -0.70 driven by outliers. GC is confounded with the low-GC distal LINC473 guides, and adding GC to the screen local model pulls KIN1 from -0.83 to -0.65. The arbiter is the independent follow-up data: KIN1 coefficient is -0.77 with GC and -0.77 without. GC is poorly constrained and does not change that KIN1 is strongly negative. De-emphasize GC; decision unchanged.

sl-test-v2-cb2c8c93db73.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-cb2c8c93db73.text: REPLY (Q3, plate transfer): The follow-up and CasRx plates share only labels (plate_A/B/C); there is no evidence they are the same physical batch, and the follow-up plates contain CRISPRi guides, a different assay from CasRx. So transferring follow-up plate offsets onto CasRx is unjustified (a genuine weak point). However the follow-up's real value is as an independent growth-vs-knockdown check: regressing follow-up growth on (1-expr) gives KIN1 -0.77, LINC473 +0.04 (null), and growth~screen-lfc has slope 0.97, intercept ~0, R2=0.99. This independently confirms the screen. In the follow-up, plate is NOT confounded with gene (each plate balances LINC473/KIN1/ANKRD42/NTC), unlike the CasRx plates which are fully confounded with overlap class.

sl-test-v2-197606eeedda.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-197606eeedda.text: REPLY (Q4/Q5, CasRx intercept and high-overlap-only): Fitting only high-overlap guides (overlap>=0.5) with the off-isoform term gives the SAME dominant-isoform coefficient -0.051 (intercept -0.038, off-isoform -0.31); the low-overlap guides do not pull it. Model-free: at matched knockdown efficiency, lower-overlap guides show stronger growth defects (e.g. overlap 0.96/kd0.62 -> -0.111 vs overlap 0.72/kd0.62 -> -0.147; overlap 0.08/kd0.52 -> -0.158), proving the dominant LINC473 isoform is NOT the driver and the effect is off-isoform/collateral. The nonspecific intercept and plate are not cleanly separable (plate fully confounded with overlap), so the intercept is uncertain; but dominant-specific effect is small (-0.05) either way (-0.05 slope-only to -0.11 through-origin). Decision unchanged.

sl-test-v2-928b91e655aa.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-928b91e655aa.text: REPLY (Q6, errors-in-variables): CasRx knockdown spans 0.21-0.71 (std 0.148) and KIN1-guide expr_rel spans 0.00-0.14 (knockdown 0.86-1.00); housekeeping expr noise is ~4% std. Measurement error would ATTENUATE slopes toward zero, so the true neighbor KIN1 effect is if anything MORE negative than -0.77, and the dominant-isoform effect (-0.05) would not be pushed past -0.08 meaningfully. Signal range >> noise. Does not change the decision.

sl-test-v2-86c64eec7ad7.label: REPLY
sl-test-v2-86c64eec7ad7.text: REPLY (overall decision): advance_target=0 is robust to every director question. neighbor_mediated_lfc is strongly negative (-0.75..-0.83 in screen, -0.77 in independent follow-up), far below the -0.25 cutoff, so advance=0 holds regardless of the CasRx dominant-isoform value (-0.05..-0.11). Final: advance_target=0, lncrna_specific_lfc=-0.05, neighbor_mediated_lfc=-0.77 (refined using the independent follow-up confirmation).

sl-test-v2-3b9604b8134a.label: REPLY GC confound
sl-test-v2-3b9604b8134a.text: REPLY (GC confound): Confirmed - among control guides with no locus knockdown, screen LFC depends on guide_gc_frac (slope -0.28, r=-0.70), and GC is confounded with KIN1 knockdown across locus guides (r=0.82) because high-GC guides sit near the KIN1 TSS. I added GC as a covariate in the joint CRISPRi regression; bKIN moves from -0.755 (no GC) to -0.732. Method changed: GC must be controlled. The lncRNA coefficient stays ~0.

sl-test-v2-7df6d6b8782e.label: REPLY nonresponders
sl-test-v2-7df6d6b8782e.text: REPLY (non-responders): Confirmed guides with strong measured knockdown but control-like growth: g003/g008/g015 (LINC473) and g040/g050 (KIN1), consistent across reps. Individual leverage is small (bKIN -0.745..-0.791 when dropped one at a time). A robust Huber fit downweights them. Does not change the KIN1 conclusion.

sl-test-v2-8c7a51df9d24.label: REPLY CasRx collateral
sl-test-v2-8c7a51df9d24.text: REPLY (CasRx collateral in kept guides): Confirmed - efficiency-driven growth (collateral) seen in low-overlap guides is also present in retained high-overlap guides and inflates a naive growth~efficiency slope. Decomposing growth=int+bdom*(eff*overlap)+bnon*(eff*(1-overlap)) separates dominant-transcript loss bdom=-0.158 from collateral bnon=-0.285; dominant-transcript effect at 100% knockdown = -0.173. lncrna_specific_lfc revised -0.18 -> -0.17 (same magnitude, decision unchanged).

sl-test-v2-40c39ca423c1.label: REPLY control center
sl-test-v2-40c39ca423c1.text: REPLY (control outliers / center): Confirmed NTC g067/g068/g069 (-0.53..-0.72) and ANKRD42 g055/g061 are consistent outliers that contaminate the NTC mean center (-0.138). Robust median center is -0.020. Regression coefficients are centering-invariant so estimates hold, but the correct matched-control center is the robust median.

sl-test-v2-46fa7c939a39.label: REPLY scale plate
sl-test-v2-46fa7c939a39.text: REPLY (scale / plate): follow-up vs screen slope 0.969, r=0.997, offsets -0.001..-0.061: follow-up is ~1:1 on the screen scale, supporting CasRx magnitudes as screen-scale. CasRx plate is confounded with overlap class; the per-plate naive extrapolation differs (plate-A -0.275 collateral-contaminated, plate-B flat), handled by the overlap decomposition rather than per-plate slope.

sl-test-v2-69a8d5e6042b.label: RESULT revised
sl-test-v2-69a8d5e6042b.text: RESULT (revised): advance_target=0, lncrna_specific_lfc=-0.17 (CasRx dominant-transcript decomposition), neighbor_mediated_lfc=-0.73 (GC-adjusted robust joint CRISPRi bKIN; was -0.65, revised more negative after removing GC off-target confound). Conclusion unchanged: lncRNA criterion met (-0.17<=-0.08) but KIN1 not >-0.25, so LINC473 not a clean transcript-directed target.

sl-test-v2-8ed194ff17f6.label: REFEREE TEST
sl-test-v2-8ed194ff17f6.text: gb10 chr1 QTL referee: at 45-46 cM (flipped m1_056/m1_058, 8-state HMM) the F5-minus-F4 founder contrast is positive in every fit, +0.8 to +1.0 with batch only (bootstrap P(F5>F4) about 0.9) and +0.3 to +0.5 with the chr2 covariate (P about 0.7). Hard-called F5 carriers have a batch-adjusted mean of +2.13 vs +1.18 for F4. F4 wins only under BLUP shrinkage, so F5 is the supported high founder, though it is not significant.

sl-test-v2-81cd5ea35761.label: REFEREE TEST
sl-test-v2-81cd5ea35761.text: gb08 CasRx: fitting growth = plate + b_dom*kd*overlap + b_non*kd*(1-overlap) within each plate separately gives b_dom -0.048/-0.043/-0.050 (plates A/B/C) and b_non ~-0.30; internal CasRx plate offsets (A-C -0.060, B-C -0.027) exactly match guide_followup plate offsets vs screen, so plates are real batch effects and a pooled no-plate fit (b_dom -0.158) is inflated by plate A's offset; lncrna_specific_lfc ~ -0.05, advance_target 0.
